title: Bounce-back year or end of an era? Where Chiefs' dynasty stands entering 2026 NFL season
summary: Coming off a six-win season, Kansas City has more to prove now than ever before in the Patrick Mahomes era
full_text:
The NFL became accustomed over the last decade to seeing the Kansas City Chiefs stand atop the AFC West and compete perennially for the Vince Lombardi Trophy, if not win it altogether. It was a shock to the collective football system to see the greatest dynasty since the Tom Brady-era New England Patriots not only miss the postseason in 2025 but also finish the year five games below .500.
Kansas City's 6-11 record last year was its worst since 2012. It fell short of the playoffs for the first time since 2014, which was also the most recent campaign in which the franchise finished with single-digit wins.
Even the greatest dynasties in football history experienced a down year here and there. The question facing the Chiefs heading into 2026 is whether last year was a blip on the radar or a sign that their reign atop the NFL is on its last legs. With a projected win total of 10.5, the betting market suggests the Chiefs will bounce back to an extent this season. But did they truly do enough this offseason to ensure that they are on the precipice of a rebound campaign?
In identifying the Chiefs' greatest deficiencies from a year ago and considering their offseason moves, we can determine in the aggregate whether Andy Reid can get his team back into the Super Bowl hunt or if this is the end of an era in Kansas City.
A spot in the postseason was very much in play for the Chiefs into late November 2025. Their 6-5 start to the season reduced the margin for error, though, and the string of catastrophic injuries that poured in over the final six weeks played a major role in keeping them out of the playoff bracket.
Here are the most significant season-ending injuries that unfolded in the back half of the campaign:
The Mahomes injury was the nail in the coffin, but the health issues reared their heads even before he went down. Kansas City closed the regular season on a six-game losing streak which coincided with that string of ailments.
The 2025 roster's shortcomings were clear even before the injuries struck, though. Perhaps most glaring was an ineffective rushing attack that behind Kareem Hunt , Isiah Pacheco and Brashard Smith ranked only 25th in the NFL in yards per game. Defensively, the pass rush lacked star talent outside of defensive tackle Chris Jones and posted just the 22nd-most sacks of any team. The lack of push up front also undoubtedly played a role in the Chiefs ranking seventh-worst in takeaways.
Counting stats showed a lack of production across the board, while less measurable factors like the clutch element were real X factors. For years, Mahomes and tight end Travis Kelce were the faces of an offense that could never be counted out of games, no matter how large the deficit. In 2025, they rarely delivered the timely plays that in years prior fueled unimaginable comebacks. If Kansas City found itself trailing in the second half, the game was all but over.
An exodus of key contributors followed the disappointing conclusion to 2025. These departures left the Chiefs with major roles to fill:
The receiving corps also faced a hiccup when Rice underwent cleanup surgery on his knee and was forced to complete much of his rehab in a jail cell after he violated his probation. And the offense as a whole remains without its coordinator, as Eric Bieniemy is at home with his wife, who is recovering from gunshot wounds suffered in an incident involving the couple's son.
Not all of the injuries and departures created net-negatives. Mahomes, Rice and Simmons, for instance, are all on track to play in Week 1 and thus should keep the passing attack humming. Mahomes' recovery is especially impressive considering he is just under eight months removed from tearing a ligament in his knee.
The run game projects to be the most improved operation on the team after the Chiefs completed the splashy signing of Kenneth Walker III . The reigning Super Bowl MVP inked the largest deal by a free agent running back in NFL history and brings a pair of 1,000-yard seasons with him to Kansas City.
Defensive reinforcements arrived in free agency and through the draft, the most impactful of which came in the secondary and on the edge. Cornerbacks L'Jarius Sneed and Kader Kohou signed free agent deals, as did safety Alohi Gilman . Kansas City then used the No. 6 overall pick on ready-made starting cornerback Mansoor Delane and selected edge rusher R Mason Thomas in the second round.
The Chiefs made enough moves to keep their floor high. It is difficult to envision the personnel on this roster allowing even more regression. But at the same time, they arguably did not improve at any spot other than the running back position, and their offensive coordinator change is effectively on hold until Bieniemy returns to the team.
What Walker adds to the offense is undeniably impactful. Taking pressure off Mahomes as he works his way back from a serious knee injury is invaluable, not to mention the enhanced weaponry the quarterback has at his disposal. The offense will be more balanced than in the last handful of years, which might help the Chiefs rekindle some of their clutch magic in addition to the obvious leaps in down-to-down production that can be expected.
Defensively, however, the secondary and edge-rushing units saw neutral changes, at best. The cornerback departures are especially concerning and were indicative of a continuing trend wherein Kansas City watches young talent depart rather than paying up to keep it.
In total, the Chiefs' personnel is about on par with last year's squad. The hope is that Walker's arrival will mask any further decline on defense and allow an aging passing offense to remain as formidable as any, and that feels like a fair bet.
So much of Kansas City's mystique over the last decade has been the ability for Mahomes to pull rabbits out of his hat and for the Chiefs to overpower defenses with a relentless aerial assault. With Mahomes coming off a knee injury, Kelce declining with age and the wide receiver group still searching for a reliable No. 1 weapon to grab onto the top role and run with it, this team's identity is as tenuous as ever.
Even then, a little bit of positive regression with regard to close-game luck will go a long way, and so long as the injury bug does not bite as hard as it did in the second half of last year, the Chiefs should be expected to win at least a couple of more games than they did in their anomalous letdown season.
A bounce-back year ought to be on deck in the sense that the Chiefs will win more than six games, but this is not the same monster that dominated the league for much of the last 10 years. As the core continues to age, Mahomes' massive contract reduces spending flexibility and deficiencies emerge at key spots, it seems more and more like the best days in Kansas City have come and gone.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Top 10 offensive and defensive play-callers entering 2026: Sean McVay, Mike Macdonald lead way
summary: CBS Sports' NFL experts ranked the league's best play-callers entering the 2026 season, with Sean McVay earning the top spot on offense
full_text:
As the season rapidly approaches, CBS Sports' NFL experts ranked the top 10 offensive play-callers and top 10 defensive play-callers entering the 2026 season.
Like the top 10 head coaches list, which came out Monday , these lists produced a wide variety of answers. In fact, 19 different defensive play-callers received at least one vote, by far the largest number of any single vote in this series, which included all offensive positions and all defensive positions as well. Note that many head coaches are also a play-caller for one side of the ball, too, so they may feature on both the head coach and play-caller lists.
Each voter ranked their top 10 head coaches, and each spot was assigned a point value: 10 points for a first-place vote, nine for a second-place vote and so on, down to one point for a 10th-place vote.
Panel: Zach Pereles, Jared Dubin, Tyler Sullivan, Jordan Dajani, Bryan DeArdo, Josh Edwards, Garrett Podell, R.J. White, Carter Bahns, Mike Renner, J.P. Acosta, Leger Douzable
Just like at head coach, McVay leads the way at offensive play-caller. His synergy with Matthew Stafford hit a new high in 2025, when the Rams finished first in yards per game, yards per play, first downs per game, points per game and success rate. McVay's cutting edge was once again on display, with the Rams leaning heavily into three-tight end sets. Los Angeles' 30.5% rate of 13 personnel was by far the highest in the league, with the Steelers second at 13.5%.
Shanahan's ability to scheme pass catchers open is second to none, and it has benefitted quarterbacks for over a decade now. The son of two-time Super Bowl champion Mike Shanahan, Kyle led successful offenses in Houston, Washington and Atlanta before earning the top coaching gig in San Francisco. In Washington, he helped engineer Robert Griffin III's rookie breakout; in Atlanta, he turned Matt Ryan into an MVP; and in San Francisco, both Jimmy Garoppolo and Brock Purdy have thrived.
Johnson's one-year leap to star head coach has been impressive, but there's been little doubting his offensive magic for a few years now, after he lifted the Lions ' offense into a premier unit. Johnson does excellent with quarterbacks, yes, but his true best attribute might be with his offensive line schemes, whether in run blocking or pass blocking. The Bears fifth in PFF's pass-blocking grades and fifth in PFF's run-blocking grades last year.
Reid and Patrick Mahomes were hitting unprecedented heights in their first few years together before a recent fall off. That dip coincided with Matt Nagy's return to Kansas City, and the Chiefs decided to move on from Nagy and back to Eric Bieniemy -- the offensive coordinator from the more successful 2018-22 run -- in an attempt to get back on course.
The lone non-head coach to make this top 10, McDaniel has the creativity to unlock the Chargers ' considerable offensive talents this year. Though he gained more notoriety in Miami for helping turn Tua Tagovailoa around (at least for a few years), McDaniel is a truly terrific run-game schemer. Last year, the Dolphins finished fourth in yards per carry and second in explosive run rate.
Kubiak had a solid debut as an offensive coordinator in 2021 with the Vikings , but Minnesota fired Mike Zimmer at the end of the season. In 2024, Kubiak got his second chance, this time with the Saints , but New Orleans ended up going through three different starting quarterbacks and moving on to a new regime, too. The third time was the charm, though. Kubiak's heavy play-action attack helped Sam Darnold thrive and turned Jaxon Smith-Njigba into a superstar. Kubiak has his work cut out for him in Las Vegas.
Coen's first NFL job came as an assistant wide receivers coach for the Rams in 2018, but he moved up the ranks quickly, and a strong 2024 as Buccaneers offensive coordinator helped him land the top job in Jacksonville last year. It took a bit, but Trevor Lawrence eventually caught fire as the Jaguars finished 13-4, their most wins in a season in the 21st century.
This season figures to be a crucial one for O'Connell, who has alternated excellent seasons with middling ones. He went 13-4 in his debut year with Kirk Cousins , then 7-10 when Cousins tore his Achilles, then 14-3 with Sam Darnold, then 9-8 last year while cycling through J.J. McCarthy , Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer . Kyler Murray could hold the key to getting things back on track in Minnesota, and it's a big bet for O'Connell, who will also hope to improve his team's running game.
LaFleur's offenses have finished in the top dozen in yards four of the last six seasons, but it's ability to adjust on the fly that earns him some props, too: He helped Malik Willis play at en extremely high level several times in the past few seasons when Jordan Love got hurt. Love's ascension has been impressive, too.
Many laughed when the Colts brought in Daniel Jones to compete with Anthony Richardson last year, but those pundits quickly quieted when Jones had the Colts' offense rolling before injuries came into play. Steichen's play action-heavy scheme and ability to work in three-wide receiver sets
Macdonald is the unanimous No. 1 after leading the Seahawks to a Super Bowl win. His ability to incorporate different, creative, matchup-specific schemes every week is a testament to how good of a game planner and teacher he is. In the Super Bowl, for example, he used Devon Witherspoon as a pass rusher six times, one of which resulted in a sack, another of which resulted in an interception. Prior to that game, Witherspoon hadn't rushed the passer since Week 16.
Even amid a down year in Kansas City, Spagnuolo's unit ranked 10th in total defense and sixth in scoring defense. Spagnuolo has an innate ability to dial up the right call in crucial moments, often sending a well-timed, unique pressure package on a big third or fourth down. Now 66, he's still getting it done.
From the University of Michigan to the Los Angeles Chargers, Minter excelled as a defensive coordinator under Jim Harbaugh. Now, he's a head coach for the first time, succeeding Jim's brother John in Baltimore. Minter's defenses have a knack for being disciplined, and he has gotten terrific play out of his secondaries especially.
Fangio, who has been a defensive coordinator for eight different teams, has been successful just about everywhere. The Eagles ranked first in total defense and second in scoring defense in 2024, his first year in Philadelphia, and were fifth in scoring defense last year. Fangio's two-high safety look has become the favored way to prevent big plays across the NFL.
After Macdonald, defensive play-callers No. 2-5 were separated by a mere nine points, so if we're tiering them, Flores really belongs in Tier 2, even if he finished No. 5 overall. In fact, Flores received two second-place votes and three third-place votes. Flores' uber-aggressive scheme -- the Vikings led the NFL in pressure rate last year -- is rattles many a quarterback from the get-go.
Saleh is back in the top gig after a second stint as 49ers defensive coordinator. Things fell apart in his first head-coaching job, with the Jets , but perhaps he is better prepared to succeed this time in Tennessee. Saleh's ability to get passable defense in San Francisco in 2025 despite multiple injuries was an impressive display of perseverance, ingenuity and adjusting on the fly.
Shula was on all but one ballot, and he is equipped with the most pass-rushing (see: Myles Garrett ) and cornerback (see: Trent McDuffie , Jaylen Watson ) talent he has ever had. The Rams have turned many mid- or late-round draft picks and journeymen into standouts -- or at least starters -- under Shula, whose creativity in using and replacing blitzers stands out.
Joseph's Broncos defense led the NFL with 68 sacks last year, 11 more than any other team and four short of tying the 1984 Bears for most in a season. Joseph's ability to put his pass rushers in positions to succeed is a big reason why. Having…

summary: Plus, Cameron Young surges in our latest Power 18 Rankings
full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
MLB teams are done trading for the year ( well, unless they use this exception ) now that the deadline has come and gone. A bevy of blockbusters flew in over the weekend as clubs positioned themselves for the stretch run, and some were more successful than others at accomplishing their buying or selling goals. We determined which front offices made the best moves with our trade deadline report card .
There are, of course, the obvious ones. The Dodgers acquiring Tarik Skubal made them the biggest winners of all, and the Red Sox bolstered their red-hot lineup with Adley Rutschman in a move that could keep them in control of their own postseason destiny. But what about the teams that made sneaky good trades ?
Our Matt Snyder loves what the Padres did in acquiring Casey Mize , which is the main reason why they received an "A" for their deadline moves.
Some clubs left us (and their fans) wanting a whole lot more, though. These are among the teams who graded out the poorest:
The top spot in the Power 18 Rankings has been untouchable all year with Scottie Scheffler retaining his status as the World No. 1. title: George Pickens' 2026 season likely to be his Cowboys swan song after Zay Flowers, Drake London contracts
summary: Pickens' market continues to rise while Dallas stares down looming contract decision with him and All-Pro DT Quinnen Williams
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys and their fan base need to treasure Pro Bowl wide receiver George Pickens while they still can because the 2026 season will likely be his last in Dallas.
While that is an incredibly gloomy thought early on in training camp, the time on the NFL calendar when hope springs eternal for all of the league's 32 teams, it's a realistic conclusion given the continual uptick in the wide receiver contracts market and what Dallas will likely choose to prioritize.
The Baltimore Ravens inked two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers to a reported four-year, $140 million extension on Tuesday prior to the start of his fourth NFL season. That deal is identical to Minnesota Vikings 2022 NFL Offensive Player of the Year wide receiver Justin Jefferson's in both years and total contract value, with Jefferson earning $2 million more than Flowers in guaranteed money, $110 million to $108 million. In June, the Atlanta Falcons re-signed wide receiver Drake London , Pickens' 2022 NFL Draft classmate, to a four-year, $141.054 million extension with $99.87 million guaranteed, making him the third-highest-paid receiver in the league.
Pickens, meanwhile, is locked in on the franchise tag, which will pay him $27.298 million fully guaranteed in 2026 after the Cowboys decided not to engage with him and agent David Mulugheta in long-term contract talks this offseason. That's puzzling with Pickens fresh off producing a career year with 1,429 yards receiving and 9 receiving touchdowns on 93 catches. Ranking third in the entire league in receiving yards earned the 25-year-old the first Pro Bowl and All-Pro selections (second team) of his career. Neither Flowers nor London has registered as gaudy a receiving yards total as Pickens did last season.
He leads the trio in career receiving yards (4,270) and career yards per reception average (16.0), while London has the edge in career receptions (309) and a narrow lead in career receiving touchdowns (22). Pickens' 21 career receiving touchdowns are one behind his 2022 NFL Draft classmate. Translation: Pickens can now demand more money than both Flowers and London on a long-term deal with a straight face. That's a significant problem for Dallas for a multitude of reasons, despite Jerry Jones feeling like Pickens having to prove it again on the franchise tag is a win-win situation for both parties.
George Pickens just picked himself and CeeDee Lamb over ANY WR duo in NFL history 😤 🎤: @BMac_SportsTalk pic.twitter.com/n3yDGqMoPD
"This can be a very win-win thing that we've done here: us, George and George being on the team," Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones said at Dallas' opening training camp press conference . "Make no mistake about it: George could be a Cowboy for the rest of his career, and that would be a long time. Make no mistake about it. This [the franchise tag] just fit for us, and thank goodness it fit for him, and we got it done."
The love between Pickens and Jones is mutual ... until the two sides have to sit down at the negotiating table again next offseason.
"Super excited. I'm always super happy when someone thinks highly of me, so shout out to Jerry," Pickens said on July 30, via The Athletic .
Receiving yards per reception
Waiting to extend Pickens, rather than doing so when trading for him as a somewhat distressed asset in May of 2025, has come back to bite them. The talent was always there, and in 2025, Pickens showed how prolific he can be with a quarterback of Dak Prescott's caliber, rather than the mediocre carousel of passers Pittsburgh paraded through its franchise from 2022 to 2024.
Now, the Cowboys have two major contractual decisions to make that will determine Pickens' future in Dallas: paying Pickens vs. paying All-Pro wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, and paying Pickens vs. paying All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . Playing the waiting game led Dallas to re-sign their present-day No. 88 to a four-year, $136 million extension with $82 million guaranteed back in 2024. Delaying those negotiations in tandem with Pickens puts the Cowboys in a position where they have to choose between paying Lamb or Pickens, and Dallas will end up choosing Lamb. Dallas puts a premium on homegrown players they choose to extend, and Lamb has been everything the Cowboys have hoped for: he's developed into an All-Pro, five-time Pro Bowler who is also a team captain.
As for the Williams vs. Pickens debate, it seems as though the Jones family has already made their choice. They're choosing to prioritize the All-Pro anchor of their defense, whom they traded for, in an effort to make people forget about how they traded away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers .
"Absolutely, we're very open to that," Cowboys COO Stephen Jones said at Dallas' opening training camp press conference when asked about extending Williams. "We want Quinnen here for the long haul. Obviously, we've got a lot of resources tied up in him. He knows what we think about him. We've had some discussions with the agent about how to go about the process.
"Certainly he's [Williams] one of the best in the business, and we know kind of what that market is. Obviously, it evolves and changes with each new deal, which is the case at any position. Certainly, he's at the top of the list in terms of the people that we want to keep around here long term, and there's other players on the roster that we may take a look at as well as we move forward."
Next offseason, the Cowboys will likely end up either tagging and trading Pickens or allowing him to walk in free agency in exchange for a third-round compensatory draft pick, thanks to their inability to get ahead of the fast-evolving wide receiver market. Either outcome is deflating because Dallas successfully identified a high-level talent who could reach new heights within their high-powered offensive ecosystem. Choosing to procrastinate on addressing his long-term contractual future will likely lead to him ending up like Parsons: another All-Pro-caliber talent Dallas developed, going on to crush it with another NFL team for the long haul.

title: “The Athletic” ranked 35 NFL QBs. Where do the Cardinals rank?
summary: The Athletic is recognized as one of the nation’s top sports sites. Just like SB Nation, they cover every sport every day. And are comprehensive. Their coverage of the NFL is always spot-on, and bring stories that are beyond the game. RELATED: BRISSETT MAY START HALF THE SEASON NFL analyst Mike Sando has put together […]
full_text: Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett (7) throws a ball during training camp July 27, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Athletic is recognized as one of the nation’s top sports sites. Just like SB Nation, they cover every sport every day. And are comprehensive. Their coverage of the NFL is always spot-on, and bring stories that are beyond the game. RELATED: BRISSETT MAY START HALF THE SEASON NFL analyst Mike Sando has put together his annual “Quarterback Tiers.” This list takes the opinions of 50 NFL GMs and coaches and then ranks the veteran quarterbacks. Rookies are excluded since they haven’t played yet. Veteran Jacoby Brissett has been penciled in as the starter for the Arizona Cardinals on the team’s first “official” depth chart. Despite missing all of the offseason programs, this was expected and is no surprise. It remains a possibility that either journeyman Gardner Minshew or rookie Carson Beck may be named the starter for Week 1, but for now, the coaching staff has named Brissett. Sando has announced his list of this year’s QBs from 1 to 35. Yes, there are only 32 clubs, which means the same number of starting quarterbacks. But some teams are unsettled about who their starter actually is, such as the Cleveland Browns and Atlanta Falcons, so there is a sprinkling of extra candidates listed. Where do the Cardinals rank? What about the remainder of the NFC West Division? One thing is certain: there’s clarity at the top. ———————————————————————————————————————— Tier 1 Carries his team each week The team wins because of him Expertly handles pure-passing situations Has no real holes in his game Patrick Mahomes – Kansas City Chiefs (tie) Josh Allen – Buffalo Bills, Matthew Stafford – Los Angeles Rams Sando said this about Stafford: “Elite physical talent plus experience plus fast processing plus top-flight scheme has equaled Tier 1 status and MVP honors for Stafford. He wins at the line of scrimmage, and then he’s got this elite arm talent, and they’re well-schemed. Everything they put on him at the line of scrimmage, he makes it come to life. Best in the league at that.” Go deeper: After making his Tier 1 debut by a narrow margin last year, Stafford surged into the elite ranks on the strength of his MVP season. “He’s scary,” a defensive coordinator said. “When I first got in the league, there were more guys you had to worry about. You knew if you played Peyton (Manning), you played (Brett) Favre, (Tom) Brady, (Drew) Brees, it was, ‘Oh my God!’ Stafford has still got that, and he’s operating in a difficult-to-defend offense.” Stafford’s 46 touchdown passes last season were 12 more than any other QB’s total. ————————————————————————————————————————— Tier 2 Carries his team sometimes Handles pure-passing situations in doses Or has other dimensions that elevate him above Tier 3 Has a hole or two in his game 11. Brock Purdy – San Francisco 49ers Sando’s reasoning: “Purdy regained all the ground lost after his 2024 season, and then some, among voters. His average tier vote (2.28) and ranking (T-11th) are career bests. I think he is better than given credit for. Kyle (Shanahan) is great, but I think Brock Purdy – he can see it so fast, and he makes quick decisions, and he’s more athletic than you think. Really good player.” Go deeper: The 49ers rank third in offensive EPA per play since 2023, Purdy’s first full season as their starter. Purdy is No. 1 in EPA per pass play over that span. “Purdy is so impressive to watch in terms of how he creates,” an offensive coordinator said. “The scramble game is awesome. He’s really hard to sack. He’s in a great system with great players around him. It’s just a good fit.” It’s tough finding voters who don’t mention Shanahan’s system when discussing Purdy. “Solid 2,” an exec said. “Deceptive athletically, deceptive strength. He is the one guy who plays bigger than he is, and then obviously he’s a good fit with Kyle.” There’s that system talk again. 14. (tie) Baker Mayfield – Tampa Bay Buccaneers & Sam Darnold – Seattle Seahawks Sando had these thoughts: “Darnold’s climb over the past three seasons is rare for an established starter in the 13-year history of QB Tiers. Sam played his ass off the last two years. Darnold’s improvement from 4.00 to 2.36 is a full tier better than runner-up Daniel Jones among the 19 quarterbacks who appeared in all three surveys and had debuted before 2024.” Go deeper: “There are so many factors that determine a quarterback’s success, and Darnold’s the best example of it,” an exec said. “To get him into the right system, with the right coaches, and you have a game-breaking receiver, and a good defense. It’s a lot easier.” Drafted by the Jets in 2018, Darnold spent two years in Tier 3 with New York, mostly on the strength of his pedigree. He dropped into Tier 4 with Carolina and stayed there entering his first season with Minnesota. —————————————————————————————————————————- Tier 3 Legit starter but needs better running game or defense to win Lower-volume dropback passing offense suits him best 23. Kyler Murray – Minnesota Vikings Sando stated this about Murray: “This is Murray’s fourth consecutive year in Tier 3 and the first time he has fallen outside the top 17 in the rankings. But there is hope. The person I think who will change a lot is Kyler Murray, just because he’s around a quarterback coach, he will have weapons, he probably has something to prove, and his ability to escape the pocket, when he is on, is no joke.” Go deeper: “I love the signing,” an offensive coach said. “He will respect the head coach (Kevin O’Connell) because he is legitimate, and he needs to shine up what people think about him. He will be on his best behavior because it’s like being in a contract year. He will have better players around him than he ever had in Arizona.” An exec suggested Murray could thrive if the Vikings continue to play good defense while putting Murray under center, giving him a solid rushing attack and featuring him in a quarterback keeper game that regulates his exposure to injury. “They were doing a good job on offense (in Arizona), but losing the line coach (Klayton Adams, who left for Dallas in 2025) was a big loss, because their run game totally changed,” an exec said. Murray is going from one of the toughest places for a quarterback to win to one of the easiest. Last season, the Vikings were the only team to finish with a winning record (9-8) while ranking outside the top 25 in offensive EPA per play. They did it on the strength of their defense and special teams, which rank third in combined EPA over the past three seasons (Arizona ranks 31st). ———————————————————————————————————————- Tier 4 Unproven player; not enough information to classify Veteran who ideally would not be a full-season starter 33. Jacoby Brissett – Arizona Cardinals Sando expressed his thoughts about the low ranking: “Brissett has a 2-15 starting record over the past two seasons partly because his teams, New England and now Arizona, have been so bad on defense and/or special teams. Of the 28 quarterbacks with at least 17 starts over the past two seasons, none has gotten worse defense/special teams support than Brissett (-6.8 EPA per start). Not that Brissett himself has been a star. He can read defenses and put the ball where it’s supposed to go. Gets it out of his hands quick, can take shots, can challenge you down the field.” Go deeper: “I’m not saying this from a talent standpoint, but he operated as a quarterback as well as anyone we saw.” Defensive coaches rated Brissett higher than offensive ones did, producing the third-largest split in that direction behind Tagovailoa and Prescott. title: Falcons training camp Day 7 news, standouts, interviews, injuries
summary: FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — The Falcons conducted their second padded practice on Wednesday, bringing in full (or close to full) contact tackling for the first time. As you might expect, that led to a livelier practice, and we got to see a lot more from the offensive line and run game than we have in […]
full_text: Jul 30, 2026; Atlanta, Falcons, USA; Atlanta Falcons cornerback Avieon Terrell Jr. (12) shown during a drill during training camp at IBM Performance Field. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — The Falcons conducted their second padded practice on Wednesday, bringing in full (or close to full) contact tackling for the first time. As you might expect, that led to a livelier practice, and we got to see a lot more from the offensive line and run game than we have in days past. Overall, this was the best practice to date, with a more evenly-matched offense and defense than we saw early in camp. Read on for my notes from Day 7 of Atlanta Falcons training camp, including some quotes from Michael Penix Jr. and the recently-extended Bijan Robinson. Falcons training camp Day 7 notes and quotes This was the second padded practice and the first with full-contact tackling in 11-on-11. The players loved this and the energy level was noticeably higher. Veteran kicker Nick Folk got extensive work today, going 7/7 in field goal attempts ranging from the 31 to the 51. The most impressive was that 51-yard kick, which started with a botched hold. Holder Jake Bailey recovered quickly, and Folk still nailed the attempt. Folk spoke on Monday about his relationship with Bailey from years past, and how important that existing experience with a holder can be. That was probably a major factor in Atlanta’s decision to sign Bailey over Bradley Pinion this offseason. Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. spoke to the media after practice today, saying that he feels good and “could be cleared any day”. The final step will be a meeting with his doctor, and that is not currently scheduled. Still, Penix says that he’s feeling better and definitely improving week-over-week. When asked about playing with RB Bijan Robinson , Penix said all the QBs joke that “if you get into trouble, just ‘Bij’ it,”. Must be nice having that luxury! Bijan Robinson spoke to the media after practice to discuss his extension. He said it was tough to be on the sidelines, but it offered him a unique perspective that he actually enjoyed. Also mentioned that getting the compensation for the running back position back to where it should be was one of his goals. It seems like he definitely accomplished that! Injury Updates Safety Jessie Bates III was not on the field today. It appears he’s dealing with some kind of injury, but we haven’t yet received any official news. DL Zach Harrison had his helmet on today but was still working on the rehab field. He seems to be inching closer to returning. CB CJ Henderson has been held out of the last two days of practices, so it appears he’s also dealing with some sort of injury. Offense QB Tua Tagovailoa appeared to be more or less “full go” today, taking all the starters reps in 11-on-11. He had an early interception on what looked like a route miscommunication, then rebounded with a number of impressive throws. He hit Drake London on a 20-yard dig, layering the pass over multiple defenders. The short game was also very effective, as Tua hit multiple receivers with plenty of room for YAC to keep the offense on schedule. This was his best and most complete practice so far. QB Michael Penix Jr. had a very efficient day, hitting almost all of his passes save for an “arm punt” interception to Sydney Brown on a play that had been blown dead due to a “sack”. Penix hit Drake London on a deep corner route that was layered beautifully, and connected on a touch pass to Jahan Dotson on the right sideline for about 20 yards. He was also throwing with better touch and timing in the short game, peppering the tight ends (especially Austin Hooper) with targets and setting up some YAC opportunities. This was a very strong practice overall from Penix, who aside from not participating in 11-on-11, looks healthy and competitive. QB Cooper Rush was ahead of QB Jack Strand on the depth chart today, and Rush had the more effective day overall. Rush was efficient in distributing the ball to his receivers and kept the offense moving. The best pass was a well-timed crosser to Zachariah Branch that the rookie nearly scored on, just barely stepping out of bounds after the first down marker. Strand got fewer opportunities today, but continued to take chances downfield that didn’t necessarily pay off. With full tackling allowed, the run game finally got a chance to shine. The blocking from just about every unit was pretty solid and there were a number of impressive runs by Brian Robinson, Nate Carter, and Tyler Goodson . Cash Jones had a quieter day but continued to be heavily involved as a receiver out of the backfield. Rookie WR Zachariah Branch is clearly the story of training camp, and the team’s veterans have completely embraced him. The sideline lights up when he catches a pass. Drake London was crushed when Branch just barely stepped out on what would’ve been a big TD catch-and-run. I would say Branch had a more mortal day (by his standards), with a drop in 1-on-1s and a lost fumble on a catch in traffic. That said, he paired it with the aforementioned impressive plays, and he continues to rise up the depth chart. Another nice catch from rookie Zachariah Branch. Becoming a daily thing #Falcons pic.twitter.com/X8GC2QETOT — Kevin Knight (@FalcoholicKevin) August 5, 2026 WR Jahan Dotson continues to play the WR2 role, taking snaps outside and in the slot. Olamide Zaccheaus continues to play WR3 and has acquitted himself well thus far. Both players have been targeted and made the most of their opportunities. With Branch in the building, I feel pretty confident that this year’s WR corps is significantly better than the 2025 iteration. In terms of the depth receivers, WR Antwane Wells Jr. continues to make plays. He caught a deep TD pass from Penix that was the play of the 1-on-1 period. Wells and Chris Blair are pretty clearly a step above the rest of the competition at this stage, and both could make the roster if Atlanta elects to keep 6 WRs. Penix hits WR Antwane Wells Jr for the deep TD against CB Cobee Bryant #Falcons pic.twitter.com/Zq5rVtRSKS — Kevin Knight (@FalcoholicKevin) August 5, 2026 It’s pretty clear that the TEs will be heavily involved in the passing game, as Austin Hooper got a lot of targets and even Charlie Woerner got involved. This will be a big change from 2025. Defense Rookie CB Avieon Terrell opened the 11-on-11 period with an interception of Tua Tagovailoa. He spent time rotating between outside and the slot, but is definitely making his presence known. His physicality stands out in the cornerback room. Rookie CB Avieon Terrell getting physical to bust up the screen pass to WR Keelan Marion #Falcons pic.twitter.com/twyK75eYew — Kevin Knight (@FalcoholicKevin) August 5, 2026 An underrated competitor in the slot competition might be safety Sydney Brown , who probably had the best rep of training camp against Zachariah Branch in the 1-on-1s. He notched a pick off Penix (on a play that was probably blown dead, but still). He’s rotated into the slot more and more in recent days and offers a bigger, more physical presence than the smaller CBs. Sydney Brown with the sticky coverage on rookie WR Zachariah Branch #Falcons pic.twitter.com/feHlpH0iIF — Kevin Knight (@FalcoholicKevin) August 5, 2026 CB Mike Hughes continues to have a great camp. He’s been targeted a lot opposite A.J. Terrell and has answered the call, playing sticky coverage and making plays. With CB CJ Henderson sidelined, Cobee Bryant and Clark Phillips III have taken advantage of increased opportunities. Bryant had a nice PBU in 11-on-11, while Phillips managed to jar the ball loose from Branch for a turnover late in practice. The pass rush continued to be effective even in Jalon Walker’s absence. title: Free Agents the Falcons could sign in response to Jalon Walker’s injury
summary: The Jalon Walker injury was a devastating blow to the Atlanta Falcons defense. There aren’t going to be players available with his exact skill set, but the free agent market isn’t completely bare (yet). Atlanta should move quickly to minimize the impact of this injury. Here are the most notable free agents on the market. […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - DECEMBER 07: Leonard Floyd #56 of the Atlanta Falcons runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on December 7, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jalon Walker injury was a devastating blow to the Atlanta Falcons defense. There aren’t going to be players available with his exact skill set, but the free agent market isn’t completely bare (yet). Atlanta should move quickly to minimize the impact of this injury. Here are the most notable free agents on the market. Leonard Floyd Floyd was one of the first names that came to mind after Walker’s injury was confirmed. It wouldn’t take Floyd long to acclimate to the playbook, and he was a productive member of last year’s pass rush, finishing with the second most pressures (36) on the team. Floyd wouldn’t be able to replace Walker’s impact in the run game, but he’s a known commodity that can produce as a pass rusher. Floyd is likely going to have to come down from his 2025 asking price if he wants to return to the Falcons. Leonard Floyd wraps up Stafford on 3rd down 💪 LARvsATL on ESPN/ABC Stream on @NFLPlus and ESPN App pic.twitter.com/7K7cJh1530 — NFL (@NFL) December 30, 2025 Joey Bosa Bosa would be a big-name addition, but he doesn’t feel like a realistic option for the team. A player that’s suffered so many injuries throughout their career probably isn’t the best player to rely on, but Bosa himself will likely want to go to a team with better Super Bowl odds. Kyle Van Noy Van Noy is getting up there in years, but he’s still been a productive player in a rotational role. In 2025, he had the fourth most pressures (27) on the Baltimore Ravens and was a net positive in the run defense. His veteran leadership would be a good addition to the locker room, and Van Noy shouldn’t break the bank, considering he most recently played on a $4.25M deal in 2025. The age concern is legitimate, but the team doesn’t have too many options. Kyle Van Noy was a genius for letting Alohi Gilman handle the rock for 6️⃣ @Accenture pic.twitter.com/ieeSeYyXRb — NFL (@NFL) December 15, 2025 Von Miller Miller is the oldest player on this list, but he also had the most sacks among the group in 2025. He’s on a low pitch count these days and likely looking for a contender like Bosa, but crazier signings have happened. Haason Reddick Reddick is a polarizing player, and his most recent season on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers has many around the league down on him. He does have history with Jeff Ulbrich, and that connection could lead to him getting one last shot in the league. Derek Barnett Barnett wasn’t a star, but he was a key role player in the vaunted 2025 Houston Texans defense. He can get the quarterback on the ground and is a serviceable run defender. Nate Ollie coached Barnett when he was a part of the Houston staff in 2024. Barnett just turned 30 and shouldn’t cost the team much, with his most recent deal coming in at $4.0M in total value. Derek Barnett with the chop/spin sack. Have a pass rush plan! #PassRush #HTownMade pic.twitter.com/W07LXvJbVM — DLineVids (@dlinevids1) December 27, 2025 None of these players will be able to fill Jalon Walker’s versatile shoes, but they can help stop the bleeding and get this training camp back on track.

title: Falcons edge group returning to familiar land of uncertainty and fear
summary: When ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler dropped his camp notebook for the Falcons on Tuesday morning, he mentioned that the Falcons wanted to add a pass rusher. At the time, that was a reasonable thought given that James Pearce Jr. will likely face a suspension from the league. In the intervening hours, it has become an […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - NOVEMBER 03: Detailed view of an Atlanta Falcons helmet prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on November 3, 2024 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images When ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler dropped his camp notebook for the Falcons on Tuesday morning, he mentioned that the Falcons wanted to add a pass rusher. At the time, that was a reasonable thought given that James Pearce Jr. will likely face a suspension from the league. In the intervening hours, it has become an imperative, thanks to a torn ACL suffered by second-year would-be star Jalon Walker . There now exists an all-too-familiar scenario in Atlanta: An unspectacular group of edge rushers being tasked with being something much greater than the sum of their parts. Instead of a lack of talent or poor coaching, however, this one will turn on injuries and suspensions, because Walker is going to miss the season and Pearce is going to miss an undetermined number of games. Today, the Falcons would be relying on veterans Samson Ebukam and Azeez Ojulari, both quality players who do not have a consistent track record of being high-end pass rushers. Ebukam put up a career-high 9.5 sacks in 2023 but missed 2024 with an injury and was working his way back in 14 games last year, so perhaps he can return to that 2023 form in a major role. However, that 9.5 sack season was a major outlier in his career. Ojulari has a career high of eight sacks in a single season, but did so all the way back in 2021; his single season high water mark since then is six sacks. Beyond them, there’s Cameron Thomas, who I suspect has more upside as a pass rusher than we’ve seen but remains a better bet for a handful of sacks and quality run defense than anything else. Bralen Trice could be an impact player, but we have no idea what to expect after he missed both the 2024 and 2025 seasons with major injuries, and he profiled to be more of a complementary pass rusher and early down asset against the run before those injuries. Keshawn Banks lacks an NFL track record even if he did well in the UFL, and DeAngelo Malone just hit the reserve/PUP list yesterday. That group is solid enough. I’m not disparaging the individual contributors because they are quality players, and the Falcons were smart to add proven veterans who can contribute significant snaps. Realistically, though, combined these guys would probably post one of the lowest sack totals of any edge group in the NFL over a full season. Were they to stand pat, the Falcons would be leaning very heavily on schemed blitzes with their talented secondary and young inside linebacker group to try to paper over that weakness. The great Nate Ollie will be even more heavily counted on for his ability to get the team’s defensive line to pile up the sacks and deliver the pressures the EDGE group might not be able to manage. The good news is that with Brandon Dorlus, Zach Harrison, new addition Maason Smith, and other contributors, they should be able to do that. The bad news is that the Falcons are a substantially less talented defense without Walker, and between his ability to rush off the edge and the likelihood that he’d be employed creatively via blitzes, they’re losing a lot of pass rushing production and potential. Pearce will be around at some point—and it may not even be that long—and he lifts both the floor and ceiling of the group substantially. But even after he returns, the team will lack a player who has a history of wreaking havoc on clear passing downs, and that remains a massive need. But about that addition: We don’t know who it’s going to be, but it’s likely to be one of the bigger names (or multiple names) left on the market. We’ll get into the full list of who is out there soon enough, but names to keep an eye include Haason Reddick, Leonard Floyd, and Von Miller if the Falcons are serious about going after players with track records. I think they will be, and more than that, I think they have to be. Quoth Fowler: The Falcons are bracing for a James Pearce Jr. suspension stemming from his domestic violence arrest in February. It’s uncertain how many games he’ll receive, but how Atlanta handles the edge position will be worth watching. The Falcons have been looking for a potential pass-rush addition this offseason. The Walker injury is an unbelievably bleak note for a team that has many fresh faces and has taken pain to lock up stars, but has also endured a 2026 defined by Pearce’s arrest and charges, uncertainty at quarterback and right tackle, and now a series of injuries and question marks. If they can’t maximize the group they have and make at least one impactful addition, we may be right back to the Falcons pass rush derailing grand dreams for this defense, a familiar but deeply depressing place to be.

summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Ravens fans and fans across the country. The Ravens backed up the Brinks truck for Zay Flowers on Tuesday, signing him to a four-year, $140 million extension that makes him the fourth-highest-paid wide […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 4: Zay Flowers #4 of the Baltimore Ravens in action during the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on January 4, 2026 in Pittsburgh, United States. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Ravens fans and fans across the country. The Ravens backed up the Brinks truck for Zay Flowers on Tuesday, signing him to a four-year, $140 million extension that makes him the fourth-highest-paid wide receiver in the NFL. In many ways, Baltimore did not have a choice but to pay their star wideout. After a long string of disappointments, the team finally hit on a homegrown first-round receiver, and extending him now results in a much better long-term deal. Case in point: many were quick to point out that Flowers now makes as much as Justin Jefferson. However, Jefferson signed back in 2024, when the salary cap was just $255.4 million. It has since jumped to $301.2 million, meaning that Flowers’ $35 million APY represents a significantly lower percentage of the cap than Jefferson’s did at signing. Flowers also has two years and just under $30 million remaining on his rookie contract; adding his new deal results in a $28.3 per-year average over the next six years, a bargain for a player of his caliber. Now, we want to hear from you. Is Flowers worth his extension? Did the Ravens come away with a steal of a deal, or did they overpay for the 5-foot-9 speedster? title: Buffalo Bills 2026 scouting reports: C/OG Austin Corbett
summary: The Buffalo Bills lost left guard David Edwards in free agency this offseason, as the veteran signed a lucrative contract with the New Orleans Saints. Edwards was a stabilizing force for a very good Buffalo offensive line, serving almost as the command center in pass protection and blitz pickup. Especially in hostile road environments, you […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - AUGUST 26: Carolina Panthers guard Austin Corbett (63) during a NFL preseason football game between the Buffalo Bills and the Carolina Panthers on August 26, 2022 at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Buffalo Bills lost left guard David Edwards in free agency this offseason, as the veteran signed a lucrative contract with the New Orleans Saints. Edwards was a stabilizing force for a very good Buffalo offensive line, serving almost as the command center in pass protection and blitz pickup. Especially in hostile road environments, you could always count on seeing Edwards pointing out potential threats incoming from opposing defenses. Those are pretty large shoes to fill for whomever ends up winning the starting gig at left guard for the 2026 NFL season. In today’s installment of our “91 players in 91 days” series, we discuss a well-traveled veteran looking to fill Edwards’ shoes this fall. _____________________________________________________________________________ Name: Austin Corbett Number: 63 Position: C/OG Height/Weight: 6’4”, 306 pounds Age: 30 (31 on 9/5/2026) Experience/Draft: 9; selected by the Cleveland Browns in the second round (No. 33 overall) of the 2018 NFL Draft College: Nevada Acquired: Signed with Buffalo on 3/26/2026 Financial situation (per Spotrac): Corbett signed a one-year contract worth a total of $1,487,500. Thanks to the veteran’s salary benefit, his cap hit will be slightly less than that, coming in at $1,262,500 for the season. That number is also what Buffalo will carry in a dead-cap charge if they release him prior to Week 1. As a vested veteran, his entire base salary — $1.3 million — becomes fully guaranteed if he’s on the team for that first week. 2025 Recap: Corbett spent last season with the Carolina Panthers, which is where he’d played from 2022 onward. He began the season as Carolina’s starting center, but a Week 2 MCL injury led to the Panthers placing him on Injured Reserve. When he returned for Carolina’s Week 7 victory over the New York Jets, Corbett started, but this time, he started at left guard. Corbett did not start the following week against the Bills, but after Cade Mays suffered an ankle injury early in the game, Corbett went right back into the lineup at center. He ended up playing in 13 total games for the Panthers, starting 11 games combined at center, left guard, and right guard. According to Pro Football Focus , he was flagged for just one penalty during the season. He allowed two sacks while earning a 67.8 grade overall, which was No. 29 among 81 qualified guards. Positional outlook: Corbett is one of four players listed at center/offensive guard on the current roster. Alec Anderson, Sedrick Van Pran-Granger, and Connor McGovern are the others. Lloyd Cushenberry is listed solely at center. Tylan Grable and Jude Bowry are listed at tackle/guard. Bruno Fina, Da’Metrius Weatherspoon, O’Cyrus Torrence, Ar’Maj Reed-Adams, and Nick Broeker are listed at guard. 2026 Offseason: Corbett is in the mix to replace David Edwards in the starting lineup at left guard. He has seen reps with the first team during early training camp practices, rotating with Alec Anderson in that role as the starting left guard. 2026 Season outlook: Throughout his career, Corbett has been an above-average performer at multiple positions. He was a starter at right guard for a Super Bowl team, as he held down that role for the Los Angeles Rams when they won the title during the 2021 NFL season. The Bills could do far worse than someone with Corbett’s ability and experience in the starting lineup. However, Corbett’s versatility and veteran savvy also makes him an ideal interior line reserve. Whether he wins the left guard competition or not, Austin Corbett is someone the Bills would love to keep on the roster. There were plenty of people, myself included, who assumed that the left guard gig this season would be Alec Anderson’s to lose given the time Buffalo has taken in developing him; however, this is a win-now league, and for the Bills, 2026 is a win-now season. They don’t have time to wonder whether the player they’ve developed is going to be good enough to start, and they certainly won’t give the job to Anderson merely because he’s been here longer. The NFL is a business, and the main goal in this business is winning. If Austin Corbett is better than Alec Anderson, he’ll start at left guard this season for the Bills. If he isn’t, then he’ll likely be an active reserve on game days given that he can slot into all three of the interior positions along the offensive line. Buffalo could decide that they like another young player that they have developed, Sedrick Van Pran-Granger, enough to use Corbett as trade bait, but SVPG has really only played center in his pro career despite his C/G listing. It’s too early to tell which player has the upper hand in the left guard competition, but it wouldn’t surprise me at all if Corbett were to earn the starting gig. He’s started 78 regular season games and six playoff games in his career, which is more than all of the other players vying to replace David Edwards have even played in, let alone started, combined. Corbett is talented enough to win a starting gig with the Bills this season.
author: Sean Murphy

title: What will Buffalo Bills turnover battle look like in 2026?
summary: For the last… well I can’t really remember how long it’s been now actually, I’ve been examining the Buffalo Bills takeaways and giveaways for quite some time. I think it’s time to look back at the Sean McDermott in totality, and try to make some guesses for the 2026 season; the dawn of the Joe […]
full_text: For the last… well I can’t really remember how long it’s been now actually, I’ve been examining the Buffalo Bills takeaways and giveaways for quite some time. I think it’s time to look back at the Sean McDermott in totality, and try to make some guesses for the 2026 season; the dawn of the Joe Brady era… McDermott era giveaways We all know the narrative around Josh Allen. He’s turnover prone. That’s not precisely wrong. It’s also not precisely right. Let’s look at a chart. I’m sorry to say it, but it’s a valid statement to say that in general, quarterbacks are a primary culprit of a team’s giveaways. That said, when it comes to Allen the phrase “your mileage may vary” is an apt one. His first year was frankly, abysmal. Then he improved drastically, with the team hovering around average from 2019 – 2021. Then we got a couple years of spikes in 2022 and 2023. Since this is a predictive feature ultimately, I should point current head coach, Joe Brady was the quarterbacks coach and interim offensive coordinator for those two seasons. In 2024 and 2025 Brady was the offensive coordinator and we had an elite year with barely any giveaways, and then a pretty average year. The team’s identity shifted toward the run under Brady’s OC tenure, but it should be noted that the 2024 season with the scant turnovers featured a balanced offense where passing attempts did edge out rushing ones. Of course we also have no idea if this was Brady’s plan or McDermott’s plan, but we’ve gotta make some kind of prediction for the season so my take is… The seasons with Brady seeing a heavier influence were both good ones. Allen and company have the potential for a disastrous season (2023 data), but those do appear to be the outliers with recent upturns coming under the Ken Dorsey era of offensive coordination. Are you curious about the splits in the 2023 season where Dorsey was ousted and Brady became the interim? Of course you do. Under Dorsey, the Bills had 18 turnovers. With Brady at the helm as OC, it went down to 10. That’s not quite the full story though as Dorsey had 10 games that season with Brady only coordinating seven. That equates to 1.8 turnovers per game vs. 1.4 turnovers per game. Brady still has the advantage, but not quite as drastic. I’ll hold off on a numeric predictor for right now. McDermott era takeaways If there was one side of the ledger that constantly had me looking foolish, it was the takeaway side. Like before, let’s consult the chart. The term “regression to the mean” is pretty much built for turnovers, where it’s tough to stay on top consistently. I predicted regression to the mean plenty of times for the Buffalo Bills and as you can see, aside from the 2025 season and the 2019 one it simply just wasn’t happening under Sean McDermott. I should also note for full disclosure that last season I penned several articles where the main premise was that the Bills’ defensive roster was less talented than many of McDermott’s squads. I mention that because I don’t think the coach is out there looking for a pick-six personally, so talent matters. This side of the ball is a bigger question mark with McDermott gone and the defensive scheme likely shifting, if not outright changing under Jim Leonhard. It’s unlikely Joe Brady will look to be a dominant influence on the defense either, with his history strongly on the offensive side of things. Like above, let’s hold off on predictions for a moment. Turnover differential As is tradition, a chart. Anything on the positive side of the ledger is a good thing, as turnover differential is strongly correlated with success. The 2024 season is preposterous so we should 100% dismiss it as an outlier. That aside, the Bills only had a negative differential one time, Josh Allen’s rookie season which was the most catastrophic one on the board for giveaways. That leads me to predictions, which of course I’ll start with last year’s. I predicted 28 takeaways as I finally learned to bet on McDermott. Just in time for an average season. Whoops. I was off by eight. For giveaways, I predicted regression to the mean with 16 turnovers on the wrong side of the ledger. That was only three off, so not too terrible. For this season, I like the Joe Brady influence to be a stabilizing one and I think the Josh Allen narrative is overblown. I’m going to predict 18 giveaways as the team emphasizes risk mitigation and careful football to support a defense going through growing pains. On the giveaways, I just don’t have much faith in the team immediately gelling. I hate to say it, as I know feelings on the man are mixed, but Sean McDermott was a masterful conductor, orchestrating ways to take the ball away. The data supports this knack and Jim Leonhard will need to prove himself to earn that rep. Until then, I have to assume he’s part of the pack. I also don’t want to assume Leonhard will be terrible at prepping the team, and there are many McDermott era starters who will still carry on what they learned. I like the Bills to still be on the positive side of the differential, but barely. I’m predicting 19 takeaways as the Bills remain at the mean.

title: Buffalo Bills 2026 scouting report: wide receiver Dante Pettis
summary: The Buffalo Bills are searching for a solid punt returner this season. Last year, they had a revolving door at the position, and they eventually used their best wide receiver in the role. While he might have been good at it, that’s not typically something a team wants to do in subjecting their top offensive […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - JANUARY 04: Dante Pettis #11 of the New Orleans Saints runs with the ball during the second quarter of the game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills are searching for a solid punt returner this season. Last year, they had a revolving door at the position, and they eventually used their best wide receiver in the role. While he might have been good at it, that’s not typically something a team wants to do in subjecting their top offensive players to even more punishment on special teams. In today’s installment of “91 players in 91 days,” we discuss a player with plenty of experience returning punts in his career. _____________________________________________________________________________ Name: Dante Pettis Number: 87 Position: WR Height/Weight: 6’1” 195 lbs. Age: 30 (31 on 10/23/2026) Experience/Draft: 8; selected by the San Francisco 49ers in the second round (No. 44 overall) of the 2018 NFL Draft College: Washington Acquired: Signed with Buffalo on 7/30/2026 Financial situation (per OvertheCap): Pettis signed a one-year contract with the Bills. That deal is worth $1.3 million overall, but thanks to the veteran’s salary benefit, his cap hit is just $1.075 million if he makes the roster. Buffalo will not carry a dead cap charge if they release him prior to Week One; however, as a vested veteran, his entire base salary is fully guaranteed if he’s on the roster for the first game of the season. 2025 Recap: Pettis spent the 2025 season with the New Orleans Saints. He appeared in all three of New Orleans’ exhibition games, and saw sixteen targets in those contests. He caught seven passes for 87 yards and a touchdown in the preseason. He also did some work as a returner, taking one kickoff return for 20 yards and three punt returns for an average of 5.7 yards per return. Pettis did not make New Orleans’ roster, though he was signed to the team’s practice squad on October 2. He was called up three times in November before signing to the active roster on December 2. Ultimately, he appeared in eight games for the Saints, working primarily on special teams returning both kickoffs and punts. He averaged 23.4 yards per kickoff return on 15 attempts and 6.1 yards per punt return on 13 tries. While he didn’t see much time on offense through his first six games, he played a total of 89 snaps on offense in the final two games of the season. Overall, he caught 9 passes for 127 yards on 11 targets; in those final two regular season games, he made 8 catches for 113 yards on 9 targets. Positional outlook: Pettis is one of 14 receivers on the current roster. Tyrell Shavers, Khalil Shakir, DJ Moore, Max Tomczak, Mac Dalena, Keon Coleman, Skyler Bell, Joshua Palmer, Ja’Mori Maclin, Stephen Gosnell, Mecole Hardman Jr., Trent Sherfield, and Quentin Skinner are the others. 2026 Offseason: Pettis has taken some reps as a punt returner since signing with Buffalo. He’s been healthy through his few days of practice at camp thus far. 2026 Season outlook: Pettis has had his professional career derailed by injury, as he’s been placed on injured reserve four separate times in his eight pro seasons. He hasn’t come close to living up to his second-round draft pick status, nor has he shown much of the ability that allowed him to set an NCAA record with nine career punt return touchdowns during his time at Washington. It would be easy to look at a signing like this and say that he’s merely an experienced camp body who has zero shot at making the team in September. And yet, the Bills had Khalil Shakir returning punts at points last season. That’s not an ideal situation, and it’s something that Bills clearly want to avoid this year. If Pettis has an explosive preseason, he could just as easily slot in as WR6 as someone like Hardman Jr., whose best shot at making the team is also as a punt returner. Keon Coleman has seen some time returning punts so far at camp, as well, so that could be a way for a second-round disappointment of Buffalo’s own drafting to make good on his draft status. Pettis has a chance at the 53-man roster, but it’s just as likely that he’s auditioning for a role on the practice squad as a veteran option just in case someone else is injured. Given his lack of production throughout his career—he’s caught just 92 passes for 1,231 yards and 13 touchdowns in seven seasons and hasn’t returned a punt for a touchdown professionally—I can’t see a scenario where he makes the club. However, weirder things have happened. I think it’s likely going to be a short engagement in a Buffalo uniform for Pettis, but a strong preseason as a punt returner could give him a chance to break camp with the team.

full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - OCTOBER 25: Star Lotulelei #98 of the Carolina Panthers defends a pass by Sam Bradford #7 of the Philadelphia Eagles in the first half during their game at Bank of America Stadium on October 25, 2015 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Streeter Lecka/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #38. Star Lotulelei The Panthers wished upon a falling Star in the first round of the 2013 NFL Draft. Star Lotulelei, considered by most pundits to be one of the best defensive prospects in the draft that year, played his college ball at Utah. He filled a major hole in the Panthers defense at that time, but most people thought he would be long gone before the Panthers picked at 14th overall, especially since that draft was notoriously thin for top tier quarterback prospects. A concerning heart condition made some teams at the top of the draft skittish, passing on Lotulelei in favor of “safer” picks. The Panthers pounced, taking Lotulelei and not looking back. In the end, his heart was never an issue. Star would go on to play the entirety of his rookie contract with the Panthers, coming in and starting immediately in the middle of the Panthers defensive line. His 42 tackles and three sacks his rookie year earned him enough votes to finish fourth in the Defensive Rookie of the Year voting. The following four years as a consistent presence up front for the Panthers defense. While defensive tackles not named Aaron Donald rarely get the flashy stats, Lotulelei was a coaching staff favorite who sacrificed his own box score to eat double teams and let other players make plays. Near the end of the 2014 season, Lotulelei suffered a broken foot, requiring surgery. He reaggravated the injury in training camp of 2015 and was never quite the same player afterwards. After his five years in Carolina, he signed with the Buffalo Bills (Panthers North) and played there for three seasons before retiring. Nose tackles rarely get the credit they deserve from fans and the media, and Star was no exception. His presence in the middle of the defensive line, especially during the Super Bowl run of 2015, allowed other players to make names (and tons of money) for themselves. Those players, like Luke Kuechly, Kawann Short, etc., would undoubtedly agree that while he wasn’t a star, Star definitely earned this spot in our countdown.

title: Panthers vs Cardinals: Defensive Preview
summary: Hello CSR! One more day until we get that precious, precious first preseason game. Its been a long off-season, but something resembling professional football is finally here! full_text: Hello CSR! One more day until we get that precious, precious first preseason game. Its been a long off-season, but something resembling professional football is finally here! The Panthers (backup) defense will face off against a Cardinals (backup) offense led by Carson Beck this week, the 3rd round pick from this past draft at quarterback, so Arizona fans will likely be heavily invested in how the Cardinals offense looks in this game. The Panthers will be getting a look at several defensive backs and defensive linemen from the back end of their roster. Let’s take a look at what to watch for. Back up pass rush With Nic Scourton on the shelf for the 2026 season, the Panthers won’t be playing Patrick Jones or Jaelan Phillips, and I wouldn’t be shocked if 2025 3rd round pick Princely Umanmielen doesn’t see much work in this game either. This leaves Trevis Gipson, Thomas Incoom, Cam Gill, and Nick Hampton expected to get the majority of the snaps throughout the game. These preseason games are opportunities for one of them to claim a primary backup spot at OLB as the 4th guy on the depth chart essentially. How well they do against a rookie quarterback and the 2nd and 3rd teams should be monitored. The Corey Thornton and Will Lee show With Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn entrenched as the top 2 CBs, they definitely won’t play in this game. Its also possible Chau Smith-Wade doesn’t see a ton of work as a guy who has been through several preseasons in Carolina. One of the more interesting things to monitor during training camp has been the extensive work 2025 UDFA Corey Thornton and 2026 4th round pick Will Lee have gotten. Both should be safe to make the roster, and both could be major factors into the depth conversation going into the regular season. They may not play more than a quarter or two, but seeing how they perform will both be fun and will have real consequences for this team. I’m excited to see Will Lee go mix it up as an outside corner for the first time. Interior Defensive line rotation Derrick Brown, Bobby Brown III and Cam Jackson are both listed as the starting interior DL, but I could see Cam Jackson getting some action here after limited time in year one. Then the Panthers spent a 2nd round pick on Lee Hunter so he should be heavily involved from day one. Behind them, there’s definitely going to be space for someone to make the roster as key depth. Joe Person of the Athletic reported after practice on Tuesday that LaBryan Ray was placed on the reserve/retired list, so its unclear when he can or will return, and he’s been a major rotational piece for a few seasons now. So that leaves plenty of snaps on Thursday for Jared Harrison-Hunte, Aaron Hall, Elijah Garcia, Tywone Malone, and Kyon Barrs, who all should see a decent amount of time during these 4 quarters of an extra preseason game. I personally have my eyes on Aaron Hall, who has been said to be very impressive this off-season thus far. What are you watching for on the defensive side on Thursday?

full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - JULY 23: Head Coach Dave Canales of the Carolina Panthers looks on during the Carolina Panthers Training Camp at Carolina Panthers Practice Fields on July 23, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The preseason begins early for the Carolina Panthers this season. They are taking on the Arizona Cardinals in the Hall of Fame Game on Thursday Night at 8:00 PM ET on NBC. This will be our first chance to see Kenny Pickett, I guess, in a Panthers uniform. In an offseason that has been marred by injuries, it’s going to be nice to watch the team’s depth come together to play something that actually resembles football. Previous preseasons under Dave Canales have left a lot to be desired and have been followed by slow starts for the Panthers. Canales’ Panthers are 1-8 in the preseason and 2-10 in the first four weeks in the three seasons he has been head coach. Fans are looking for any sign of life tomorrow to suggest that the team has sorted out how to play football before October. One complaint they have had is that Canales is notoriously shy when it comes to playing starters in the preseason. The general idea is that keeping veteran starters and quarterback Bryce Young out of “meaningless” games protects them from injury. That is an idea that has merit on a team with as little depth as the Panthers have and with as many injuries as the Panthers already add up. The simple counterargument is that the team starts flat and guarantees losses in meaningful regular season games without the preseason experience to knock the rust off. I’m not expecting major changes this season, but perhaps there is a chance with the extra game provided by the Hall of Fame Game on the schedule. This week we are simply asking if you are confident in the current direction of the Carolina Panthers. As always, this is not asking if you think they are going to win this week’s game so much as your general feeling about the overall momentum of the franchise. Greene played for the Panthers from 1998-99. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #39. Kevin Greene The Carolina Panthers had one of the most successful integrations into the NFL of any expansion franchise in league history. Kevin Greene was a big part of that, as he led the team in sacks in all three of his seasons in Carolina, anchoring an overachieving defense for such a new team. Greene entered the NFL with the Rams. After three modest seasons, he broke out as a pass rusher with his first of 10 double digit sack seasons. He left the Rams after eight seasons for greener pastures and joined the Steelers, where he continued to dominate the league as a pass rusher. After the 1995 season, he joined up with his former defensive coordinator Dom Capers, who was then the head coach of the Carolina Panthers. Greene led the league in sacks and was named a first team All Pro at 34 years old. Despite the success, Greene and the team could not work out a new contract, and Greene was released. He spent one year with the 49ers, after which he returned to the Panthers and picked up where he left off. He racked up 27 more sacks and more Pro Bowl nomination at age 36 and 37 before calling it a career. Greene finished his career with 160 sacks, good for third all time. 41.5 of those came in his three seasons with the Panthers, which ranks sixth in franchise history. His time with the team was short and sometimes tumultuous given the contract dispute, but there’s no denying that Greene was one of the best pass rushers to ever come through Charlotte. He unfortunately passed away from a heart attack back in 2020, but he will always be immortalized in the Hall of Fame and in Panthers history. His massive production and contributions to the unlikely rise of the Panthers land him at number 39 on the list of top 100 Panthers of all time.
