title: How Anton Harrison Could Follow Cole Van Lanen’s Path
summary: When Jacksonville Jaguars starting left tackle Cole Van Lanen opened the 2026 training camp on the Active/Physically Unable to Perform list, the fan and media expectation seemed pretty straightforward: Walker Little would hold down the left tackle spot until Van Lanen returned. The offensive line depth chart would stay largely intact. Just six practices later, […]
full_text: When Jacksonville Jaguars starting left tackle Cole Van Lanen opened the 2026 training camp on the Active/Physically Unable to Perform list, the fan and media expectation seemed pretty straightforward: Walker Little would hold down the left tackle spot until Van Lanen returned. The offensive line depth chart would stay largely intact. Just six practices later, that expectation looks considerably less certain. Anton Harrison, the Jaguars’ 23rd overall pick in 2023 who has started 48 career games at right tackle, has spent the last six days primarily on the left side, and he has been dominant . Harrison was initially a left tackle in college at Oklahoma before Jacksonville drafted him 23rd overall in 2023 and moved him to the right side. Three years later, the conversation about moving him back to his natural position seems no longer hypothetical; it is happening on the practice field every single day. Coen-Approved Anton won all four of his one-on-one pass rush reps on the first padded practice day, including two against Josh Hines-Allen, the franchise’s all-time sack leader, while head coach Liam Coen praised his consistency publicly after Day 5. But most importantly, Coen stopped well short of closing the door on the switch becoming permanent, telling reporters simply that the team was seeing what works and what does not and that a permanent move would not be unwelcome. “I think he’s done a nice job. It’s part of what we’ve done, moving those guys around and seeing what sticks and if that ends up sticking, hopefully that’s a good thing for us.” For a coaching staff that has pretty clearly made a habit of backing up their public words with actions, this doesn’t ring as the normal NFL coachspeak word salad. The question is no longer whether Harrison can play left tackle. It’s about whether it makes sense for the Jaguars to allow him to. Contingency or Test Drive? The Harrison experiment did not emerge from nowhere, however. This is not the first time the current Jacksonville regime has leaned into offensive line versatility as a competitive philosophy. In their first season implementing Coen’s offensive system in 2025, the Jaguars cross-trained the majority of their offensive linemen throughout the offseason, deliberately creating competition and flexibility across every position on the front five. The result of that wide-open competition was a starting unit that most observers ultimately expected, but the process of getting there seemed to be an intentional, not accidental, process towards gaining a variety of experiences. Also, one piece of context from that 2025 competition sharpens the current picture considerably. Cole Van Lanen likely entered that offseason as a general depth option for the team, with Walker Little as the expected starter at left tackle. In the true competition that ensued, he may have been a contender for the starting left tackle job before a shoulder injury temporarily removed him from the offseason program. Whether Van Lanen would have won that role outright then, had he remained healthy, is impossible to say with certainty, though a reasonable assumption with hindsight. Using that example as a gauge, the team’s cross-training history clearly supports the move. If the Jaguars’ commitment to offensive line competition is a genuine organizational belief rather than simply a talking point, then Harrison’s current run at left tackle carries real weight beyond a temporary fill-in role. Additional Considerations Van Lanen ultimately earned the starting job in 2025, and with it, a Week 17, three-year, $51 million extension that followed. Were Van Lanen to remain on the right upon his eventual return from injury, his $17-million annual average salary would place him as a top-10 right tackle salary, behind the Denver Broncos’ Mike McGlinchey ($17.5 million). Harrison, meanwhile, is under contract through 2027, following the team picking up his fifth-year option in April. He’s currently eligible for an extension, which adds just another layer to this conversation of where to play, and pay him. Left or right? Chicago Bears RT Darnell Wright recently put ink to paper on a four-year, $116M extension with $93M guaranteed. Wright was drafted in the same class as Harrison and could be viewed as a similar prospect by some. Could Lightning Strike Twice? Notably, the catalyst that prompted Cole Van-Lanen’s 2025 move for the starting left tackle role was Uneven play early on by Walker Little, and A Walker Little concussion opening the door to Van-Lanen to permanently man the role, after what initially seemed to be only a temporary assignment The resemblance to last season is hard to miss. Harrison is now performing in a different starting role, created by Van Lanen’s absence, and he is doing so convincingly enough that the coaching staff would like to see more. Whether this storyline ends the same way Van Lanen’s did a year ago remains to be seen. But the blueprint for exactly that outcome already exists inside this building: Injury to an expected starter Camp performer locks down a higher-profile role in spot-duty Performer earns the contract to match new role Competition breeds change. And change can often move quickly. As the practice days continue to stack up, Anton Harrison is very clearly making a legitimate case to remain at left tackle. Jaguars fans, let us know your thoughts and predictions on the Cole Van-Lanen/Anton Harrison competition in the comments below!

title: Chiefs News: Chiefs drop ‘GEHA’ from Arrowhead Stadium name
summary: The latest The home of the Kansas City Chiefs is once again Arrowhead Stadium. Not GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. No, just Arrowhead Stadium. It has been that way since 1972, so the team “shedding” the sponsorship is not only welcome, but a nice way to pay tribute to a legendary stadium before the team […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - AUGUST 22: Kansas City Chiefs flag team after a score against the Chicago Bears on August 22nd, 2025 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri (Photo by William Purnell/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The latest The home of the Kansas City Chiefs is once again Arrowhead Stadium. Not GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. No, just Arrowhead Stadium. It has been that way since 1972, so the team “shedding” the sponsorship is not only welcome, but a nice way to pay tribute to a legendary stadium before the team moves across the state line in 2031. Kansas City Chiefs drop GEHA Field from stadium, return to simply Arrowhead Stadium | Associated Press The Chiefs and GEHA signed a naming rights deal in 2021 that resulted in the name change. But it never stuck among fans, and even players and coaches often forgot to use the official moniker, instead using the name it was christened with upon opening in 1972. In fact, Arrowhead Stadium has become such a well-known brand that just about everybody in Kansas City and beyond continued to refer to it that way during the recent World Cup, when FIFA renamed it “Kansas City Stadium” for the six matches played there. Eight observations from Day 7 of Chiefs camp: Kahlil Benson takes control at RT | The Kansas City Star In 11-on-11 near the 25-yard line, Mahomes drew the defense in to set up a screen for Kenneth Walker, who likely would have taken it for a touchdown in a game setting. Closer to the goal line, Mahomes nearly had a touchdown pass to Travis Kelce, but Kelce couldn’t keep his feet in bounds from my vantage point. From the 10-yard line, wide receiver Tyquan Thornton high-pointed a pass from Mahomes along the left sideline and, despite being elevated, found a way to toe-tap in bounds to complete the reception. A few plays later, the quarterback threw a quick pass to tight end Noah Gray, who scored the first of four touchdowns during team periods on the day. As the Chiefs experiment with heavier looks, especially in scoring areas, Gray remains a target to watch. Jake Briningstool and 4 more Kansas City Chiefs players with stock on the rise after first week of training camp practices | A to Z Sports S Xavier Nwankpa Dave Toub put Nwankpa on everyone’s radar back in June. Now, Nwankpa is putting himself squarely on the radar through his play during practice. He’s primarily worked with the second-team defense at safety, along with special teams. On defense, he’s flashed numerous times. His interception and return against Justin Fields on the first day of pads stood out most. Nick Jacobs’ Chiefs Camp Notebook: It’s Noah Gray Day in St. Joseph | KSHB Quarterback Patrick Mahomes and tight end Noah Gray connected on multiple touchdown throws during red zone work. The first touchdown Mahomes was able to bullet between two defenders. The second one, Gray was able to keep the defender at bay and catch the far-shoulder throw. Rookie quarterback Garrett Nussmeier made an impressive throw on the run and placed it in a spot where only wide receiver Omari Evans could reach for a sliding touchdown. Kansas City Chiefs reveal limited-edition Red Thursday flag for 2026 | KMBC Similar to last year, the 13th edition of the flag displays head coach Andy Reid’s iconic phrase, “How ‘Bout Those Chiefs,” this time on a red background with white and gold lettering. Flags are available for presale here starting at 10 a.m. Thursday, Aug. 6. Fans can snag a flag for a $10 donation, with proceeds going toward the Ronald McDonald House Kansas City. Around the NFL Sources: WR Stefon Diggs set to sign with Commanders | ESPN Diggs strengthens a receiver group whose depth had improved from 2025 but was still facing questions at the top, aside from McLaurin. Diggs, who was born in suburban Washington and played collegiately at Maryland, had made his desire to play for the Commanders known. Diggs attended Maryland’s first fall practice Wednesday and the university shared a video message on Instagram from the former Terrapins wide receiver. “Shout out to my Terps and go Commanders,” he said in the video. “Let’s go!” Sean McVay on Aaron Donald’s Rams tryout: ‘I think he can make the team’ | The Athletic Labeling the workout at the Rams’ facility as a “tryout” was a formality to comply with league rules and processes, head coach Sean McVay later said in an interview with NFL Daily, which is why it appeared on the league’s official transaction wire. “Best tryout that we’ve ever had,” a grinning McVay said. “I think he can make the team.” D.J. Jones says Broncos can break ‘84 Bears’ sack record: ‘We’re about to eat again’ | NFL.com “We can break it. We can break the record,” the veteran defensive tackle said Wednesday when asked about the Broncos’ sack goals in 2026. “What is that, 72? We can break it.” Those 72 sacks were compiled by the 1984 Bears, one of the best defenses in the history of the game. And Chicago set that mark in just 16 games, as compared to the 17 that the current Broncos have to work with. The ’25 Broncos’ 68 quarterback takedowns are tied for fifth-most all time behind the ’84 Bears, ’89 Vikings (71), ’22 Eagles (70) and ’87 Bears (70). Jones isn’t the only Denver defender who’s been confident this offseason about snapping Chicago’s record. Pass rush mate Zach Allen said in early July that the Broncos “fully expect to break it” in 2026. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Khyiris Tonga: ‘Peter Woods is a little pitbull’ “P-Woods, he’s a little pitbull,” defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga said after Tuesday’s practice. “He’s nasty. He’s got something to him, and he’s got a chip on his shoulder. [He’s] eager to learn — just a sponge. Just taking everything in and just learning and growing, it’s cool to see that. Really, all the rookies too. (Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs are coming off their worst season in over a decade. 2025 was not only the first losing season of the Patrick Mahomes era, but it was also the first losing season for head coach Andy Reid since joining the organization in 2013. Finishing 6-11, the Chiefs lost eight of their final nine games in 2025, including losses to division rivals the Denver Broncos , Las Vegas Raiders , and Los Angeles Chargers . There were a lot of factors that played into the Chiefs’ disappointing 2025 campaign. Like the fact that the Chiefs’ pass rush was exclusively found on a milk carton, or the absence of any hint of explosiveness at the running back position. Kansas City’s season was already in the trash heap by the time Mahomes tore his ACL in the Week 15 loss to the Chargers. Still, there is no doubt that Mahomes’ injury is when things went from bad to a dumpster fire. For a team that appeared in three straight Super Bowls from 2022-2024 (winning two of them), 2025’s fall from grace was a stark reminder that in today’s NFL, the fate of a franchise is constantly ebbing and flowing. As hard as the climb to the top is, the fall from grace is twice as sudden and bumpy on the way down. If the Chiefs want to climb out of the AFC West cellar and improve on last season’s third-place finish, they need to be more balanced on offense and find a way to get to the opposing quarterback. Kansas City seems to think they’ve figured out the solution to these problems. The Chiefs signed star running back Kenneth Walker in free agency this offseason, and on the defensive side of the ball, Kansas City invested heavily in the pass rush by selecting defensive lineman Peter Woods and edge rusher R Mason Thomas within the top 100 picks of the draft. In addition, the Chiefs retooled their coaching staff on offense, bringing offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy back into the fold, as well as hiring new running backs coach Demarco Murray and wide receivers coach Chad O’Shea. The big question is, have the Chiefs done enough to contend for a Super Bowl in 2026? FanDuel Sportsbook seems to think so. The Over/Under win total for the Chiefs is set at 10.5 this season, and has given Kansas City the fifth-best odds in the NFL to make the playoffs at -184. title: Chiefs training camp notebook Day 7: Josh Simmons is up a weight class
summary: On Wednesday, the Kansas City Chiefs had a weather-impacted practice for the second time in seven practices at training camp in St. Joe. This time, the team moved indoors for a good portion of practice, then came back out and finished on the wet grass fields to cap off the longest start-to-finish practice of camp. […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Josh Simmons #71 walks to the field before practice during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on July 29, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Wednesday, the Kansas City Chiefs had a weather-impacted practice for the second time in seven practices at training camp in St. Joe. This time, the team moved indoors for a good portion of practice, then came back out and finished on the wet grass fields to cap off the longest start-to-finish practice of camp. In this post-practice interview with CBS Sports’ Evan Washburn, head coach Andy Reid praised the players for staying focused through “sudden change.” It seemed like the old ball coach enjoyed putting his team through a unique circumstance, one that was rare, according to defensive tackle Chris Jones in a separate interview with Washburn . “It started lightning earlier; we went inside. The first time ever, in 11 years, we came back to the field,” Jones told Washburn. “It was a really, really good practice… get out here so the fans can see us and give us a little energy on defense.” Due to the rain, there were limited in-person observations from the Arrowhead Pride crew today. Check out the notes that were taken down in The Feed this morning . Reid broke down the list of injured players after practice, but he also provided notes on a few different players . One of the most significant was about second-year left tackle Josh Simmons. Andy Reid approves of Josh Simmons going up a weight class Reid was asked about Simmons’ weight in his press conference, a point of discussion among many in Chiefs Kingdom this offseason when he debuted a stronger, bigger physique during OTAs. “He put on weight in the offseason; he’s been able to maintain it,” Reid told the media. “I think it’ll help him, not that he couldn’t do it at the other weight, but this gives him a little bit more lead in his pants, and that pays off over time during the season.” In his own post-practice press conference on Wednesday, Simmons confirmed he is playing at a weight the team is satisfied with. “It’s definitely where it needs to be,” Simmons said about his weight. Simmons is paired up with third-year left guard Kingsley Suamataia on one side of the line. The two are building their chemistry; Reid has taken note. “You can see them communicating,” Reid noted. “Kingsley does a nice job with that, making sure Josh gets all the calls and everything. The more they play together, the better it’ll be; they’re both very gifted athletically, it’s just a matter of technique, fundamentals and all that stuff. They work like crazy on it.” “I understand how he goes about blocks now,” Simmons said of Suamataia. “What he’s seeing when he’s coming to the line. If I can understand and kind of have that telepathy with him, I think that we can play a lot faster.” On the other side of the offensive line, rookie right tackle Kahlil Benson seems to be settling in as a potential long-term starter alongside Simmons and Suamataia. Before we all get too far ahead of ourselves, Simmons has given Benson advice on how to proceed from a strong initial impression. “I think Kahlil’s doing a great job; he’s a very physical player,” Simmons shared. “I think he should just add onto that; I don’t think you can really teach effort. I mean, that’s what he’s giving out there, so that’s really all I’m telling him right now.” R Mason Thomas is testing Simmons, Chiefs’ offensive line “Extremely explosive,” Simmons described rookie edge rusher R Mason Thomas. “You almost have to be offsides to stay in front of him. I think he’ll definitely keep me and any tackle on their toes to make sure we’re on the snap count, for sure.” Get ready for Simmons leading the way on screen passes “Extremely scary,” Simmons said about running back Kenneth Walker when asked about the screen game. “We kind of know what [Walker] does and what he’s capable of doing. As long as we can just target and get to our assignments, we know he’s going to take us home. One-hundred percent.” Other notes from Andy Reid Fourth-year defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah is looking for a career resurgence in 2026. One aspect of his game that lacked early in his career was speed off the ball. Reid has noted improvement in that area. “With Gillotte down, he’s getting a few more reps in there, doing a nice job,” Reid said. “You can tell that his explosion off the ball is better… way different at getting off the ball. If there’s one thing that jumps out at me, it’s that.” It was a strong day for the tight ends at training camp Wednesday. Noah Gray was the star of practice, but second-year tight end Jake Briningstool has finally been able to showcase his skills to Reid and the coaching staff after missing nearly all of last offseason with a hamstring injury. “It’s great that he’s back-to-back in these practices here, then you get a chance to see what he’s all about,” Reid said of the former Clemson tight end. “He’s a good receiver, and he’s stuck his nose in there, and he’s blocking. My hat goes off to him; he just has to keep stacking them right now.” Without wide receivers Xavier Worthy and rookie Cyrus Allen in the mix for practice Tuesday and Wednesday, two lesser-known names have stepped up: Andrew Armstrong and Jimmy Holiday. “I like what Armstrong’s doing,” Reid pointed out. “He’s a big kid, strong, looks like the quarterbacks trust him… they trust him on his route running. He’s got good speed for a big kid and good transition; he’s not stiff coming out of breaks.” “Jimmy’s the other one,” Reid continued. “He’s really shown the last few days here, and that’s important for his job here.”

title: Andy Reid gives injury update after Wednesday’s Chiefs camp practice
summary: The seventh full-team practice of Kansas City Chiefs training camp took place on a rainy morning in St. Joe. After a brief warm-up, the team went inside to begin practice, but came back out for roughly an hour to finish practice on the grass fields at Missouri Western State University. After its conclusion, head coach […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 30: Head coach Andy Reid participates during Kansas City Chiefs training camp at Missouri Western State University on July 30, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The seventh full-team practice of Kansas City Chiefs training camp took place on a rainy morning in St. Joe. After a brief warm-up, the team went inside to begin practice, but came back out for roughly an hour to finish practice on the grass fields at Missouri Western State University. After its conclusion, head coach Andy Reid provided an injury update that was the longest it has been all of camp. He began by sharing that rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen, who has not practiced since sustaining a bone bruise during Monday’s practice, is “making improvement.” He added that defensive end Ashton Gillotte, out of practice with a hamstring strain since last Friday, is “making progress.” The same note was made of wide receiver Xavier Worthy, who missed a second practice due to a shoulder injury. Cornerback Kristian Fulton missed his second consecutive practice on Wednesday with a hip-flexor strain, according to Reid. During Wednesday’s practice, the linebacker position suffered two injuries that took players in the starting mix off the field. Chiefs LB Drue Tranquill has made an appearance in the training tent. pic.twitter.com/y9eFJldWDV — Matt Derrick (@mattderrick) August 5, 2026 Second-year linebacker Jeffrey Bassa suffered a groin strain, and veteran linebacker Drue Tranquill was seen off to the side of practice working through an ailment. “We’ll just see where that goes,” Reid said of Bassa. “Tranquill just had a little back spasm, so we backed off him there,” Reid added. In the place of Tranquill and Bassa was veteran linebacker Jack Cochrane, who is entering his fifth season with the Chiefs. He has earned a strong reputation among the coaching staff during that time. “Jack knows all the positions; he knows everything,” Reid said. “He’s a good special teams player on top of that. You feel comfortable, as a coach, putting him in any of those spots, and he knows that part of it. You need a couple guys like that out there.” In a positive trend at the receiver position, Rashee Rice took a step forward in his journey to 100% by participating in full-team, 11-on-11 periods for the first time this camp. “He got a lot of good reps today, which is important,” Reid said of Rice. “We just have to ease him back in and keep working, and we know he’s a good football player. You could see it actually got better as practice went on.” After a third consecutive day in pads at training camp, a lighter practice is anticipated for Thursday, starting at 9:15 a.m.

title: Chiefs training camp: 3 players with the most to gain
summary: Training camp is here, and the Kansas City Chiefs are ramping up practices in St. Joe, Missouri. During the first week of camp, the Chiefs practiced with no pads, but the team strapped up on Monday to kick off the physical portion of training camp. Within the 90-man roster, some players can see their stock fall, while others […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Esa Pole #79 walks to the field before practice during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on July 29, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Training camp is here, and the Kansas City Chiefs are ramping up practices in St. Joe, Missouri. During the first week of camp, the Chiefs practiced with no pads, but the team strapped up on Monday to kick off the physical portion of training camp. Within the 90-man roster, some players can see their stock fall, while others can rise to the occasion. It may just be practice, but camp performance can set the tone for how a player’s season will go, whether it is in a positive direction or negative. Let’s look at three players with the most to gain in training camp. Defensive end Ashton Gillotte Entering camp after a fairly unproductive rookie season, Gillotte will have a chance to show he has improved from year one to year two and earn more snaps. The Chiefs are in desperate need of pass rush help, and a thin edge-rushing unit means the young players in the group need to step up. Last season, Gillotte played primarily on run downs and finished with only 1.5 sacks on the season. While he was a stout run defender, any improvement in his pass rush could help him see his snaps jump significantly. Entering training camp listed on the second team, Gillotte will compete with players like Felix Andudike-Uzomah and rookie R Mason Thomas for more playing time. This trio of players is fairly unproven, and any player who can show a consistent impact in the pass rush game will likely find themselves taking most of the snaps opposite of George Karlaftis in 2026. Unfortunately, a hamstring injury sidelined Gillotte for the first few days of pads . Hopefully his medical status improves so that he can find his way back to the field soon. Cornerback Kristian Fulton Like Gillotte, Fulton did not participate in Tuesday’s practice, which is unfortunate because he has a lot to gain from a solid camp and the preseason. After signing a two-year deal with the Chiefs last offseason, Fulton missed half the season and did not see regular snaps until the second half of the season. When he was on the field, he played well, but the Chiefs’ cornerback room has gotten a bit more crowded this offseason despite the team trading All-Pro corner Trent McDuffie this offseason. The Chiefs cornerback room will be comprised of Mansoor Delane, L’Jarius Sneed, and Nohl Williams, with Kader Kohou able to play in a hybrid role between cornerback and Nickel. Fulton will have his work cut out for him, but with Delane yet to participate in camp, these are practices where he can show he can play consistently at corner for the Chiefs. If Fulton can push himself ot get back on the field, he could find himself earning more snaps headed into the regular season. Offensive tackle Esa Pole Last season, Pole turned heads as an undrafted free-agent tackle with solid performances in camp and the preseason, and by the season’s end, he found himself starting at left tackle for the final three games. It is clear that the staff likes what they have seen so far from Pole during his time in Kansas City, and headed into this training camp period, he is in a great overall spot. At worst, a “win-win situation”: Pole will likely reprise his role as one of the team’s reserve tackles, while he will still have a chance to compete for the starting right tackle job as camp progresses. So far in camp, newcomer Kahlil Benson has been the talk of camp, taking nearly every snap at right tackle over both Pole and Jaylon Moore. Despite this, camp is still in the early stages, and anything can happen between now and the regular season opener. Pole is still just as much in the competition as Benson or Moore to find the field, but another solid camp and preseason could not only help him find a starting role, but also lock up his status as the team’s swing tackle for the near future.
author: Caleb James

title: Khyiris Tonga: ‘Peter Woods is a little pitbull’
summary: Through the Kansas City Chiefs’ first two padded practices this week at training camp at Missouri Western State University in St. Joe, rookie defensive tackle has looked like a star in the making. Woods comes to the team via Clemson after the Chiefs made him the 29th overall selection in the April draft. The rookie […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Peter Woods #99 walks to the field before practice during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on July 29, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Through the Kansas City Chiefs ’ first two padded practices this week at training camp at Missouri Western State University in St. Joe, rookie defensive tackle has looked like a star in the making. Chiefs’ Peter Woods (99) vs. Hunter Nourzad pic.twitter.com/GuBWow4Z5Z — Jesse Newell (@jessenewell) August 3, 2026 Woods comes to the team via Clemson after the Chiefs made him the 29th overall selection in the April draft. The rookie — as well as his fellow first-year defenders — is also impressing one of his more veteran new teammates. “P-Woods, he’s a little pitbull,” defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga said after Tuesday’s practice. “He’s nasty. He’s got something to him, and he’s got a chip on his shoulder. [He’s] eager to learn — just a sponge. Just taking everything in and just learning and growing, it’s cool to see that. Really, all the rookies too. We’ve got a good group of rookies coming in.” Tonga also noted Woods’ advanced moves for a rookie and fathoms that he will only improve with time. “He’s a D-lineman,” Tonga explained. “He can play the run. He can do the pass. Technique stuff, he’s obviously learning. It’s different in college, the speed of the game. He’s there. You watch him during practice and the things he’ll be flashing. Just for him to continue to learn and to grow, the sky’s the limit for P-Woods.” Walker cheats in run period a little… but Woods looks like such a handful inside pic.twitter.com/Q4VhGZcaiV — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) August 4, 2026 Woods also should benefit from cutting his NFL teeth against some of the NFL’s best interior offensive linemen in center Creed Humphrey and guards Trey Smith and Kingsley Suamataia. Tonga confirmed that the trio is proving a formidable test for all of Kansas City’s defensive tackles in camp. “They’re the real deal having the three up front,” observed Tonga. “Really, the whole O-line, but going against Creed and Trey and all those boys, it’s iron on iron. Just being able to sharpen up and get better with those boys, it’s definitely good work.”

summary: The latest As the Kansas City Chiefs prepare for the 2026 season at training camp, there are plenty of players on the 90-man offseason roster with plenty to prove. full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Rashee Rice #4 walks to the field before practice during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on July 29, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The latest As the Kansas City Chiefs prepare for the 2026 season at training camp, there are plenty of players on the 90-man offseason roster with plenty to prove. However, when it comes to contract years and who needs to perform well this season to continue their career trajectory, wide receiver Rashee Rice fits the bill. He definitely has a lot to prove to the Chiefs and the NFL this season. Several big-name NFL players enter this season with something to prove | Associated Press Rashee Rice, WR, Chiefs The 26-year-old wide receiver, who missed the Chiefs’ voluntary offseason workouts and mandatory minicamp, served a 30-day sentence in a Dallas County jail for violating the terms of his probation, stemming from his role in a car crash that left multiple people injured on a Texas highway. Rice also had surgery to clean debris in his right knee shortly before he was sentenced. When he has played, he has been a productive target for Patrick Mahomes with 156 catches for 1,797 yards and 14 touchdowns. But Rice has also played just 28 games in three seasons because of a suspension and injuries. Why Your Team Sucks 2026: Kansas City Chiefs | Defector Let’s savor the flavor, shall we? Here’s Justin Herbert torching the shit out of the Chiefs down in Brazil to open the 2025 season. Here’s TE Travis Kelce , who used to be good, fumbling an easy touchdown pass which the Eagles picked off and nearly housed on the return. Here’s QB Patrick Mahomes , who also used to be good, gifting Devin Lloyd and the Jags a 99-yard pick-six Five Observations from Tuesday’s Practice | Chiefs Training Camp 8/4 | The Mothership 1. It was Alumni Day at camp. As they do every year, the Chiefs invited dozens of former players to practice on Tuesday morning. In total, twenty-six former players – representing generations of Chiefs football – attended the practice. Some recent players who stopped by included Spencer Ware, Charcandrick West and Dwayne Bowe. Following practice, Head Coach Andy Reid invited the alumni onto the field to break down the huddle alongside the current players. Observations from Chiefs camp Day 6: Rashee Rice, L’Jarius Sneed take next steps | The Kansas City Star Beginning the next 11-on-11 period out of the shotgun, Mahomes served up a perfect pass to Tyquan Thornton, who was breaking to the right sideline. Two plays later, Mahomes hit Walker in the left flat, and upon seeing traffic, Walker flipped the field the other way to find open grass. “That’s just how I’ve been playing since I was a kid,” Walker said. “Just learning from my pops and watching backs in the league. Honestly — just learning from my pops though. He says, ‘Too many people over here? Go the other way.’ And I feel like it still works to this day. I don’t want to run into a crowd if I can go somewhere in open field.” Seeing more ‘Stop the Chop’ signs around Kansas City? Campaign to rename Chiefs goes even bigger | NPR in Kansas City Every year, the Kansas City Indian Center puts up billboards in the fall that call on the Kansas City Chiefs football team to change their name and stop the so-called “tomahawk chop.” Gaylene Crouser, executive director of the Center, said that the billboards could be seen a little earlier and more widely than usual this year because of the World Cup. “It was a little more than we normally do just because of the opportunity based on the number of people that we were expecting to be able to see them,” Crouser told KCUR’s Up To Date. Around the NFL Sources: Falcons, RB Robinson reach 3-year deal worth up to $75M | ESPN Robinson will receive $51 million guaranteed. The deal, negotiated by Nicole Lynn of Klutch Sports, will end the running back’s weeklong hold-in at training camp. With the new deal, Robinson will now make $22.25 million per year, surpassing the Philadelphia Eagles’ Saquon Barkley ($20.6 million) as the highest-paid running back year-over-year in the league. That could change soon, though, with Detroit Lions star Jahmyr Gibbs also holding in while he waits for a contract extension. Ravens, wide receiver Zay Flowers agree to 4-year contract extension | The Athletic The extension is for four years and worth $140 million, with $108 million in guaranteed money, per team sources who were not permitted to speak because financial details had not yet been released. This extension makes Flowers the fourth-highest-paid receiver in the NFL behind the Seattle Seahawks’ Jaxon Smith-Njigba ($42.15 million per year), the Cincinnati Bengals’ Ja’Marr Chase ($40.25 million) and the Atlanta Falcons’ Drake London ($35.3 million). Dexter Lawrence ‘terrorizing practice’ at Bengals training camp | NFL.com “Honestly, he’s been terrorizing practice,” wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase told Jori Epstein of Yahoo Sports . “I can honestly say that.” Lawrence is coming off a ½-sack season, but that stat belies his ability to impact the middle of a defense, both against the run and pass. title: Los Angeles Chargers Roster: Trey Pipkins, OL, scheme fit, 2026 outlook
summary: Next up in our 90-in-90 series is veteran offensive lineman Trey Pipkins! Will the seven-year veteran find his way back into the starting lineup for the Chargers this year? Let’s take a look at his chances! Basic Info Height: 6’6Weight: 307College: Sioux FallsExperience: 7 A native of Apple Valley, Minnesota, Pipkins starred on the offensive […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - JANUARY 11: Trey Pipkins III #79 of the Los Angeles Chargers looks on during the national anthem prior to an NFL wild card playoff game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on January 11, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Next up in our 90-in-90 series is veteran offensive lineman Trey Pipkins! Will the seven-year veteran find his way back into the starting lineup for the Chargers this year? Let’s take a look at his chances! Basic Info Height: 6’6 Weight: 307 College: Sioux Falls Experience: 7 A native of Apple Valley, Minnesota, Pipkins starred on the offensive line for Apple Valley High School. As a junior, he helped lead his team to a 8-3 record and the school’s first appearance in the state playoffs in over 19 years. As a senior, he blocked for a quarterback that set school records in single-season passing yards and passing touchdowns. Pipkins stayed fairly close to home by committing to play at the University of Sioux Falls where he was a three-year starter for the Cougars. After redshirting in 2014, Pipkins saw time in 10 games while playing mainly on special teams and sparingly on the line. In those limited snaps, he managed to allow zero sacks. As a first time starter in 2016, he got the nod for all 10 games the team played and earned his first All-NSIC honor with the second team. He repeated the postseason accolade after starting 12 games the following year, as well. In 2018, Pipkins put the cherry on top of his lengthy college career by earning not only a First-Team All-NSIC selection, but he was also voted to the AP’s Division II All- American First Team. This was the season that helped him catch the eye of NFL scouts and it earned him an invite to the East-West Shrine Game to play against some of the best talent in the country. In March of 2019, Pipkins also became the first player from Sioux Falls to be invited to the NFL Scouting Combine and he certainly did not disappoint. At 309 pounds, he ran a 5.12 forty-yard dash and jumped 33.5 inches in the vertical which was a top mark among all offensive linemen at the event. Following Pipkins’ selection with the 91st pick, the Chargers had no intentions of having him see the field as a rookie. However, thanks to a string of injuries, Pipkins was called upon to start three games, including the final two of the season. During his sophomore campaign, Pipkins lost the training camp battle to Sam Tevi for the starting left tackle spot. However, with nagging injuries to right tackle Bryan Bulaga, Pipkins ended up starting five games last year, mainly at right tackle. During the 2021 season, Pipkins lost the starting right tackle job to Storm Norton in training camp. Norton started the majority of games but Pipkins still recorded a pair of starts due to injuries to the former. In 2022, Pipkins finally broke through to win the starting job which he held for 14 games during the regular season. A nagging MCL injury kept him out of three contests, but overall Pipkins had his best season as a pro. Following the season, the Chargers signed him to a three-year contract to keep him as the team’s starting right tackle for the foreseeable future. Zion Johnson, Trey Pipkins, and Donald Parham parted the red sea at the goal line 😤 pic.twitter.com/9mcorO9Jkn — Steven Haglund (@StevenIHaglund) December 20, 2022 In 2023, Pipkins stayed healthy and started all 17 games for the Chargers. The 2024 season brought with it a position change for Pipkins who started 15 games at right guard following the drafting of Joe Alt to hold down the right edge. After beginning the 2025 season looking like he be the team’s swing tackle, Pipkins was forced into starting duties following injuries to both Rashawn Slater and Alt. The veteran saw starts at multiple spots, but spent most of his 10 starts that year at right tackle. The Good Pipkins is the longest-tenured offensive lineman on the Chargers and he’s managed to keep his value high as a versatile blocker who could play both tackle and guard spots in a pinch. He’s always been an athletic lineman and that could serve him well as a potential starter in Mike McDaniels’ outside zone scheme. The Bad Pipkins has always been “fine” when he’s been on the field for the Chargers, but his games where he’s been impactful have always been few and far between. After seven years with the Chargers, I believe we’ve come to what Pipkins is and will continue to be in the NFL which is a dependable backup who can be a starter when needed. 2026 Outlook Pipkins is currently in the running for the starting left guard job, but that also happens to be a competition that features four other players in Kayode Awosika, Jake Slaughter, Trevor Penning, and Branson Taylor. Pipkins’ athletic profile should fit well, but it’s been mostly Awosika and Slaughter who have been earning reps with the first team. If Pipkins does not earn a starting job, he’d then look to earn the swing tackle role which may not be a sure-thing given Penning’s experience there for the team in 2025.

title: Which Ram falls off the roster if Aaron Donald returns?
summary: With each passing day, Aaron Donald’s return to the Los Angeles Rams seems more and more likely. Donald worked out with team equipment on Wednesday, which required the Rams to report his activity to the league office. Sean McVay and the team have maintained that Donald would not return unless he was confident he could […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - JANUARY 14: Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams runs around the edge during an NFC Wild Card Playoff football game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on January 14, 2024 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Ryan Kang/Getty Images) | Getty Images With each passing day, Aaron Donald’s return to the Los Angeles Rams seems more and more likely. Donald worked out with team equipment on Wednesday , which required the Rams to report his activity to the league office. Sean McVay and the team have maintained that Donald would not return unless he was confident he could play at the elite level we are accustomed to from him. Donald wouldn’t come back to be a part-time player or live off his reputation. He wants to make a difference on the defensive line next to Myles Garrett. While Donald’s return would largely be positive news for the Rams organization, it would also in turn be bad news for someone on the back of the roster. LA would need to cut someone from training camp in order to make room for the future hall of famer. So who becomes the odd man out? Here are some options: Defensive line The most logical place to start. It’s purely a numbers game and if Donald is added to the roster, the most likely place to trim would be his same position group. These are the players on uncertain ground: Larrell Murchison Jaxson Moi Payton Zdroik Bill Norton One benefit working in Norton’s favor is that he is more of a defensive tackle while the other aforementioned names are more ends. Still, the Rams have plenty of backups at tackle even though Norton did show promise last preseason. Kobie Turner, Poona Ford, Tyler Davis are locks to make the roster. Recent draft choices in Ty Hamilton and Tim Keenan may be competing for a spot. Murchison is also likely safe for now, though he’s bounced on and off the roster multiple times in recent years. Moi and Zdroik don’t bring much name recognition to the table. That isn’t a positive in training camp. Other names to watch Matthew Caldwell, QB LA may need Caldwell just to make it through the three preseason games. We still don’t know how much or if at all we will see each of Stetson Bennett and/or Ty Simpson in the exhibitions. But the main question is whether the Rams keep two or three quarterbacks. Caldwell has a remote chance to make the team. Why not sever ties now?

title: Aaron Donald has official ‘workout’ with Rams
summary: For the first time in two years, Aaron Donald is officially involved in Rams training camp. Donald, who has been mulling a return from retirement over the last couple of months, worked out with the team on Wednesday. The “workout” was submitted by the team to the NFL, per league rules, because Donald was using […]
full_text: For the first time in two years, Aaron Donald is officially involved in Rams training camp. Donald, who has been mulling a return from retirement over the last couple of months, worked out with the team on Wednesday. The “workout” was submitted by the team to the NFL, per league rules, because Donald was using team equipment at their facilities at Loyola Marymount University. It’s not a return yet. But it is the closest thing fans have had so far as proof that Donald has one foot back in the door. Aaron Donald wanted to do a workout in a football helmet, and even though he did not wear pads during it, he used Rams’ team equipment at their facility during training camp, requiring them to report his activity to the NFL. https://t.co/4egBgDAiLH — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 5, 2026 The Aaron Donald saga continues to move forward. Earlier this week, it was reported that Aaron Donald would not rejoin the team until the team returned back to Woodland Hills . However, today’s news certainly accelerates the timeline of Donald’s potential return to the team for the 2026 season. There is also the issue of the $30 million that needs to be worked out . Speculation on Donald’s return has been a daily recurrence, from one day when he may return midseason to the next when he’s supposedly going to join the team any minute now and go full, 100-percent when the season starts. Can confirm that Aaron Donald's workout at the team facility in Woodland Hills today was reported on the daily NFL transactions as a "tryout." Just another sign that Donald is getting closer to a return to the LA Rams. pic.twitter.com/i9tk4afHaf — Michael J. Duarte (@michaeljduarte) August 5, 2026 And what will Donald’s return do to the players expected to play his position before this all started? Should the team trade Braden Fiske if they’re just going to push him to the side for Donald? Donald’s return is exciting, but anything other than simple. If there’s anything that’s not confusing though, it’s that every single news item and rumor that has come through since the beginning has gotten Donald closer to return, with not one of those reports suggesting he’s not coming back.

title: Rams predicted to win NFC West in 14-3 tiebreaker
summary: The Seattle Seahawks may have won the NFC West by two games last year, but that alone doesn’t paint a clear picture of just how close both the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers came to winning the division and earning the number one seed. The 12-5 Rams had multiple opportunities to beat the […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - DECEMBER 18: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams avoids a tackle from Leonard Williams #99 of the Seattle Seahawks during overtime at Lumen Field on December 18, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks may have won the NFC West by two games last year, but that alone doesn’t paint a clear picture of just how close both the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers came to winning the division and earning the number one seed. The 12-5 Rams had multiple opportunities to beat the Seahawks and virtually lock up the NFC West in Week 16, then the 12-5 just had to beat Seattle in Week 18 to do it. What if this year’s division doesn’t just feature one 14-3 team like it did last year, but two? And what if the Rams come out ahead and win the tiebreakers this time? That could be their ticket back to the Super Bowl because nothing is as powerful as the number one seed. At least one writer thinks that will happen. USAToday’s Nate Davis not only predicted that the Rams would win the Super Bowl , but that they would win the division in a tiebreaker of the 14-3 Seattle Seahawks, prior to defeating the Seahawks, Cowboys, and Bills in the playoffs. (1) Los Angeles Rams (14-3): What else needs to be said about this would-be juggernaut? Sure, reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, 38, must continue to defy Father Time. WR Puka Nacua needs to stay out of the off-field headlines as he tries to convince the organization he’s worthy of a bodacious bag. DC Chris Shula has those significant new parts to mesh – and maybe an old one if Donald unretires. At the very minimum, the special teams can’t be an Achilles heel. And the Seahawks remain a bugaboo. Still, the Rams have won 20 of their last 28 games, many of the losses over that stretch of the fluky variety, and have more star power than any team in the league. Anything less than a Lombardi would be a disappointment – especially since Stafford’s age and several expiring contracts, Nacua’s chief among them, could necessitate a drastically altered roster in 2027. It would be one thing for Davis to cop out and say that no other NFC teams were a real challenge to L.A., and that could certainly happen, but instead he set up a situation in which Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford need every last second of the NFL season to earn the number one seed and win the Super Bowl because he also has the Seahawks going 14-3 this season. That’s far more exciting. Especially because the Rams and Seahawks face each other twice in the last three weeks. The No. 1 Rams are the Super Bowl favorites, and for great reason. They're the most aggressive team in the NFL, and it has paid off with the top roster in the sport. https://t.co/tdMsibJSCx — Frank Schwab (@YahooSchwab) August 5, 2026 Consider the massive implications of Week 16 and Week 18 if the Rams and Seahawks both go 14-3. Presumably if the Rams win the division, they must beat Seattle at least once in that span. Let’s say it’s Week 18. Then the Week 18 game would be a 13-3 team against a 14-2 team and the 13-3 team wins the Super Bowl. 14-2 vs. 13-3 would be the second-biggest such game in history, only defeated by the time that the 15-2 Lions beat the 14-3 Vikings two years ago for the NFC North and the number one seed. L.A. vs Seattle could be even bigger than that. Davis also has the 49ers going 11-6, but losing in the first round to the Bears. He has Seattle beating the Saints and the Cowboys beating the Lions in the first round. Then the Rams beat the Seahawks and the Cowboys beat the Bears, setting up Roger Goodell’s dream matchup of the Rams vs the Cowboys in the NFC Championship. In the AFC Championship, the Bills beat the Ravens. Do I think this will happen? It’s all pretty chalky to me. Davis shies away from any surprises, which is never the case. I like at least one team to shock the world this year, and my pick is the Tennessee Titans. Maybe the Titans won’t win a playoff game, but I’ll say that they can reach the playoffs and Cam Ward becomes one of the NFL’s biggest stars. Having the Saints in the playoffs is a bit surprising, but less so because of the division they play in; although Tyler Shough could also become a star. The Rams already have many stars of their own. That’s why many expect them to win the NFC West and the Super Bowl, even if for the second year in a row, the division has both of the league’s two best teams.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Rams making different travel plans than 49ers
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are taking a completely different approach in their travel plans to Melbourne, Australia than the San Francisco 49ers are for their season-opening game. Whereas the Niners will leave nine full days before the game, the Rams will reportedly arrive just one day before kickoff, according to ESPN’s Dan Graziano. This lines […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 09: Kyren Williams #23 of the Los Angeles Rams runs the ball against Dee Winters #53, Drake Nugent #66, and Renardo Green #0 of the San Francisco 49ers in the first quarter of a game at Levi's Stadium on November 09, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are taking a completely different approach in their travel plans to Melbourne, Australia than the San Francisco 49ers are for their season-opening game. Whereas the Niners will leave nine full days before the game, the Rams will reportedly arrive just one day before kickoff, according to ESPN’s Dan Graziano . This lines up with something Sean McVay said four months ago on the Up and Adams show : “We were like SEAL Team 6,” coach Sean McVay said of the team’s trip to London. “We’re in and out before you know what happened.” How will those plans impact the players in Australia? For clarity, when I was researching this piece, I found it much simpler to ignore mentions of days of the week. There is a 17-hour time difference at that time of year which is all you need to know. Circadian rhythms and two ways to balance them Your circadian rhythm is your body’s natural 24-hour internal clock. It controls when you sleep, wake, eat, and release hormones. Schedule changes, such as shift work or jet lag from travel, or when you eat and exercise, can affect this natural rhythm, resulting in poor sleep quality and daytime fatigue. Kyle Shanahan wants to give his players ample time to acclimate to the time change: “Usually when you travel with a [16]-hour flight, you don’t want to get there the day before because you lose like a whole day there or two and you’re just messed up,” Shanahan said. “The people we’ve talked to, you don’t feel normal until like the third or fourth day,” Shanahan said. “So, we’d like to go out seven days early. But since it takes a day and a half to travel there, we’re going to go nine. I think we leave on Wednesday and land on a Friday. And so, then we get there about seven days before our game.” The issue with this approach is that they’ll face the same acclimation period when they return stateside. Will they be fully recovered for their Sunday afternoon game 10 days later? McVay and the Rams are taking the opposite strategy: “It’ll be a similar approach, and really the goal for us is to try to keep guys in as close to a rhythm and routine as possible,” McVay said. “This is new to us, even going this far. I trust our group and most importantly, what’s going to be best for our players. We always try to take that into consideration.” A possible Rams itinerary All times are PST Leave 5:00 am Wednesday Arrive 9:00 pm Bed 11:00 pm Breakfast 8:00 am Thursday Game 5:35 pm With the exception of weights and some treatments, the typical gameday routine can be followed with some modifications. The players can follow their typical sleep routines on the flight home, and they shouldn’t upset their circadian rhythms. As an added bonus, the Rams have an extra 28 hours, compared to the Niners’ prep time, to prepare for their Giants game. The only real obstacle should be finding rooms with blackout curtains and quiet rooms so the players can sleep during their body clocks’ hours. Oh…and having Matthew Stafford’s back hold up over the two 16-hour flights.
author: John Newman

title: Matthew Stafford is QB under the most pressure in 2026
summary: Despite winning a Super Bowl and MVP honors, Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford still has plenty to prove. In fact, it’s fair to label him as the signal caller facing the most pressure ahead of the 2026 season. Yep, more than Dak Prescott, who has yet to guide the Cowboys to the NFC Championship […]
full_text: Westchester, - August 01: Quarterback Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams during the Los Angeles Rams training camp on the campus of Loyola Marymount University in Westchester on Saturday, August 1, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Despite winning a Super Bowl and MVP honors, Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford still has plenty to prove. In fact, it’s fair to label him as the signal caller facing the most pressure ahead of the 2026 season. Yep, more than Dak Prescott, who has yet to guide the Cowboys to the NFC Championship and beyond. More than Justin Herbert, who has yet to win a playoff game. More than Jalen Hurts, who has won a Super Bowl, but most everyone is still unsure about him. Heck, more than even Josh Allen, who has failed in his mission (thus far) to lead the Bills back to the Super Bowl. Stafford is facing the heat more than any of those other QBs simply because he’s the face of a super team. Los Angeles improved its defense by adding Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson, and decided to throw in Myles Garrett for the hell of it. The veteran recently called the Garrett acquisition a “shot in the arm,” which is definitely underselling it. Garrett is more than a “shot in the arm” — he’s what pushes a contender into title favorite status. The Rams were considered one of the best teams in the NFL before his arrival, and with him in tow, they’re clear favorites to win it all in February. TST’s own JB Scott noted L.A.’s Super Bowl odds improved by at least 200 points following the trade. FanDuel Sportsbook has the team at +550 odds to win the 2027 Super Bowl, way ahead of Seattle at +1100. Winning a Super Bowl was the goal all offseason after falling short against the Seahawks in the NFC Championship. Now, thanks to the all-in moves for Garrett and company, winning the big game is the only acceptable outcome. As we know, quarterbacks face the brunt of the heat whenever they fall short of expectations. In a team sport like football, I guess it’s only fair to do so. That’s the cost of playing QB in the NFL. You hear that, Stafford? You asked for this! Look, Stafford has already been in this position before. He faced pressure to guide a loaded Rams team to the Super Bowl in Year 1, and he delivered. Stafford doesn’t need another MVP season. His legacy and Hall of Fame chances will only be helped if he can secure another title. However, what he needs is to avoid the key mistakes that derail a title run while also providing the steady leadership expected of a veteran quarterback. Simply put, he must be the leader his team needs if they have any hope of meeting their lofty goals. Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk said it correctly: the Rams cannot allow themselves to get complacent despite the high expectations. Stafford will be tasked with keeping his hungry young team in check and ensuring they don’t get too ahead of themselves. View this post on Instagram The Rams traded for Garrett to win the Super Bowl, and anything less than a Lombardi Trophy will certainly be disappointing. Stafford already owns a ring, but this season isn’t about proving he can win another one. It’s about proving he can lead a different loaded roster back to the promised land, rather than another talented team that falls short.

title: Rams are limiting their time in Australia for Week 1 game
summary: It is being reported that the Los Angeles Rams will arrive in Australia for their pivotal Week 1 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers one day before the contest kicks off. Meanwhile, the 49ers will reportedly spend about a week in The Outback as they prepare to start their season off on the right foot. […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 29: Head coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams shakes hands with head coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers after the San Francisco 49ers defeated the Los Angeles Rams 23-20 at SoFi Stadium on November 29, 2020 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is being reported that the Los Angeles Rams will arrive in Australia for their pivotal Week 1 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers one day before the contest kicks off. Meanwhile, the 49ers will reportedly spend about a week in The Outback as they prepare to start their season off on the right foot. Fans, and media personalities attending the Week 1 international game are likely to end up spending more time in Australia than the Rams do. The Rams will arrive in Australia the day before their Week 1 matchup against the 49ers and depart Melbourne immediately after the game, per @DanGrazianoESPN . San Francisco will arrive a full week earlier so players and coaches can adjust to the time difference. pic.twitter.com/JfuhQ0CVcx — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) August 5, 2026 It’s two different approaches by two very successful franchises. For the Rams, this was perhaps to be expected since last year when they went to London, they limited their time across the pond, and ended up having their best game of the year against the Jacksonville Jaguars as L.A. won by a final score of 35 to 7. The traditional idea is that teams acclimate themselves to whatever area they have to travel to before gameday. The Rams are basically saying we don’t need to acclimate to anything, just give us a football field, and we’ll play. If the Rams win this game against SF, then their travel plans will be studied, if they aren’t being studied already. Keep an eye out for any changes to the Rams plans, but at this point, what they are planning in August is likely what they will do in September, with regard to their travel plans. Now, in terms of gameplans, expect Kyle Shanahan and McVay to dial it up. We’ll have to tune in on gameday to see which team’s travel plans seemingly worked out better, and which unit is ultimately able to find a way to secure the victory.
author: Danny Stone

title: What Bijan Robinson’s extension says about Kyren Williams
summary: The Atlanta Falcons signed running back Bijan Robinson to a record-breaking contract on Tuesday, and the deal emphasizes just how good of a bargain Kyren Williams is to the Los Angeles Rams. According to Spotrac, Williams will be making less than half of the $22,250,000 AAV Robinson is now being paid. In fact, Williams is […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 25: Kyren Williams #23 of the Los Angeles Rams runs with the ball during an NFC Championship NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on January 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons signed running back Bijan Robinson to a record-breaking contract on Tuesday, and the deal emphasizes just how good of a bargain Kyren Williams is to the Los Angeles Rams. According to Spotrac, Williams will be making less than half of the $22,250,000 AAV Robinson is now being paid. In fact, Williams is listed as the 13th highest-paid RB in the league at $11,000,000 AAV. Even rookie Jeremiyah Love is making more before he even touches the ball in the NFL! Is Robinson worth twice as much as Williams? The short answer here is no, but it’s like comparing apples to oranges. Yes, they both play running back, but their skill sets and how their coaches use them in different scenarios differ. If you look at Robinson’s year-over-year numbers from Pro Football Reference, you will see that his past two years have been very similar when running the ball in terms of number of carries and yards gained. The total yards gained, as well as his average per carry last season, will have been slightly skewed by that 93-yard scamper. There is a big change, however, in how he was used as a receiver. A targeted increase of almost 43% and an increase in receiving yards of just under 100%. With new head coach Kevin Stefanski’s offensive background, I doubt very much that his pass targets will drop this year. He’ll be used much like Christian McCaffrey in San Francisco as the workhorse of the offense. Kyren Williams’ numbers tell a different story of their own. Even though there’s a drop in his number of carries due to Blake Corum getting more touches, his total yards are almost the same, while his yards per carry increase from 4.1 to 4.8. Fresher legs throughout the game? Have a look at the Succ%. That’s the rushing success rate per PFR: measures the percentage of run plays that keep an offense on schedule by gaining a specific value of needed yardage based on the down. A rush is successful if it gains at least 40% of the yards needed on 1st down, 60% on 2nd down, and 100% on 3rd or 4th down. In other words, very useful carries. Robinson’s dropped while Kyren’s improved. There were grumblings among some Rams fans when Williams was extended, but I’m not sure why. It’s obvious his production is similar, but he’s lacking the long speed and ‘flash’ that fans crave. The improvement in Williams’ receiving game is terrific, and if it continues, his deal gets better and better. At the risk of jinxing him, his ball security seems like less of an issue as well. Robinson, in a lot of ways, is like McCaffrey. The opposition knows they are getting the ball, and yet they still produce at high levels. Again, I’m not trying to compare the two, simply pointing out that to me, Williams is the better deal.

Aaron Donald looks to establish a media and entertainment footprint (nbcsports) “Via Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports , Donald has hired Jon Rosen of Envisionary to “grow his businesses, brand partnerships, and overall profile in the media and entertainment industries .” Per Glasspiegel, Donald is currently developing a docuseries. It appears that Donald will be re-entering the public eye in a significant way. Donald has signed with Jon Rosen’s management team at Envisionary to grow his businesses, brand partnerships, and overall profile in the media and entertainment industries, Rosen confirmed to FOS.“ Rams will fly into Australia just one day before Week 1 game vs. 49ers (ramswire) “The Rams’ Week 1 game is against the 49ers in the league’s first game in Australia. The Rams are handling the trip differently than the 49ers, flying in the day before the game and flying out right after. It’s similar to what they did for a game last year in London, when they arrived the morning of the game, beat the Jaguars and got right back on a plane to go home. The Rams actually had people from their organization fly from Los Angeles to Melbourne and back, tracking when and how much they felt the effects of the jet lag. They came to the conclusion that the best way to handle it would be to prepare at home, fly as close to the game as possible, let adrenaline carry them through the game and then fly right home and rest up on the back end. Their Week 2 game is on Monday night at home against the Giants .“
author: Danny Stone

title: Segun Olubi’s special teams prowess, speed difficult to knock off roster
summary: It’s easy to overlook Segun Olubi’s addition to the Las Vegas Raiders. The linebacker isn’t as big of a name as his fellow free agent additions like Quay Walker and Nakobe Dean. The former Green Bay Packer and Philadelphia Eagle, respectively, are set to be the faces of the Raider recalibration at the starting linebacker […]
full_text: May 28, 2026; Henderson, NV, USA; Las Vegas Raiders linebacker Segun Olubi (50) during organized team activities at Intermountain Health Performance Center. Mandatory Credit: Candice Ward-Imagn Images | Candice Ward-Imagn Images It’s easy to overlook Segun Olubi’s addition to the Las Vegas Raiders. The linebacker isn’t as big of a name as his fellow free agent additions like Quay Walker and Nakobe Dean. The former Green Bay Packer and Philadelphia Eagle, respectively, are set to be the faces of the Raider recalibration at the starting linebacker spots, after all. Then came the announcements of center Tyler Linderbaum, edge rusher Kwity Paye, and wide receiver Jalen Nailor being as official acquisitions shortly after the NFL’s transaction wire kicked into gear at the start of the new league year on March 11. Five days after the flurry of money deals were made amongst the 32 teams in the league, Las Vegas made official the signing of Olubi. Like his former Indianapolis Colts and current Raiders teammate Paye, the 26-year-old linebacker was brought in for specific reasons. And in the San Diego State product, the Silver & Black land an elite, high-impact special teams ace. “He’s a difference maker-type guy,” Raiders special teams coordinator Joe DeCamillis said of Olubi back in June after one of the team’s minicamp sessions. “He’s blocked punts in the league. He obviously had one against the Raiders last year. He’s a guy that is twitchy, he’s a guy that has already shown what he can do on the field, and he’s brought a lot to the to the group for us already. So, it’s going to be good to coach him. I’m excited we have him.” Olubi’s special teams prowess and speed is going to be hard to knock off the Raiders roster this offseason. By The Numbers Segun Olubi, Linebacker, 5th Year 2025: 17 games (zero starts), 11 total tackles, 1 forced fumble, 1 blocked punt; 362 snaps on special teams, 6 on defense Career: (2022-25) 51 games (2 starts), 50 total tackles, 1 interception, 1 pass deflection, 2 forced fumbles, 2 fumble recoveries, 2 blocked punts; 1,095 snaps on special teams, 141 on defense #RAIDERS ROSTER MOVE: – Signed LB Segun Olubi #RaiderNation | @Raiders pic.twitter.com/gAB6wvL5Ka — Raiders PR (@RAIDERS_PR) March 16, 2026 Luring DeCamillis out of the collegiate ranks — the veteran special teams boss spent the last three seasons in the SEC coaching at Texas and South Carolina — was a task but the connection with the Kubiak family was too strong to turn down. “There’s a lot of similarities between him and his dad, but there’s some differences too,” DeCamillis said of Klint and his father Gary Kubiak “Both are very, very detail-oriented. They love ball, which I think is huge, and he’s done a great job of organizing things since he’s been here, which I knew he would. It’s great to be with him, for sure, and the whole staff. I’ve worked with a few guys that are on the staff also.” That attention to detail meant reconstituting all three phases of the Raiders’ game: Offense, defense, and special teams. Hence signing Olubi and fellow special teams dynamo wide receiver Dareke Young (who Klint Kubiak is all too familiar with during their respective time with the Seattle Seahawks last season). It’s never a bad idea to add elite or upper echelon talent — even on special teams. DeCamillis and his assistant coaches, Marquice Williams and Tim McConnell, are charged with providing the defibrillator to a Las Vegas special teams group that flatlined last season. From blocked kicks ( Daniel Carlson’s game-winning try thwarted by the Chicago Bears in Week 4; AJ Cole III’s two punts in Week 5 and Week 10 , respectively), to awful coverage (Washington Commanders rookie receiver Jaylin Lane torching the team for a 90-yard punt return touchdown in Week 3 , chief among them), and kicking instability (large portion to why Carlson is gone and veteran Matt Gay and undrafted rookie Kansei Matsuzawa are competing for the place kicker gig), the Silver & Black were a case study in breakdowns and blunders. And this is for a special teams group that historically flourished while the rest of the team floundered. In order to do a 180-degree turn, bringing in proven impact players like Olubi is the way to go about it. That Week 5 punt block that ended up hobbling Cole was Olubi. The 6-foot-1 and 233-pound difference maker still exhibits the 4.44 speed he clocked in at San Diego State’s pro day heading into the league in 2022 and brings a tremendous chip on his shoulder, frenetic energy tailor made for special teams work, and all-important work ethic and accountability. Yep, this is the guy the #Raiders just signed. pic.twitter.com/59oEdMlvWw — Levi Edwards (@theleviedwards) March 16, 2026 Look at the block Olubi had of Cole’s punt in the above tweet. That kind of game-altering screaming off the edge impact play has been sorely missing for Las Vegas as takeaways have become a rarity. He paced the Colts with 30 special teams tackles including a highly efficient 2025 campaign where he notched 11 stops on special teams — including a forced fumble — and a blocked punt putting him in select company as only one of a baker’s dozen (13) to achieve the same stat line last season. Don’t expect a drastic role change for Olubi in Silver & Black. He compiled 1,095 special teams snaps during his time in Indianapolis and he’s expected to be a core special teamer in Las Vegas. The linebacker notched 362 special teams snaps in 2025 to just six defensive snaps. And his heaviest workload in both groups occurred in his second season in 2024 where Olubi tallied 334 special teams and 114 defensive snaps. Olubi’s competition in DeCamillis’ department are fellow young linebackers Tommy Eichenberg and Cody Lindenberg. That duo accounted for 371 and 362 snaps on special teams in 2025 and it’s the former that showcased some jarring hitting ability in coverage. But neither of the Bergs bring what Olubi has: Explosiveness and unadulterated speed. Couple that with a resume of impact plays, and it’s difficult to see the Bergs knock off the latest addition off the roster. Although, there’s plenty of special teams work to be had. “Like you said, he’s very energetic, and I think that for special teams at this level, I think that’s very, very critical, because the reality is most people don’t grow up wanting to play left tackle on punt team. They want to be the starting linebacker,” Cole said of DeCamillis’ importance to the special teams room. “Most people don’t grow up saying, ‘Oh, I want to be the wing.’ They want to be the starting running back, but we need those guys to do that job at a high level. And so, when he comes into the room with that energy and that fire and that passion, I think it lights it in a bunch of other people. And so, hopefully, I mean, I’m confident that that will bring the best out of the group.” Olubi certainly matches that energy, fire, and passion. And barring an injury or sudden plummet to ineffectiveness, he’ll not only make the final 53-man roster, but likely be worth more than the one-year, $1.145 million contract he inked with the Raiders.

title: Malik Benson making strong push for role on Las Vegas Raiders’ offense during training camp
summary: It’s no secret that the third wide receiver spot on the Las Vegas Raiders’ depth chart is up for grabs during training camp. While 2025 second-round pick Jack Bech is the logical choice to win the job, Bech had an underwhelming rookie season and is far from a heavy favorite to earn the role on […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - AUGUST 03: Malik Benson #19 of the Las Vegas Raiders practice during the team's training camp at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on August 03, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s no secret that the third wide receiver spot on the Las Vegas Raiders’ depth chart is up for grabs during training camp . While 2025 second-round pick Jack Bech is the logical choice to win the job, Bech had an underwhelming rookie season and is far from a heavy favorite to earn the role on offense. That opens the door for a dark horse to factor into the mix, and 2026 sixth-rounder Malik Benson has turned some heads early in camp. “Another late-round rookie who’s put veterans on notice this camp is Benson,” The Athletic’s Sam Warren wrote on Aug. 3. “The sixth-round draft pick has found good chemistry with No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza so far, earning him more opportunities as camp has gone on.” With plenty of eyes on Mendoza this summer, developing a connection with the future of the franchise will certainly help the Oregon product make a name for himself and climb up the depth chart. But Benson hasn’t just caught the media’s attention; he’s drawn good reviews from the coaching staff and his teammates as well. Head coach Klint Kubiak was asked about the rookie receiver’s performance so far, and, in typical stoic Kubiak fashion, the coach said Benson has had a “good head start” and is “playing good football” while also noting that he still has a lot to prove to the coaching staff (h/t SleeperRaiders on X/Twitter ). The latter is certainly a fair statement. The Raiders only have about a week’s worth of practices under their belts, and the pads just came on at the time of writing. So, the first-year wideout still has plenty of checkpoints to clear before reaching the finish line and winning the race. But he’s out to an early lead and has drawn praise from his potential running mates, veteran wide receivers Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor. “Man, I’m so excited for him because as an older guy coming to the league with the guys that I had in my room, the one thing you want to see is a young guy that wants to get better,” Tucker replied when asked about Benson. “They’re not going through the motions, and Leek (Malik) comes in every single day and wants to get better. And he is getting better every play, every rep, and he can run all day. “That’s something that I tell him that makes you super here in a way because if you can run all day, you can play fast, like there’s a spot for you here. So, I’m excited for him. I have him under my wing just to keep him going because I know what it’s like to be a rookie. I’m very excited for him, and I think he’s going to be a very big part of us this year too.” Nailor shared a similar statement on the sixth-rounder’s performance. “He’s a young kid; he has a ways to go, but he’s asking questions, he’s asking the right questions,” Nailor said. “He wants to be better, he wants to play, he wants to be on this team, he wants to show himself. So, just having that type of mindset as a young rookie, it means a lot. Just to have him asking questions, to me, it shows that he cares. I care as well, so I want to give him all the pointers that I can with whatever he’s asking.” It will be interesting to see what Kubiak and Co. want to do with the wide receiver rotation moving forward. The passing game will likely be run through two-time Pro Bowl tight end Brock Bowers, and Kubiak leaned heavily on 12 personnel as the Seattle Seahawks’ offensive coordinator last year. Also, Tucker, Nailor and Benson have similar skill sets while Bech can bring something different out wide. Of course, the Raiders’ coaching staff doesn’t have to have that figured out right now, as the season opener against the Miami Dolphins is still more than a month away. Additionally, it’s still early in training camp, so there’s time for Benson’s hype train to slow down. But that doesn’t change the fact that the Raiders’ sixth-round pick appears to be ahead of schedule and has a chance to take on a bigger role than previously expected.
