title: Ex-Jets Progress Report: Part 2 (AFC)
summary: With training camp underway, it’s a good time to keep track of where any former Jets are currently playing, so we can start to access how likely they are to have successful seasons elsewhere, or to lose their jobs and potentially become available for a reunion with the Jets. We are covering this over two […]
full_text: Browns linebacker Quincy Williams celebrates after a play during a practice, June 2, 2026, in Berea. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co With training camp underway, it’s a good time to keep track of where any former Jets are currently playing, so we can start to access how likely they are to have successful seasons elsewhere, or to lose their jobs and potentially become available for a reunion with the Jets. We are covering this over two parts, looking at NFC teams last week and AFC teams today. Every AFC team currently has at least one former Jet on it apart from the Denver Broncos. As ever, this list is intended to be exhaustive, but if we missed anyone, let us know in the comments. Bills: The Bills still have running back Ty Johnson under contract after he had been a solid third down back for them in recent years. Also on offense, Buffalo has three ex-Jets receivers but they are all probably long shots to make the team. Mecole Hardman was signed to a futures deal at the end of last season while Mac Dalena and Quentin Skinner were each picked up after the Jets released them recently. On defense, they re-signed defensive tackle Phidarian Mathis to compete for a role and linebacker Jimmy Ciarlo is back after contributing on special teams last year. Dolphins: After a solid 2025 season, Miami opted to keep ex-Jets placekicker Riley Patterson , clearing a path for Jason Sanders to end up with the Jets. They also have former preseason standout Donovan Edwards at running back and offensive tackle Carter Warren is also with the team but he is already on injured reserve. They cut ties with tight end Zack Kuntz, who ended up in Las Vegas. Patriots: New England made a splash by signing guard Alijah Vera-Tucker during the offseason and, if he makes it to the regular season, he could end up starting alongside one of his old teammates in Morgan Moses . The Patriots also retained defensive tackle Leonard Taylor III after he contributed to their postseason success last year. Bengals: Cincinnati has two former Jets quarterbacks batting to be the number two behind Joe Burrow, as they added Josh Johnson and re-signed Joe Flacco . Defensive back Ja’Sir Taylor is also now with the Bengals after being with the Jets for the second half of last season. Browns: Cleveland picked up former Jets linebacker Quincy Williams in free agency and he should start for them. Two other former Jets – tight end Brenden Bates and wide receiver Malachi Corley – will also compete for a roster spot. Ravens: Baltimore’s only ex-Jets player is currently guard John Simpson who is expected to start for them. Steelers: After much deliberation, the Steelers did eventually opt to re-sign quarterback Aaron Rodgers , who will reunite with defensive back Brandin Echols on the main roster. Wide receiver Brandon Smith and linebacker Jamin Davis are also with the team in training camp, but they released offensive lineman Calvin Anderson. Texans: Houston re-signed Sheldon Rankins after he played well for them last season and also added two former Jets to their special teams unit: Punter Kai Kroeger and return specialist Brandon Codrington . Colts: After their blockbuster trade somewhat backfired last season, the Colts will be hoping to see cornerback Sauce Gardner at his best in 2026. Indianapolis also signed defensive lineman Micheal Clemons to a three-year deal worth almost $6 million per season. Another defensive lineman, Derrick Nnadi was also brought in to compete and kicker Spencer Shrader is battling with Blake Grupe for a role. Titans: Robert Saleh is leaning on familiar faces as, by our count, the Titans have an incredible 12 ex-Jets on their roster right now, including six defensive linemen. Not all of these were Jets while Saleh was coaching, though, to be fair. That defensive line includes Jermaine Johnson , John Franklin-Myers and Solomon Thomas . Further depth comes from Jacob Martin , Jalyn Holmes and the most recent signing Khalen Saunders . At safety, Tony Adams previously started for Saleh, so he has a shot at a key role. Cornerback Mario Goodrich is more of a long-shot though. It’s possible none of their four offensive players that are former Jets will make the roster. These include running back Michael Carter , offensive linemen Austin Deculus , wide receiver Lance McCutcheon and quarterback Hendon Hooker . Jaguars: Jacksonville will get some offensive line depth from two former Jets in Chuma Edoga and Trystan Colon . They also added defensive back and special teamer Corey Ballentine . Broncos: As noted, this is the only NFL team without any ex-Jets players currently on it. Chargers: The Chargers re-signed linebacker Del’Shawn Phillips , who continues to be a special teams standout, to a two-year deal. Raiders: The only former Jets player on the Raiders’ roster is tight end Zack Kuntz , who was picked up after Miami let him go. Chiefs: Finally, the Chiefs’ most significant former Jets player is quarterback Justin Fields , who was acquired by trade but doesn’t look likely to get an opportunity with Patrick Mahomes already back on the practice field. Offensive tackle Esa Pole and wide receiver Jason Brownlee return from last year’s team and defensive back Tanner McCalister was a recent addition. We’ll be back after preseason with a look at which players made the final roster, or ended up in new homes…

full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Florham Park, NJ, USA; New York Jets tight end Kenyon Sadiq (16) participates in a drill during training camp at Atlantic Health Jets Training Center. Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jets rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq is going to miss time in training camp per head coach Aaron Glenn. Jets HC Aaron Glenn told reporters that rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq suffered “a little setback” to the offseason hernia surgery he had, and he now will miss some time. But Glenn still is confident that Sadiq will be ready for the regular-season opener. pic.twitter.com/CZKyzH5SD5 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 4, 2026 It’s a positive that Sadiq is likely to be ready by Week 1, but the Jets are surely hoping he won’t be out for long. Training camp reps are arguably more important to Sadiq than any other player on the team. Sadiq is a rookie who is working to master the playbook. He also plays one of the most complex positions to learn in the NFL. He is also a player working to refine his technique. And he needs to develop chemistry with quarterback Geno Smith. Simply put, these practices are built to benefit players like Sadiq far more than your run of the mill NFL veterans. Glenn’s statement has a lot of wiggle room so it is conceivable that Sadiq’s absence will be short lived. That certainly would be a positive for the Jets.

title: Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: Jalen Hurts looked sharp
summary: Today marked the sixth Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Here’s what I observed at the Jefferson Health Training Complex! EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES UP NEXT: The Eagles have a walkthrough closed to media access on Thursday. They’ll return to practice on Friday at 10:00 AM Eastern.
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JULY 30: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during training camp at Jefferson Health Training Complex on July 30, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Today marked the sixth Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Here’s what I observed at the Jefferson Health Training Complex! EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES Today was a lighter day of practice. No pads. 75 minutes long. EAGLES INJURY UPDATES: BGN’s Alexis Chassen wrote up a comprehensive Eagles training camp injury report . The highlights: still no Lane Johnson (excused/not injury related), DeVonta Smith (hamstring), or Makai Lemon. Also, Landon Dickerson (rest/not injury related) sat out of practice for the first time this summer. JALEN HURTS UPDATE: Hurts looked pretty sharp today! QB1 completed all of his attempts in 7-on-7 … save for one dropped pass by E.J. Jenkins that hit the tight end in his hands. Hurts connected with Dallas Goedert over the middle with a ball that was placed just over the flyswatter dummy that’s designed to simulate a leaping defensive lineman. Hurts threw a perfect pass with anticipation into a tight window along the left sideline down the field to Dontayvion Wicks. Unlike earlier in his career, Hurts also doesn’t really take off running in 7-on-7, which is refreshing to see since that’s a useless thing to do in a pure passing drill. In 11-on-11, Hurts ripped a ball to Elijah Moore on a curl for a short gain. Hurts almost had a deep touchdown to Darius Cooper … but the second-year wide receiver couldn’t secure the ball that hit him in the hands as he was going to the ground. Would’ve been a tough grab but Hurts did his part to give Cooper a chance for the score. Stock up. Jalen Hurts singled out Darius Cooper when asked about the Eagles' wide receiver room. pic.twitter.com/Kt1moWHCUs — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) August 5, 2026 Drew Kendall took first-team left guard reps with Dickerson resting. Markell Bell continued to work at first-team right tackle with Lane Johnson not practicing. Jihaad Campbell broke up a pass in front of him meant for Samari Toure. Later, Campbell was flagged for defensive pass interference while covering Tank Bigsby. Speaking of Bigsby, it sure seems like he’s seen a lot of targets. BACKUP QUARTERBACK BATTLE: Tanner McKee was first up as QB2 in 7-on-7 but Andy Dalton took the first 11-on-11 series with the second-team offense. One of McKee’s best passes was a throw over the middle to Stone Smart … who had a really bad drop. Dalton hit a crossing Johnny Wilson (Dalton really likes throwing to him) in stride for a chunk gain. Dalton also hit a crossing Cam Latu in stride. Dalton did overthrow Danny Gray in the end zone to the right side. All told, Dalton has outplayed McKee in camp so far. Of course, still plenty of summer left to go. Arnold Ebiketie beat Fred Johnson to notch a “sack.” I tend to think the Eagles will keep Big Fred on the roster … but I don’t think he’s had a very good summer. I’ve been wondering if he’s a surprise cut candidate but he already has a $1.4 million guaranteed salary this season. The Eagles could trade him to clear $1.3 million in cap space with only $160,000 in dead money. Johnson could be made expendable if Bell proves to earn the coaching staff’s trust and, say, John Ojukwu emerges as a depth tackle option. The Eagles’ second-team offensive line: LT Fred Johnson, LG Jake Majors, C Willie Lampkin, RG Michael Jordan, RT John Ojukwu. It seems like Lampkin is climbing up the depth chart after previously repping on the third-team offensive line. Really interested to see him in preseason action. Grant Calcaterra had a ball bounce off his hands for a drop. Elijah Mitchell caught my eye multiple times today. He looked physical and eager for contact in pass protection against Jeremiah Trotter Jr. Mitchell also had a long run and he caught a pass from McKee in the flat for a good catch-and-run. Dameon Pierce also had a long run. Some good competition going on for RB4. (Or RB3?). Ambry Thomas got shook badly on a play where Quez Watkins made a short catch and juked the cornerback. The Eagles re-signed Brandon Hayes to help fill wide receiver reps due to multiple injuries. Hayes, perhaps shaking off some rust, dropped a pass from Dalton. Cole Payton threw another interception today. The rookie quarterback targeted Samari Toure over the middle but the ball was tipped into the air and caught by Tariq Castro-Fields. I much prefer Payton to be fearless than to look too scared to pull the trigger. That being said, Payton probably has to reign the aggression in a bit as he develops. Payton did connect with a crossing Erik Ezukanma in stride with a throw over the middle. Jeremy Maclin attended today’s practice. The former Eagles wide receiver has been the head coach of Kirkwood High School in Missouri since 2021. UP NEXT: The Eagles have a walkthrough closed to media access on Thursday. They’ll return to practice on Friday at 10:00 AM Eastern.

title: Vic Fangio says you shouldn’t sleep on this Eagles linebacker
summary: The Eagles were back on the practice field Wednesday, and defensive coordinator Vic Fangio spoke to reporters before things got started. He talked about Jordan Davis’ development as a pass rusher, and what he’s seen from some of the depth players, especially at linebacker. Here’s what the DC had to say: On Jordan Davis’ development […]
full_text: The Eagles were back on the practice field Wednesday, and defensive coordinator Vic Fangio spoke to reporters before things got started. He talked about Jordan Davis’ development as a pass rusher, and what he’s seen from some of the depth players, especially at linebacker. Here’s what the DC had to say: On Jordan Davis’ development Fangio was asked about how DT Jordan Davis has developed as a pass rusher, and the DC pointed to Davis’ physical changes. “Well, it first started at the end of the 2024 season. He got in better shape. He’s a much better pass rusher in the 330s than he is what he was, and that to me is the biggest thing.” He went on to explain that Davis needs to be his full 6-foot-6 when it’s to his advantage, but he also needs to bend his knees and be 6-foot-3 at times, which is easier to do when he weighs less and is in better shape. Being able to do move around easier and for a longer duration of time is what really propelled Davis’ game. Individual assessments OLB Arnold Ebiketie “He’s made nice progress here. I think coming in on the offseason, in the six OTAs that we had, it was kind of new to him. He was hesitant, not sure. I think he’s made a lot of progress in that manner, and is having a much better camp. Him, and some of the other guys are taking advantage of the reps their gaining with [Jonathan] Greenard being out for awhile.” DB Michael Carter “Right now, I feel good about him playing nickel, playing safety if need be. Maybe some of the other DBs in that bag, not so yet, but doesn’t mean they won’t get there. We don’t have a lot of new, young players on defense, so most of the guys that are here, have some background with us. So, we should be able to make those decisions a little quicker.” LB Chance Campbell “Don’t sleep on Chance [Campbell], now. You guys when you make your lists out there. We like Chance. Chance — he’s a good football player. Had some injuries earlier in his career that set him back, but since the day we picked him up last year, he’s shown that he’s a football player, and we like him. Interesting, last year, we picked him up the last week of the preseason game — I don’t remember the exact day, but it was just a few days before the game, and he didn’t need that acclimation period.“ LB Jeremiah Trotter “Trot’s had a very good camp. Trot, to me, along the same lines as we talked about with [Andrew] Mukuba — looking better, moving better, playing better. And I just think it’s not so much a conditioning and physical thing, it’s more of a knowing what he’s doing, seeing things quicker, faster, and playing faster. But, he’s had an excellent camp. It’s the best I’ve seen him look since we’ve had him.” Other notables Fangio talked a bit about how it’s difficult to balance getting starters reps while also keeping them healthy. And while they are committed to the development of the young players and new players, they aren’t prioritizing that over what’s best for the team and where the reps need to be. The DC says he hasn’t learned much about the Eagles new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion and his play-calling style yet, noting that even though they’ve gone against each other in practice, there’s no scoreboard and it’s not a real game. “I wouldn’t be worried. And like I told [Sean Mannion], we obviously got the best of yesterday’s practice by a long shot, but that’s the way it’s been the last two years in training camp, the defense has gotten the best of the offense. So, not to be too concerned.” He did say that the new Eagles offensive style gives them some more opportunities to prepare for different teams they see throughout the season — especially as Jalen Hurts does more things under center. Fangio admitted it gives the defense more variety in practice than they’ve had the past few years. The DC talked about how the whole league is playing a lot more nickel, for many reasons, the biggest being the fullback position disappearing from offenses and being replaced by a third wideout or tight end. He noted that the Eagles played a lot of nickel in 2024 because he felt that was the best way to get their best players on the field. But, Fangio has a sense that things are reverting back a little bit, so there’s a chance that there’s more base defense this year by the Eagles and others around the league.

title: Eagles training camp injury updates
summary: It didn’t take long, but we’ve reached the point of Philadelphia Eagles training camp where a successful day is one with no injuries. That wasn’t the case on Tuesday and Wednesday. Perhaps most concerning was Cooper DeJean being sidelined with an arm injury on Tuesday. It wasn’t something that appeared concerning after being looked at […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 01: Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean #33 is shown during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 1st, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It didn’t take long, but we’ve reached the point of Philadelphia Eagles training camp where a successful day is one with no injuries. That wasn’t the case on Tuesday and Wednesday. Perhaps most concerning was Cooper DeJean being sidelined with an arm injury on Tuesday. It wasn’t something that appeared concerning after being looked at by the trainers. Thankfully, he was back on the field Wednesday. Wide receiver/return specialist Britain Covey also left Tuesday’s practice early. He didn’t practice on Wednesday due to a hamstring injury. He’s now the third receiver to deal with a hammy issue — joining both DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon , who missed practice entirely Tuesday and Wednesday. This now looks problematic for the rookie Lemon, who missed the last two weeks of OTAs after pulling a hamstring, and has now missed his third training camp practice in a row for the same thing. Reports suggest the team isn’t concerned about it, but it’s still not ideal for a young player to miss so many valuable reps. Lane Johnson missed Saturday’s practice with an “excused (not injury related)” designation, but it wasn’t announced why he was away. That mystery continued into mid-week, with the Eagles RT still not returning to training camp. Jeff McLane reported that Johnson was expected to return soon. Hopefully, he has the time and space for whatever he’s dealing with — and hopefully he’s able to get back soon, because after his injury last season and having to work with a new OL coach on a new scheme, this time is valuable. Wednesday 8/5 Not practicing: WR Britain Covey (hamstring) G Landon Dickerson (rest/not injury related) OLB Keyshawn James-Newby (ankle) RT Lane Johnson (excused/not injury related) WR Makai Lemon (hamstring) WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) S Cole Wisniewski (hamstring) Limited: G Micah Morris (shoulder) G Jaeden Roberts (calf contusion)

Hayes originally participated in the Eagles’ rookie minicamp on a tryout basis in early May before being signed by the team ahead of their first media-attended OTA practice on May 27. […]
full_text: May 1, 2026; Philadelphia, PA, USA; Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Brandon Hayes (82) runs drills during rookie minicamp at NovaCare Complex. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Philadelphia Eagles are re-signing undrafted rookie free agent wide receiver Brandon Hayes, according to his agency , Quattro Sports Group (hat tip to @DiBonaNFL ). Hayes originally participated in the Eagles’ rookie minicamp on a tryout basis in early May before being signed by the team ahead of their first media-attended OTA practice on May 27. Hayes was then waived on June 6 ahead of the Eagles’ two-day mandatory minicamp to make room on the roster for the Zion Wilson signing. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Makai Lemon (hamstring), and Britain Covey (injury unclear) recently getting banged up, the Eagles found themselves in need of more receiver depth. Signing Hayes gives them an extra practice body in training camp who has some level of familiarity with their system. He will help to fill reps. As of this writing, the Eagles have yet to officially announce this move and any corresponding roster news. Stay tuned for updates.

title: Eagles News: A.J. Epenesa is “happy that I’m not a Brown and that I’m an Eagle”
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … A.J. Epenesa not inclined to discuss “weird situation” with Browns – PFTBefore Eagles defensive end A.J. Epenesa landed in Philadelphia, he had a one-year deal worth up to $5 million in place with the Browns. Until he didn’t. The Browns pulled out of the agreement, […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JULY 30: Philadelphia Eagles defensive end A.J. Epenesa #57 runs a drill during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on July 30th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … A.J. Epenesa not inclined to discuss “weird situation” with Browns – PFT Before Eagles defensive end A.J. Epenesa landed in Philadelphia, he had a one-year deal worth up to $5 million in place with the Browns. Until he didn’t. The Browns pulled out of the agreement, due to concerns regarding his physical. Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Epenesa didn’t want to say much about the Browns. He made it clear that he’s happy to be with the Eagles. “Cleveland, you know, it was a weird situation,” Epenesa told reporters. “But I don’t necessarily want to go back and talk on that in just a weird sense but I’ll just leave that in the past and just be happy that I’m not a Brown and that I’m an Eagle.” Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: Offense out of sync as DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon miss time – BGN WR Makai Lemon (hamstring). Lemon’s injury also isn’t considered serious. But the rookie wide receiver previously missed at least four of the Eagles’ eight spring practices due to a hamstring injury (currently unclear if it’s the same one or a new one). And now he’s missed full team drills in two of their five training camp practices thus far. Doesn’t seem ideal if he’s out for extended period of time. Stock up, stock down after the first week of 2026 Eagles training camp – PhillyVoice STOCK DOWN — WR Makai Lemon: I hate to put rookies on this part of the list after just five practices, but leaving Lemon off of it would be a pretty glaring omission. Lemon missed half of spring practices with a hamstring injury, and he’s on the shelf four practices into camp again with… another hamstring injury. Before he suffered his second hamstring injury, Lemon was quiet during the first three practices. He entered camp as the favorite to be the second-most targeted receiver, but he’s not that anymore. TE Eli Stowers: If we put Lemon on this list, we probably have to put Stowers on it, too, since he has been every bit as quiet. Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee are in a competition for QB2 duties. And they’re trying to embrace it. – Inquirer Sixteen years into his NFL career, Andy Dalton has seen just about everything. But this training camp — his first with the Eagles — is unlike any Dalton has participated in before. Dalton, 38, is competing with incumbent Tanner McKee to back up Jalen Hurts. That isn’t a new phenomenon for Dalton. He hasn’t been a full-time starter since 2019, his ninth and final year with the Cincinnati Bengals, the team that drafted him 35th overall in 2011. What is unfamiliar, however, is that Dalton doesn’t know when it’s his turn to take reps with the second-string offense in team drills. Neither does McKee. Both quarterbacks wait for orders from their coaches before one or the other joins the huddle. At first, Dalton had questions about how they would split reps. Now, he’s accepted the surprise element of their current situation, which is reminiscent of game days for the backup quarterback. “I was joking with Tanner, I was like, ‘This is just real life right here,’” Dalton said Tuesday. “‘You don’t know when you’re going to be going in.’” 2026 Philadelphia Eagles training camp: Latest intel, updates – ESPN It’s important to note that new plays are being installed in the early portion of camp, so it makes sense why the offensive operation can look rough in spots. It’s no coincidence that the offense’s breakout day on Monday was a review of plays that had been installed previously. In other words, patience is required. An incredible full-circle story with Uar Bernard and Arnold Ebiketie – NBCSP Most people in the football world learned about Uar Bernard during the pre-draft process when the Nigerian’s incredible athleticism began to go viral. Not Arnold Ebiketie. The veteran edge rusher has known about Bernard for years and actually coached him at an NFL Africa camp in Kenya back in April of 2023. Three years later, they’re teammates in Philly. “I was actually looking the other day at some of the videos from back three years ago,” Ebiketie said after practice on Tuesday. “It’s fun to see him. He was not that big back then. But it’s fun to see him. He’s developing pretty well. He’s getting accustomed to the system and everything. “Obviously, he’s a freak of nature. The more he can get better and understand the scheme and everything, the better he’s going to be.” All-Access: Day in The Life of Clint Hurtt – PhiladelphiaEagles.com What does it take to teach and motivate NFL players? Senior Defensive Assistant/Defensive Line/Associate Head Coach Clint Hurtt offers a peek inside his world in the latest episode of All-Access, presented by Lincoln Financial. Best NFL team fits for notable remaining free agents: Stefon Diggs to NFC East? – NFL.com Gregg Rosenthal 101 ranking: Unranked. Ertz doesn’t want the final play of his phenomenal career to be tearing his ACL, and he’s set for his 14th NFL season, having been cleared for all football activities, ESPN reported on Aug. 4. Last season, Tommy Tremble and Ja’Tavion Sanders combined for 56 catches in Carolina. Ertz had 50 catches for Washington in 13 games. The last tight end with 50-plus catches in a season for the Panthers is calling games in the booth now — Greg Olsen (2019). Providing Bryce Young with a trusty veteran tight end in a pivotal campaign for the quarterback would be a boon for his confidence and maturation, and likely the same for a very young receiving corps. Other options: Buccaneers, Patriots, Saints. Falcons training camp Day 6 news, standouts, interviews, injuries – The Falcoholic EDGE DeAngelo Malone was placed on reserve/PUP today. In a corresponding move, the team signed DT Marlon Tuipulotu. [BLG Note: You may recall Tuipulotu is a former Eagles draft pick who returned to Philly’s final mandatory minicamp practice on a tryout basis back in the spring.] Cobie Durant is playing like the Cowboys’ best cornerback – Blogging The Boys Calling anyone the best or worst anything right now after a handful of practices is making quite the mountain out of barely a mole hill, but facts are facts to this point. And at this point Durant is flashing more than anybody else and had a particularly strong showing during the group’s first padded practice on Monday. The mothership’s Patrik Walker caught a great video of his interception that really shows how he managed to focus all the way through the play and pick off Dak Prescott. Bill Croskey-Merritt committed to being an asset in Commanders pass game – Hogs Haven Commanders running back Bill Croskey-Merritt wasn’t involved much in the pass game last season. He had just nine catches for 68 yards on 13 targets, stats that show a lack of production, opportunity and (let’s just say it) trust from the coaching staff to use the rookie in those situations. That wasn’t a massive shock, considering Croskey-Merritt didn’t do much receiving in college, either. He had just seven receptions for New Mexico in 2023, his last full collegiate season after odd eligibility issues essentially nullified his 2024 campaign at Arizona. The Commanders pushed him to improve as a receiver and a pass protector in 2026, and are testing him in those areas during training camp. QB tiers: NY Giants’ Jaxson Dart ranked No. 24 by coaches, executives – Big Blue View The New York Giants are at something of crossroads in 2026. They’re hoping that the combination of quarterback Jaxson Dart and head coach John Harbaugh can lift the team back to competitiveness. The rest of the NFL seems to be taking a “wait and see” approach, particularly with respect to Dart. The Athletic released itsannual Quarterback Tiers list on Tuesday, ranking the…

title: Nick Sirianni has been impressed with new Eagles assistant coaches
summary: The Eagles are nearly a week into training camp, and head coach Nick Sirianni gave some updates about how OC Sean Mannion is leading the offense, how new OL coach Chris Kuper is acclimating, and about rookies Makai Lemon and Eli Stowers. Here’s what the head coach had to say: On Sean Mannion’s leadership Sirianni […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 01: Philadelphia Eagles offensive line coach Chris Kuper speaks with Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 1st, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Eagles are nearly a week into training camp, and head coach Nick Sirianni gave some updates about how OC Sean Mannion is leading the offense, how new OL coach Chris Kuper is acclimating, and about rookies Makai Lemon and Eli Stowers. Here’s what the head coach had to say: On Sean Mannion’s leadership Sirianni said that despite many of the changes to the coaching staff, meetings are still structured the same way. When asked if new run-game coordinator Ryan Mahaffey was leading the run-game portion of meetings, Sirianni revealed that OC Sean Mannion has actually lead most of the meetings up to this point. “What Sean [Mannion] just shows, is a very good overall view of the offense. When he comes up here, he has everybody’s attention and is able to talk to every position. I’ve been very impressed by that — obviously, one of the reasons we hired him as far as just his expertise. And, I think the guys have been really impressed by that.” The head coach went on to explain that it makes sense as they’re learning a newer system that Mannion is the vocal one in meetings, and then the group splits up and hears from their position coaches. Sirianni complimented his new OC with how he’s done speaking to the group, keeping everyone on the same page, and showing his expertise at every position. On training camp success Sirianni was asked what a successful training camp looked like to him, and he explained that it’s about looking at each particular day individually, because there’s going to be back and forth between the offense and defense, and different position groups. “When we come in here and we watch as a team, are we getting better at the little things? Are we getting better at our fundamentals? Are we taking steps? Are we taking steps with our things that require no talent, our ball security? When I say require no talent, just everybody being on the same page at all times. You’re looking for little progressions each and every day. It’s a marathon. Some days, it’s going to look like this, and some days, it’s going to look like this. It’s never just a true line. “ He admitted that as coaches, they’d all like it to be so simple, but progression ebbs and flows, and they’re ultimately just trying to get a little better each day. On new OL coach Chris Kuper “I hired him for a reason. We were really impressed by him, and we know he’s a phenomenal coach, and he’s doing a good job of building relationships with his players. He’s doing a good job of teaching his players. Obviously, I talk to guys all the time, and I know those guys think very highly of him and have been really impressed early on here in camp and through the OTAs. Building trust is the most important thing. You build trust by your daily habits, you build trust by consistently doing the right things. Those are the things that he’s been doing.” On rookie performances Sirianni said that it’s all about getting better everyday for rookies like Makai Lemon and Eli Stowers, but he really likes the skillset they have and how it will continue to develop. Specifically, the head coach said he loves the way Lemon goes about his business, and that the WR’s effort in the run game is awesome. He also pointed out Lemon’s quickness, which maybe isn’t on display with every catch, but is all over the film. Sirianni also spoke about Stowers and how his athletic ability with help him in third-down situations. “I think Eli has a really good feel for the zone, of where to sit in zones, and how to get open versus different types of zone coverage. We know that his athletic ability will [help him] shake free on third down when it is man coverage because he’s quick, he’s fast, he’s explosive. But what I’ve been impressed with him is just his ability to kind of read defenses and find the areas of the zone where he needs to sit and be at the right spot at the right time.” Other notables When asked about Landon Dickerson revealing he returned from injury too soon last season , Sirianni said that their organizational approach is to put player safety at the forefront. He explained that they work closely with the medical staff and are always thinking about the long-term health of the players. Sirianni addressed more pass plays to the running backs in the early days of training camp, saying that it all just depends on the style of offense they’re running at any particular time, and they’re always looking to utilize the skillset of their players. They don’t want to stop a guy like Saquon Barkley from running the ball, and they know the RBs have the ability to affect the game in other ways, too. The head coach explained his approach to getting QB4 Cole Payton reps during camp, and said that his job is to provide enough reps throughout practice to allow guys to develop. He noted that it can be especially easy in training camp to get locked into reps for the ones and twos, but Sirianni said the team has done a good job finding ways to work the developmental guys.

summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have officially released their first depth chart of training camp, just over a week ahead of their preseason opener against the Green Bay Packers. full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 19: A closeup view of a Pittsburgh Steelers helmet prior to a game against the Cleveland Browns at Cleveland Browns Stadium on November 19, 2023 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have officially released their first depth chart of training camp, just over a week ahead of their preseason opener against the Green Bay Packers. Offensively, it’s a lot of chalk. All eyes have been on the battle for the backup quarterback spot. As it currently stands, Mason Rudolph is listed in the QB2 spot, with Will Howard at QB3 and Drew Allar at QB4. The offensive line is as expected, with the lineup from left to right being Troy Fautanu, Mason McCormick, Zach Frazier, Spencer Anderson, and Dylan Cook. Broderick Jones is listed as the backup left tackle with Max Iheanachor as the backup right tackle. Roman Wilson is the starting slot receiver alongside DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman as the other two starters, Germie Bernard is listed behind Pittman. Defensively, there were some actual surprises. Yahya Black is listed as the team’s starting nose tackle, with veteran Sebastian Joseph-Day as the No. 2. Linebacker Carson Bruener is in the top four of the linebacker rotation, with Malik Harrison coming in fifth on the depth chart. Considering his price tag, that could hint at his future with the Steelers being short. The full depth chart can be seen at Steelers.com . Let us know what you think in the comments . Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In just over one month’s time, the Pittsburgh Steelers will begin their regular season when they host the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium. This marks the second time in three years that Pittsburgh and Atlanta will face one another in Week 1, with the Steelers winning in 2024 by the score of 18-16. Chris Boswell’s first of two six-field-goal games helped the Justin Fields-led Steelers defeat Kirk Cousins and the Falcons. Two years later, both teams have different signal-callers. Aaron Rodgers has returned for a second season in Pittsburgh, while the Falcons will choose between Michael Penix and former Miami Dolphins quarterback Tua Tagovaila to be their Week 1 starter. According to Ian Rapoport, though, that decision appears all but made. “My general feel is that Tua will be the starter for Week 1,” Rapoport said on The Pat McAfee Show . “Penix has not been cleared. They’re having a quarterback battle, but [Tua starting] is what it feels like to me.” The Steelers faced Tagovailoa in Week 15 of the 2025 season, hosting the Dolphins on Monday Night Football . The Steelers won 28-15 and held Tagovailoa to a QBR of 12.2. Pittsburgh and Atlanta will face-off on Fox. The last time the two teams played one another in Week 1 on Fox in Pittsburgh, Rashard Mendehnall scored on a 50-yard touchdown in overtime to give the Steelers a 15-9 win. Over a nice and tight five minutes, we discussed how well the defense performed, the Sam Darnold-Rashid Shaheed connection, an interesting name to watch at safety, Nehemiah Pritchett’s increased role with the starters, Rylie Mills’ versatility, and the work in progress that is a rebuilding running game. full_text: The Seattle Seahawks announced a pair of signings on Wednesday afternoon, adding running back T.J. Harden and cornerback Jordan Washington, who both went undrafted earlier this year. They are already at Wednesday’s practice. In a corresponding move, cornerback Brandon Johnson and edge rusher Garrett Nelson were waived. Johnson had been with the team since mid-July, and Nelson signed on Tuesday. Across four years at UCLA, Harden totaled 1,658 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns, before transferring to SMU for his senior season. He continued to impress with the Mustangs, leading the team with 787 rushing yards, accompanied by 12 touchdowns. While it wasn’t enough to be drafted, he signed with the Cleveland Browns in May, before being waived on August 3. Washington, a familiar face, spent rookie camp with Seattle after going undrafted out of Stanford. Prior to transferring before his senior season, Washington played four seasons at Dartmouth where he recorded 72 tackles, 6.5 tackles for loss and 20 passes defended.

title: Sam Darnold continues remarkable ascent in The Athletic’s NFL QB Tiers survey
summary: Where does the Seattle Seahawks’ Super Bowl champion quarterback fit in the NFL’s landscape? A lot higher than he used to be. The Athletic’s Mike Sando compiles an annual survey of 50 coaches and executives to rank the starting quarterbacks (plus would-be young starters and lingering veterans who are borderline starters/backups) by tiers. A Tier […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 25: Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks celebrates after defeating the Los Angeles Rams an NFC Championship NFL football game at Lumen Field on January 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Where does the Seattle Seahawks’ Super Bowl champion quarterback fit in the NFL’s landscape? A lot higher than he used to be. The Athletic’s Mike Sando compiles an annual survey of 50 coaches and executives to rank the starting quarterbacks (plus would-be young starters and lingering veterans who are borderline starters/backups) by tiers. A Tier 1 quarterback is the best of the best, whereas a Tier 5 quarterback is is anywhere from an unknown to not a viable starter. The tier numbers (1, 2, 3, 4, and 5) are then averaged out and QBs are ranked accordingly by their average tier ranking, not where the evaluators would rank a QB as far as top five, top ten, etc. Sam Darnold has had to take the difficult road to work his way up the rankings. From purgatory with the New York Jets to the Lombardi Trophy with Seattle, Darnold has moved up a tier for a third consecutive year. His aggregate ranking is 14th, tied with Baker Mayfield. Check out some of the quotes: Darnold’s climb over the past three seasons is rare for an established starter in the 13-year history of QB Tiers. “Sam played his ass off the last two years,” a head coach said. Darnold’s improvement from 4.00 to 2.36 is a full tier better than runner-up Daniel Jones among the 19 quarterbacks who appeared in all three surveys and had debuted before 2024. […] “There are so many factors that determine a quarterback’s success, and Darnold’s the best example of it,” an exec said. “To get him into the right system, with the right coaches, and you have a game-breaking receiver, and a good defense. It’s a lot easier.” […] “Sam is at his best when you run the ball, play defense and then he’s not in position to turn the ball over,” an exec said, “but when his number is called, he can make big plays. If they don’t start running the football, they probably don’t win the Super Bowl.” For more context, a Tier 2 quarterback, “carries his team sometimes,” “handles pure-passing situations in doses or has other dimensions that elevate him above Tier 3,” and “has a hole or two in his game.” The Tier 2 range starts with Lamar Jackson at No. 5 and cuts off at Jalen Hurts at No. 17. The Tier 3 “Legit starter but needs better running game or defense to win” quarterback starts with Bo Nix and ends with the 2026 version of Kirk Cousins. The only Tier 1 QBs are Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen, Matthew Stafford, and Joe Burrow. The one sort of critical remark re Darnold is not completely unfounded. Sando noted that Darnold has had the best support from his defense and special teams over the past two seasons, which means he’s been in one of the more optimal environments for a quarterback to succeed. The good news? He’s succeeding instead of dragging a talented team down. In many respects, this is not too dissimilar from Russell Wilson getting to benefit from an elite defense and special teams unit at the start of his career. It’s almost as if being good to great in all of the most important areas of football is extremely valuable, and putting everything on the QB’s plate is not optimal! I have no issue with Darnold’s tier ranking even if I’d separate the tie and put Darnold above Mayfield (who somehow got a Tier 1 vote). I’d also rank him above No. 11 Caleb Williams, who’s being over-stated in my opinion and we should probably wait a little bit to see if he can build on 2025 by not having to rely on so many improbable fourth quarter comebacks. Brock Purdy is still in Tier 2, which is totally fine when you consider he was an MVP finalist in 2023 and played well under difficult circumstances in 2025. Every Tier 1 or Tier 2 QB except Justin Herbert has at least won a playoff start, while 12 out of 17 have made a Conference Championship, and eight have reached a Super Bowl. These are the two tiers you want your QB to be in, otherwise you have functionally no shot at a championship run. Seattle is fortunate to have another Tier 1-2 quarterback to build around, and even if you think Darnold should individually be ranked higher within that specific tier, that he keeps improving his ranking is a sign of respect and acknowledgement of improvement from the league’s evaluators. In case you’re wondering, former Seahawks starter Geno Smith has plunged all the day down to Tier 4 (“Veteran who ideally would not be a full-season starter”) at No.30. While he’s likely nothing more than a camp body, that nugget is important as it would allow De’Zhaun Stribling, or maybe Deebo Samuel, or whichever player they want to focus on getting more slot reps. It’s going to be a critical couple of weeks for players like Jacob Cowing and Junior Bergen. Both are fighting for that final roster spot at wideout. It also helps, in Cowing’s case, that he has the upper hand at punt returner — for now, at least.” 49ers’ Dre Greenlaw opens up on lost season with Broncos: ‘Fighting demons left and right’ (paywall) “I don’t blame anything on the Broncos,” he said. “Coming off the Achilles and the calf (injuries), I just wasn’t in the shape that I needed to be to go out there with them and give it all I got. I should have taken it slow. (But) naturally, they’d just paid me, so that’s all I wanted to do — go show them what I could do. And it bit me in the ass, the second day I got there.” Similarly, Greenlaw owns his failure to master Joseph’s scheme. “I know what I could have done better, as far as being in that film,” he said. “That’s where I feel like I let myself and everybody down.” …“Dre, he grew up different, and I always felt like he thrived in San Francisco because he had the right group of people who he trusted,” Al-Shaair said. “When you’re used to doing things the same way for so long, and you’ve been exposed to that gold standard, it’s tough to break that — even if you go to a building where people are good at what they do.” 49ers interim head coach Chris Foerster shares Week 3 training camp updates “It seems like we’re very healthy. I mean, we have injuries. We have dings and bumps and bruises, and guys are missing practices. It’s yet to come up in anything I’ve heard. Doesn’t mean it hasn’t been discussed, but, shoot, I think it will be plenty. If you’re two deep at every position, you can practice. You can always adjust with the threes, one, two, threes. Threes are hard to stay healthy through the course of training camp, if you’re practicing football hard. If you’re not practicing football hard, you can get through camp easily without injuries, a couple muscles here and there. But if you’re practicing hitting, contact, style of football, whatever it is. So, yeah, that’s not come up at this point.” 49ers signing Ogbo Okoronkwo to bolster pass rush depth “Okoronkwo’s 2025 campaign was cut short after he suffered a season-ending triceps tear in Week 4. His last full season came in 2024 with the Browns, when he totaled 23 tackles, five tackles for loss, three sacks, and one forced fumble. Over two seasons in Cleveland, he recorded 7.5 sacks. His most productive season came in 2022 with the Texans, when he posted career highs with 44 tackles and five sacks. Across 81 career games (13 starts), Okoronkwo has compiled 132 tackles, 17 sacks, four forced fumbles, one fumble recovery, and four passes defensed.” The Good and Not So Good from Day 7 of 49ers Camp: Bosa and Greenlaw Miss a Day “By far the most physically gifted quarterback on the roster even though he’s the smallest quarterback on the roster. He’s just so quick and difficult to contain in the pocket, which is important for the 49ers, because they don’t provide much of a pocket. And when it’s time to throw, Purdy is making outstanding decisions with the ball. He hasn’t forced a pass into coverage in more than a week. Unfortunately for him, his best receiver remains his running back, and his best wide receiver currently is Jordan Watkins….Now that Mike Evans, Ricky Pearsall and Jacob Cowing are injured, the 49ers’ top-three healthy wide receivers on the depth chart are Demarcus Robinson, Deebo Samuel and Jordan Watkins. And today, the best of those three clearly was Watkins, who caught a deep touchdown pass from Purdy during 11-on-11s. Of these three healthy wide receivers, Watkins is the youngest, the fastest, the quickest, and the best route runner. He can beat you with a quick slant or a post over the top. The only area of the field where he struggles is over the middle, because he’s not particularly big. Still, he’s improving.” ESPN proposes 49ers trade for All-Pro safety Jessie Bates “They would risk losing Bates without getting a compensatory pick in return if he walks in free agency,” Walder added. “So it’s better for Atlanta to deal him now….San Francisco would be giving up real draft capital for a short-term player, but that’s an indicator of Bates’ skill and the fact that his contract would cost the 49ers only $13 million in 2026 — a below-market price to sign a player of his caliber,” Walder wrote.” Early 49ers training camp trends: CB, LB groups look fierce; DE already an issue (paywall) “ Thanks to newcomers Jack Jones, Nate Hobbs and rookie Ephesians Prysock, it’s a deep group. And it’s a group that’s being allowed to play to its feisty strength. The biggest critique of San Francisco’s defense in recent years is that it’s been too static and predictable. Robert Saleh, who implemented the system in 2017, preferred to keep things simple because he wanted his players to be fast and aggressive. ….A more aggressive style of cornerback play has been apparent in the first few practices. It’s a style that seems to fit starters Deommodore Lenoir, Renardo Green and Upton Stout, all of whom see themselves as “dogs” on defense. (Well, Lenoir sees himself as a hyena, which is doglike.)”

title: 49ers’ Chris Foerster: ‘If you’re not practicing football hard, you can get through camp easily without injuries’
summary: Chris Foerster and the coaching staff have been tasked with managing the injuries for the San Francisco 49ers. Four players were added to the injury list ahead of Wednesday’s practice. If you include the players on the Injured Reserve, the Niners were without 23 players. That’s enough to field an offense and a defense. The […]
full_text: San Francisco 49ers acting head coach Chris Foerster during a news conference at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara on Sunday, July 26, 2026. Foerster is the assistant head coach and offensive line coach stepping in as acting head coach as Kyle Shanahan recovers from a car crash. (Photo by Santiago Mejia/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images) Chris Foerster and the coaching staff have been tasked with managing the injuries for the San Francisco 49ers. Four players were added to the injury list ahead of Wednesday’s practice. If you include the players on the Injured Reserve, the Niners were without 23 players. That’s enough to field an offense and a defense. The plan was to give Robert Jones and Carver Willis some work at left guard with the starters, while Connor Colby would play right guard. Unfortunately for Willis, he’s in the concussion protocol. Add in Brett Toth, and that meant Foerster didn’t have enough bodies to play musical chairs with the interior line on Wednesday. Foerster said, “I had a lot more in store,” but ultimately only ended up using Jones at left guard. Foerster was asked if the 49ers would need to cancel their joint practice next week. He said, “It’s yet to come up in anything I’ve heard. Doesn’t mean it hasn’t been discussed, but shoot, I think we’ll have plenty of players.” He understands that physicality is necessary to get your team ready for the regular season: “If you’re not practicing football hard, you can get through camp easily without injuries, a couple of muscles here and there. But if you’re practicing hitting, contact, style of football, whatever it is — so yeah, that’s not come up at this point.” Foerster made it sound like the team is taking caution with some of the injuries, as they should. For example, Trent Williams, who isn’t injured, is on a rep count. Foerster had a phenomenal quote that applies to every player: “You always have to be careful that reps in July don’t take away from reps in January.” Foerster continued, “It seems like we’re very healthy. I mean, we have injuries. We have dings and bumps and bruises, and guys are missing practices. If you have two deep at every position, you can practice. You can always adjust with the threes. One, two, threes. Threes are hard to stay healthy through the course of training camp if you’re practicing football hard.” The 49ers have adjusted their practice schedule to avoid injuries. The league even mandated specific days off so teams aren’t practicing consecutive days in a row. Yet, despite the 49ers not having double-digit practices yet, nearly a quarter of their team has “dings and bumps and bruises.”
author: Kyle Posey

title: Deebo Samuel on 49ers return: ‘It was a matter of time’
summary: The San Francisco 49ers have done their best at reuniting with past players before Week 1 of the 2026 season. LB Dre Greenlaw is back after one season with the Denver Broncos, and WR Deebo Samuel is back following his lone season in Washington. Greenlaw’s return is exciting as he will pair again with Fred […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 30: Deebo Samuel Sr. #1 of the San Francisco 49ers warms up before the game against the Detroit Lions at Levi's Stadium on December 30, 2024 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers have done their best at reuniting with past players before Week 1 of the 2026 season. LB Dre Greenlaw is back after one season with the Denver Broncos, and WR Deebo Samuel is back following his lone season in Washington. Greenlaw’s return is exciting as he will pair again with Fred Warner, but Samuel’s return is out of pure necessity and is a pivot from the 49ers’ original plan for the offense. Ricky Pearsall is done for the season. Mike Evans and D’Zhaun Stribling are dealing with injuries, and Christian Kirk is sidelined with a calf injury. Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing are nothing more than question marks, leaving Demarcus Robinson as a virtual lock to make the roster as a veteran presence. The team was forced to add KhaDarel Hodge to the room as insurance to run one-on-ones in training camp. Samuel’s contract details are a signal for his usage. The 49ers are looking for 800 total yards, while using Samuel in a myriad of positions on the field. Running back, wide receiver, decoy, and kick returner are some of his tasks in 2026. 49ers GM John Lynch outlined the plans for Samuel on special teams. “The dynamic kickoff has brought the kickoff return back to the game,” Lynch said. “You’ve got to be really well positioned. … He’s committed to kind of doing that. … We look forward to using him there. But then offensively, you guys have seen him, and I think Kyle has a great vision in being real creative in how we use him.” Samuel has stepped back in the building and hasn’t missed a beat. The wide receiver spoke to ESPN’s Nick Wagoner about his return and how the one-year deal came together. “It kind of felt like I didn’t even go nowhere, to be honest,” Samuel said, via ESPN . “When I got back, I was just like, ‘Well, I know what’s going on. I know the people here. Staff still the same.’ So it’s kind of like the same for real.” “Conversations with me, John and Kyle have just always kind of been the same,” Samuel said. “It was just a matter of time before it happened.” Samuel spoke about leaving for Washington via trade and reiterated there was zero animosity towards Lynch and 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan. It sounds like even without the injuries to the 49ers receiver room, the team was interested in bringing back the wide back.
author: Jason Aponte

Hip flexors are tricky, and it’s generally an injury that keeps a player out for a couple of weeks if it’s a mild strain. Wide receivers Mike Evans, De’Zhaun Stribling, and Christian Kirk are still not practicing. That leaves the door open for one of the young receivers to step in and make a name for themselves. The second-team offense has been a struggle — mainly because it’s really the 3s and 4s with all of the injuries. They take a hit with Toth and Willis sidelined. title: KhaDarel Hodge, another former Raheem Morris player, joins the 49ers
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are signing KhaDarel Hodge, an undrafted free agent from the 2018 class. Hodge is another former Raheem Morris player. He spent the previous four seasons with the Atlanta Falcons. Hodge, 6’2″, 210 pounds, only registered three receptions in 2025 and seven in 2024. He had 14 catches in 2023 for 232 […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - NOVEMBER 16: Khadarel Hodge #4 of the Atlanta Falcons stands on the field during the NFL 2025 game between Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are signing KhaDarel Hodge, an undrafted free agent from the 2018 class. Hodge is another former Raheem Morris player. He spent the previous four seasons with the Atlanta Falcons. Hodge, 6’2″, 210 pounds, only registered three receptions in 2025 and seven in 2024. He had 14 catches in 2023 for 232 yards, and 13 for 202 in 2022. Dodge lined up primarily on the outside with the Falcons. While he’s likely nothing more than a camp body, that nugget is important as it would allow De’Zhaun Stribling, or maybe Deebo Samuel, or whichever player they want to focus on getting more slot reps. It’s going to be a critical couple of weeks for players like Jacob Cowing and Junior Bergen. Both are fighting for that final roster spot at wideout. They’ll need to show they can win inside and outside. It shouldn’t be ruled out that if both excel, Christian Kirk might be the odd man out, even if it’s because of an injury. It also helps, in Cowing’s case, that he has the upper hand at punt returner — for now, at least. Demarcus Robinson has been one of the biggest beneficiaries of the injuries at wide receiver. He went from “will he even make the roster” to potentially playing starter-level snaps. Funny how things change in a week. We’ll see if Hodge turns into anything more than relief during practice for the six or so receivers slated to make the roster.
author: Kyle Posey

title: Ogbo Okoronkwo reunites with Raheem Morris; signs with the 49ers
summary: The San Francisco 49ers worked out Ogbo Okoronkwo this past Sunday. On Wednesday morning, the team officially reunited Okoronkwo with Raheem Morris. The former fifth-round pick out of the 2018 NFL Draft has played with some of the best defensive coordinators in the NFL, including Morris, DeMeco Ryans, Jim Schwartz, and Vic Fangio. Okoronkwo, 31, […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JULY 31: Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Joshua Uche (13) participates in a drill with linebacker Ogbo Okoronkwo (50) during training camp on July 31, 2025 at the Novacare Complex in Philadelphia, PA (Photo by John Jones/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers worked out Ogbo Okoronkwo this past Sunday. On Wednesday morning, the team officially reunited Okoronkwo with Raheem Morris. The former fifth-round pick out of the 2018 NFL Draft has played with some of the best defensive coordinators in the NFL, including Morris, DeMeco Ryans, Jim Schwartz, and Vic Fangio. Okoronkwo, 31, has been a backup for most of his career. He played sparingly under Morris in the one year they spent together with the Rams. Okoronkwo actually played more in Los Angeles once Morris left. From the 2022 to 2024 seasons, he played around 400 snaps per season. To date, Okoronkwo’s best year came with the Texans in 2022, where he generated a 18.5% pressure rate, had 33 stops, and 5 sacks. The 49ers are in need of edge rush help after losing a potential depth piece in Mikail Kamara to a torn ACL , Keion White with an adductor injury , and Cameron Sample to a knee injury. Mykel Williams remains on the active/PUP List, while Nick Bosa continues to work his way up to participating in 11-on-11 drills. The injuries had mounted to a point where rookie Jaden Dugger was working with the pass rushers . Dugger might continue to cross-train there, but Okoronkwo at least gives that room a veteran who knows what is being asked of Morris’s scheme.

title: Breaking down the incentives in 49ers’ WR Deebo Samuel’s contract
summary: Spotrac has an in-depth breakdown of Deebo Samuel’s contract and every incentive the San Francisco 49ers gave him. The details are important as it’s the team’s way of telling us what to expect from Deebo. Samuel received $3.76 million guaranteed. He only received a $490,000 signing bonus. That’s a far cry from the $58 million […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 04: Deebo Samuel #1 of the Washington Commanders walks through the tunnel prior to the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on January 04, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images Spotrac has an in-depth breakdown of Deebo Samuel’s contract and every incentive the San Francisco 49ers gave him. The details are important as it’s the team’s way of telling us what to expect from Deebo. Samuel received $3.76 million guaranteed. He only received a $490,000 signing bonus. That’s a far cry from the $58 million in guarantees that had roughly $16 million in total bonuses in the previous contract extension Deebo signed in 2022. Deebo Samuel’s incentives in 2026 Samuel will receive a $20,000 per game active bonus. That’s filed under “Likely to be earned.” So that’s an extra $340,000 in Deebo’s pocket if he’s active for all 17 regular season games. Samuel also has a Pro Bowl incentive. If he makes it, he’ll earn $100,000. There’s a “scrimmage yard incentive” for Deebo as well. If he has 600 yards from scrimmage, he’ll earn $200,000. If he reaches 803 scrimmage yards, Deebo would earn $450,000. There’s an important qualifier here, as these values double if the 49ers make the playoffs. That goes for the other incentives we’ll touch on, too. There’s a total touchdown incentive for Samuel. If he scores five times, he earns $200,000. If he scores seven touchdowns, Samuel will earn $450,000. We just talked about whether Deebo would return kicks . If he finishes in the top 10, on average, he’ll earn $250,000. Finally, there’s a playing time incentive. Samuel needs to play 68% of the offensive snaps this upcoming season to earn $250,000. Again, all of these values double if the 49ers make the playoffs. Deebo’s cap number in 2026 will be $4.73 million.
author: Kyle Posey

title: 49ers News: Opening the injury report today with my hands over my eyes
summary: How a friendly 49ers competition produced training camp’s most pleasant surprise so far (paywall)“Jack and I have had a lot of conversations,” Green said. “He’s a real savvy football player, and Jack has real good ball skills. He has a very aggressive playing style when it comes to playing the ball, and I try and […]
full_text: A Silicon Valley Power substation in Santa Clara, California, US, on Monday, Nov. 3, 2025. Two of the world's biggest data center developers have projects in Nvidia Corp.'s hometown that may sit empty for years because the local utility isn't ready to supply electricity. Photographer: Jason Henry/Bloomberg via Getty Images | Bloomberg via Getty Images How a friendly 49ers competition produced training camp’s most pleasant surprise so far (paywall) “Jack and I have had a lot of conversations,” Green said. “He’s a real savvy football player, and Jack has real good ball skills. He has a very aggressive playing style when it comes to playing the ball, and I try and pick that up. “You should try to learn from who you can because we’re all in this together, basically.” …“He’s a great corner,” Jones said of Green. “I think he has the potential to be one of the true lockdown corners in the league, you know what I’m saying? As far as from me to him, I’ve just been trying to really tell him to go get that ball. Focus on the ball and not just PBUs. “That’s what I am preaching. … We’re all making each other better. A guy makes a play, and that gives you an energy boost.” Raheem Morris has been a big part of that, and Green is really enjoying his third defensive coordinator in three years. You get the sense that the 2024 second-round pick is not just saying that because it’s what people want to hear. “It’s easier to play faster, and I feel like he’s more detailed with just, like, realistic things, and there’s a lot less thinking,” Green said. “I’ve been able to get attached to guys and contest catches, make plays. That’s what he wants, and that fits us.” …“People don’t just wake up with that ability to go get the ball,” Jones said. “It comes with film study, it comes with practice and repetition. Sometimes you got to take a million reps just to get it right one time. “I played receiver too growing up. But I didn’t want to get thrown the ball. I wanted to go take it.” Source: Details of Deebo Samuel’s 49ers contract tied to usage, playoffs “Samuel will receive a $200,000 bonus if his combined rushing and receiving yards are 600 to 802 on the season. He will receive $450,000 if he achieves 803 scrimmage yards or more. He will earn double those amounts if the 49ers make the playoffs. Samuel will make an additional $200,000 if he scores five or six touchdowns in the regular season. If he scores seven or more touchdowns, he’ll receive a $450,000 incentive. Again, those figures will be doubled if the 49ers make the playoffs. Samuel will receive a $250,000 bonus for the season if he ranks 10th or better in average yards per kick return (minimum 20 returns). He’ll receive another $250,000 if he meets that incentive and the 49ers make the postseason. Samuel also is scheduled to make $250,000 if he plays 68 percent or more of the 49ers’ offensive snaps.” How 49ers’ offense, defense can benefit from Raheem Morris’ schematic changes “The 49ers’ changes on defense include expanded usage of five defensive linemen and a simplified set of coverage assignments designed to enable the cornerbacks and safeties to play fast without being required to make too many split-second adjustments.” Kawakami: ‘We know who we are’ — Brock Purdy on QB play and the 49ers’ 2026 vision (paywall) “The most visible proof came toward the end of last season, after Purdy came back from his injury and looked in complete command of every part of the Shanahan offense. Purdy “canned” plays — Shanahan terminology for switching to an alternate call — swiftly and with confidence and just seemed to run things like he knew most of the answers before the questions were asked.” 49ers’ Eddy Piñeiro gets kick out of finally finding job security in NFL (paywall) “That’s why I think it’s so hard for rookies when they come in,” said Piñeiro, who finally found some stability with the Panthers from 2022-24. “It’s just such a short leash they have with kickers. You miss kicks, you’re gone. It’s just part of the process, and I wish I would have known that faster in my career. I’m like, ‘Oh, I miss one, I’m gonna be OK.’ No, you’re not gonna be OK.” 49ers training camp Week 3: Full practice schedule, media availability, and key dates “ Wednesday, August 5 10:15 a.m. – Practice Following practice – Chris Foerster press conference Following Foerster – Player availability Thursday, August 6 10:15 a.m. – Practice Following practice – Raheem Morris press conference Following Morris – Player availability Friday, August 7 Walk-through – No media availability Saturday, August 8 9:15 a.m. – Klay Kubiak press conference 10:15 a.m. – Practice Following practice – Player availability” 49ers rookie De’Zhaun Stribling reveals what he’s learning from Mike Evans, veteran teammates “We kind of weren’t even ready for the whole thing,” Stribling admitted during a conversation with Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area. “Everyone was still parking cars and trying to get set up. And got the call from a San Jose area code.” 49ers rookie Jaden Dugger… the pass rusher? “Dugger went from practicing with the off-ball linebackers to doing the same individual drills as Osa Odighizuwa in a matter of a week. Dugger may need to beef up. He’s 240 pounds. That’s not somebody who is going to hold up on a down-to-down basis. However, he’s 6’5” with a 7’ wingspan. Dugger’s 35” arms should allow him to stay clean, but it’s going to take some time to learn the trades of a pass rusher. The flashes are happening. During Monday’s practice, Dugger beat Trent Williams on a rep. That’s right, one of the best left tackles in the game. That’s where Dugger’s athleticism shows. A 10-foot-6 inch broad jump translates to a quick first step that would give any tackle, even Williams, problems. But there were supposedly plenty of plays when Dugger looked lost, or didn’t have an answer to combat Isaac Alarcon, who is unlikely to make the roster. It’ll take time. Pass rushing is a craft that takes several years to master. It’s more than athleticism. Thankfully, he has another fellow rookie to lean on. There’s a reason the 49ers were cautious with Romello Height. It doesn’t take long to realize he has the “it” factor. Height moves differently than everybody else not named Nick Bosa. It’s reminiscent of Dee Ford. Height will be the designated pass rusher, much like Ford was. He has a deep bag of tricks. Dugger, if he’s going to continue to cross-train as a pass rusher, should follow Height closely.”
author: Yinon Raviv
