title: Cam Ward 2026 passing yards: What’s a success for Titans QB?
summary: Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward is expected to take a sizable step forward as a sophomore. After an impressive rookie season despite lackluster surroundings, the Titans bet big on Ward this offseason. They invested in his development by hiring Brian Daboll as his OC, and adding Wan’Dale Robinson and Carnell Tate at wide receiver. Ward […]
full_text: Jun 16, 2026; Nashville, TN, USA; Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward (1) talks with the media post practice during day 1 of mini-camp at Vanderbilt Health Football Center. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | Steve Roberts-Imagn Images Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward is expected to take a sizable step forward as a sophomore. After an impressive rookie season despite lackluster surroundings, the Titans bet big on Ward this offseason. They invested in his development by hiring Brian Daboll as his OC, and adding Wan’Dale Robinson and Carnell Tate at wide receiver. Ward finished his rookie season with 3,169 passing yards, 15 touchdowns, and seven interceptions. Ward had two head coaches (Brian Callahan and Mike McCoy) and two play callers (Callahan and Mike McCoy). His top wide receivers were fourth-round rookies Chimere Dike and Elic Ayomanor. Ward finished his rookie season ranked 17th in passing yards. The No. 1 overall pick likely would have been 16th had he not injured his shoulder on the first series of the Week 18 regular season finale. With a massive sophomore campaign looming, how many passing yards would you consider a success for Ward in 2026? The theme of OTAs and minicamp was that Ward apparently struggled . He’s learning Daboll’s offense while figuring out how to test tight throwing windows. Ward was better at minicamp than OTAs, proving he’s growing in Daboll’s scheme. We’re now underway at training camp, where he’s had mostly positive practices to date. Ward should aim for about 3,500 passing yards in 2026. That total would have placed 13th in the league last season ahead of Jordan Love and Aaron Rodgers. If Ward starts all 17 games, he’d just need to average roughly 206 passing yards per game to reach 3,500. Titans fans are hoping Ward takes a Drake Maye or Caleb Williams-like sophomore step. Maye finished fourth in passing yards last season with 4,394. Williams was seventh with 3,942. Perhaps Ward can flirt with 4,000 passing yards if he really thrives in Daboll’s system. Expectations are high for Ward as a sophomore. About 3,500+ passing yards would signal a success. Hopefully Ward establishes himself as the Titans’ franchise quarterback in 2026.
author: Justin Melo

title: Washington Commanders Week 2 training camp observations, standouts
summary: There is a lot going on in Ashburn, VA, as the Commanders are now over a full week into training camp. Unlike previous camps run by head coach Dan Quinn, this one seems a lot different in everything from access to vet rest days. What has been an entertaining start is expected to ramp up […]
full_text: There is a lot going on in Ashburn, VA, as the Commanders are now over a full week into training camp. Unlike previous camps run by head coach Dan Quinn , this one seems a lot different in everything from access to vet rest days. What has been an entertaining start is expected to ramp up even more as we head towards joint practices next week against the Dolphins. That’s especially true after Wednesday afternoon’s once-year pact with receiver Stefon Diggs . Before we look forward to all that on a Thursday off date on the training-camp calendar, let’s look back at my observations as we get into Week 2. Who has been running with the first team? Camp is a time to mix things up and see what guys can do when they are in certain situations. There is certainly a LOT of rotation going on, but from a first-team glance, this appears to be the way things have played out very early in camp, though the receiver should change with Diggs coming aboard. Offense: QB: Jayden Daniels RB: Bill Croskey-Merritt WR: Terry McLaurin WR: Treylon Burks WR: Luke McCaffrey TE: Chig Okonkwo TE 2 (12 personnel): Ben Sinnott LT: Laremy Tunsil LG: Chris Paul C: Julian Good-Jones (while Nick Allegretti has been out) RG: Sam Cosmi RT: Josh Conerly *Antonio Williams and Brandon Coleman have also gotten some work with the first team. Defense: EDGE: Odafe Oweh DT: Daron Payne DT: Javon Kinlaw DT 3 (when in an odd front): Tim Settle EDGE: K’Lavon Chaisson ILB: Frankie Luvu ILB: Sonny Styles SAM (walked-up): Leo Chenal CB: Mike Sainristil CB: Amik Robertson S: Nick Cross S: Jeremy Reaves S: Will Harris *Sainristil has been seeing time on the outside and in the slot. Before his abrupt retirement, Witherspoon was the other outside corner when Mikey was in the slot, with Rasul Douglas seeing some time mixed in with the first team on the outside. The Green Dot There was talk that rookie Sonny Styles or free agent signing Leo Chenal would get the green dot for defensive communication. After a week of camp, however, it appears Frankie Luvu is directing the defense. As The Athletic reporter Nicki Jhabvala says below, it’s still early and things can change once live action is upon us in September, but as of now, this is where things stand. For the “green dot” crowd … it’s still early, but Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw have both said that Frankie Luvu has been that guy getting everyone set. — Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) August 4, 2026 Camp standouts: Luke McCaffrey: The third-year wideout continues to stack good practices. He was a beast on Tuesday , having arguably the best practice of all the Commanders, and scored again Wednesday in team work on a dime from quarterback Jayden. He’s working both inside and outside and has been said to look good wherever he’s lining up. Ben Sinnott: The increased playing time is certainly benefitting Sinnott. He’s working with the ones in 12 personnel and coordinator David Blough is using him in a variety of different ways, including in-line and as an H-back. Bill Croskey-Merritt: Bill is noticeably bigger and is bringing that physicality with him during runs, however, it’s his hands out of the backfield that have stood out early on. Odafe Oweh/K’Lavon Chaisson: The EDGE duo have been as advertised, and MORE! Camp observers have spoken of the explosion to which both players get off the ball and there have been plays every day where the whistle needs to be blown to protect the quarterbacks. Sonny Styles: The way he triggers is just different! He’s a true sideline-to-sideline defender who brought the wood a few times during padded practice . Teammates have raved about his preparation, fluidity and overall athleticism. Frankie Luvu: Observers have stated that Luvu looks like the 2024 version, not the one we saw struggle last season. He’s been looking great on timely blitzes. Sam Cosmi: Fully healthy now, Cosmi is said to be bullying guys out there, especially during Monday’s padded practice one-on-one session. Nick Cross: Cross has been all over the field, and there were many times when observers said if it was live action, he would have blown the play up. He’s going to have a big role for this new defense. Colson Yankoff: Yankoff, who has seen more time with the first and second groups with John Bates out, has made the most of his opportunities. That’s especially true in the passing game; hauling in a few really impressive catches in traffic. Josh Josephs: The rookie has impressed with his length, get-off and even coverage ability working primarily with the second group. Antonio Williams: Observers have commented on how smooth Williams is and how quickly he can uncover. He’s been with the second group a lot and backup quarterback Marcus Mariota has missed him on a few occasions where he’s been wide open. On Wednesday, during the second padded practice, he absolutely TOASTED the third- and fourth-string defense for an easy touchdown. Rasul Douglas: Douglas showed up the first two days of camp, when observers said he was all around the ball. He had a pick-six on Day 2 and supposedly looked pretty good during padded practice. Mike Sainristil: It’s been a mixed bag for Sainristil in coverage, but observers have said he’s constantly working, and it seems when he gets beat, he comes back and makes some plays. His leadership has been lauded by some of the coaches. Jeremy Reaves: Coaches have praised his effort and communication in this new defense. Who has struggled? There is a lot of praise early in camp, so the observations on who has struggled have been limited. Below is some of what I have heard early on. Marcus Mariota: Observers have said he’s not seeing things as quickly and hasn’t pulled the trigger on some throws he should have made. Quan Martin: Martin has been running with the second team after being a starter the previous two seasons. I’m not hearing that he’s been particularly bad, but he may have lost his starting job early on. He did get stiff-armed into another galaxy today by Fatman Allen. Jaylin Lane: Lane had some early drop issues, but it seems he has cleared those up over the past few sessions. Consistency will be key for the second-year pro. Car’lin Vigers: The young corner made some plays during the first day of camp, but recent reports are that he’s struggled staying with receivers in his zone. Josh Conerly: I don’t know how much struggling Conerly has actually done considering Washington has been in pads just two days, but MANY reports out of practice cite both Oweh and Chaisson getting into the backfield quickly, and I don’t believe Tunsil’s name was mentioned as someone who has been blowing a lot of pass sets. Competition between Blough and Jones We knew this would be a theme all camp, but it’s so refreshing to hear that coordinators David Blough and Daronte Jones are out here playing 3D chess against one another during sessions. Iron shapes iron, so this is absolutely music to my ears, especially after putting up with two very predictable offenses and defenses over the past two seasons. Blough has also been getting into his bag of tricks, as he looks for ways to slow down Jones’ furious rush. Wednesday he had, by all accounts, three trick plays, including a pretty hook-and-ladder between Jayden, Terry and Burks.

title: State of Commanders receiver corps after Stefon Diggs acquisition
summary: The Commanders receiver corps obviously got better with the Stefon Diggs acquisition. The veteran is a top-tier route runner and a steady producer with a long track record of success. While he’s 32 years old, Diggs can still move and make important catches in the clutch.   Head coach Dan Quinn has established a competitive […]
full_text: The Commanders receiver corps obviously got better with the Stefon Diggs acquisition . The veteran is a top-tier route runner and a steady producer with a long track record of success. While he’s 32 years old, Diggs can still move and make important catches in the clutch. Head coach Dan Quinn has established a competitive Commanders training camp, but it’s safe to say Diggs will eventually step into the No. 2 receiver slot opposite Terry McLaurin. He’s expected to get significant playing time and get targeted a ton, even though he may not be a true every-down player after playing 55% of the offensive snaps in New England last season. He’ll also impact his position group just by joining it. A roster spot just got harder to earn at the position with Terry McLaurin, Diggs and third-round pick Antonio Williams as roster locks. Jaylin Lane’s punt-return ability makes him darn-close to one, with maybe two more roster spots available. Fierce battles will be waged for those, among talented individuals. A few thoughts on how the Diggs addition might impact the receiver corps. Terry McLaurin Terry will remain scary while continuing to move around the formation as new coordinator David Blough always intended. McLaurin is the alpha around here, on a long-term deal and one of the longest-tenured players on the Commanders roster. He also has an even-keeled leadership vibe that will hold his position group together and help it improve with all the extra behind-the-scenes work he does. None of that will change with Diggs around. The new guy commands respect and should keep defenses from focusing too heavily on McLaurin. That’s nothing but a positive for the veteran, who could be in for a monster year. Antonio Williams Having a savvy veteran who’s next-level at creating separation should help the young rookie become more adept in his own right at creating separation. It should actually be a huge help in his development. Toss out those thoughts of Diggs impeding Williams’ progress. This will allow the third-round pick to develop without the pressure of having to be a primary target early in his first professional season. Trust me, if Williams gets open a ton and builds trust, quarterback Jayden Daniels will throw him the football. While Williams has experience and college production playing in the slot, he could move around a bunch like Diggs and McLaurin. Jaylin Lane/Luke McCaffrey These young guys have speed and have flashed potential as NFL playmakers. Both guys can take the top off a defense and at least expand a coverage area to create room for others. Development will be key for both players this summer, as they work to earn opportunities and provide the quality depth most good teams possess. Injuries happen, and the Commanders must be ready for them. Treylon Burks The Diggs signing might’ve impacted the fifth-year veteran the most. Treylon Burks was in the conversation to be Washington’s No. 2 receiver, with a shot to be a heavily-involved on-field presence. That seems unlikely now, if the top receivers stay healthy. Burks still has a lot to offer in terms of size and physicality in the pattern, but a large sum of targets potentially available to him might be gone now. He can earn a role on the team with a solid summer, but he has more of an uphill battle to that end than he did on Tuesday. Dyami Brown Head coach Dan Quinn was complimentary of Brown on Wednesday morning, saying how much better he looks in this second stint in Washington. He has solid chemistry with Daniels , which puts him in serious play for a roster spot. Realistic expectations around his involvement certainly dropped on Wednesday, though. Everything we just discussed is projection, though, with much of training camp and the preseason to sort things out now that Diggs is a Commander. A way-too-early WR roster projection: Terry McLaurin Stefon Diggs Antonio Williams Jaylin Lane Luke McCaffrey Treylon Burks *NOTE: I have a tough time seeing seven receivers make the 53-man roster, even with two returners in the position group. There are too many other depth needs in other spots. I also think Burks could make it over Dyami Brown because he’s a big dude and his physical, contested-catch ability could be useful within this group, but it’s a toss-up. Lane and McCaffrey provide speed. Burks and Brown will battle it out, forcing coaches to make a tough decision on the sixth receiver. What do you think of this receiver roster projection? Who’s impacted most by the Diggs signing? Who’s helped by it? Let everyone know in the comments below.

title: How Stefon Diggs will help Jayden Daniels, elevate Commanders offense
summary: The Commanders need an established, legit No. 2 receiver opposite Terry McLaurin to help quarterback Jayden Daniels.   That statement was true back in 2024. And in 2025. And again, heading into 2026 training camp.   It isn’t a fact anymore. Not after the Commanders agreed on terms of a one-year contract with veteran receiver […]
full_text: The Commanders need an established, legit No. 2 receiver opposite Terry McLaurin to help quarterback Jayden Daniels. That statement was true back in 2024. And in 2025. And again, heading into 2026 training camp. It isn’t a fact anymore. Not after the Commanders agreed on terms of a one-year contract with veteran receiver Stefon Diggs. A league source confirmed the pact on Wednesday afternoon, which ESPN reports is worth up to $12 million . Commanders general manager Adam Peters fortified the team’s greatest roster weakness with the Diggs addition, adding an established producer to a position group previously lacking it outside of McLaurin. Diggs is a tide to lift all boats, someone who will make those around him better. He’ll take coverage away from McLaurin and tight end Chig Okonkwo. He’ll allow rookie third-round pick Antonio Williams to develop without the pressure of needing to make a massive and immediate impact. He’ll be a leader by example in terms of route running and creating separation for all pass catchers and Williams in particular. I mean, just look at these highlights: Welcome home to Stefon Diggs. "We all we got, we all we need." The floor has been elevated. #RaiseHail #Terps pic.twitter.com/BBVODzZjBu — George Carmi (@Gcarmi21) August 5, 2026 Diggs is also a quarterback-friendly receiver who will do wonders for Jayden Daniels. While he hasn’t averaged above 12 yards per reception since 2022, Diggs remains steadily productive. That’s what Daniels needs, maybe above all else. Diggs has exceeded 1,000 receiving yards in seven of his last eight seasons , save a 2024 campaign in Houston where he tore an ACL. Diggs rebounded from that event in a big way, totaling 85 catches for 1,103 receiving yards and three touchdowns on 105 targets in his first (and only) season with the New England Patriots. Going deeper inside those numbers shows immense value and the reliability Daniels needs, as expressed with stats unearthed by Warren Sharp. Stefon Diggs to DC his 2025 season: #1 EPA/target (+0.68) #2 success rate (66%) #6 yards/target (9.9) the consistency was MASSIVE: #1 catch rate (83%) #1 accurate target catch rate (89%) #1 lowest WR error rate (2%) and only 2 drops all season! (out of all WR w 100+ targ) pic.twitter.com/gLJWDSM8PE — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) August 5, 2026 That’s trust quantified right there. Diggs will make the quarterback better, and he’ll make skill players around him better because he’s a threat who has earned opponent’s respect. He’s also become known as a vocal leader later in his career with high standards (and maybe some tough love) and expectations for those around him. His resume should command respect, though it will still remain McLaurin’s meeting room. He’s the alpha in Washington, even with Diggs around. It’s also important that Diggs sign at this point in camp, with sufficient time to learn David Blough’s new offense and its verbiage. There’s alaso time to get reps with Daniels and to bond with the Commanders other pass catchers. Diggs doesn’t come to Washington as a savior. He is a high-efficacy supplement to a Commanders roster with tremendous upside and a top-tier quarterback who comes through in the clutch. He’s 32 years old, but the DMV native and University of Maryland product remains in great shape and seems genuinely excited to play near his hometown. Stefon Diggs is at Maryland’s first fall practice. “Shout out to my Terps, man. And go Commanders. Let’s go.” pic.twitter.com/QIghaTF2a2 — Scott Bair (@ScottBairNFL) August 5, 2026 Mark Tyler and John Portis will surely chime in with more detailed breakdowns of Diggs’ fit in the coming days, but it doesn’t take a film expert to realize how the veteran receiver can help Daniels and a Washington offense that could’ve been good without him. Now that Diggs is in the mix, it should be much, much better. How does the Stefon Diggs signing change your expectations for the Commanders offense in 2026? Let us know in the comments below:

title: What we’ve learned from the Commanders’ first week of training camp
summary: We’re just one week into training camp, and the Washington Commanders are already beginning to answer many of the biggest questions that surrounded their roster entering the 2026 season. Offensively, Washington entered camp confident its wide receiver and center depth could withstand the difficulties of a 17-game season. That confidence is already being tested, however, […]
full_text: We’re just one week into training camp, and the Washington Commanders are already beginning to answer many of the biggest questions that surrounded their roster entering the 2026 season. Offensively, Washington entered camp confident its wide receiver and center depth could withstand the difficulties of a 17-game season. That confidence is already being tested, however, as projected starting center Nick Allegretti (calf) is missing valuable practice time with an early camp injury . Practices under new offensive coordinator David Blough have seemingly breathed life into the team’s tight ends, and while injuries have created uncertainty up front, they’ve also opened opportunities elsewhere. John Bates is missing time due to an injury, though Ben Sinnott and Colson Yankoff each have had shining moments throughout the first few practices. With Sinnott and Yankoff both stepping up to the plate, the real question now centers on which guy proves themselves more valuable to Blough? Sinnott, a former second-round pick, is finally receiving meaningful opportunities. Instead of running away with the job, he’s locked in a legitimate competition with Colson Yankoff for a larger role in Blough’s offense. Defensively, one of the biggest offseason questions centered on new coordinator Daronte Jones and what his defense would look like once practices began. Jones has quickly established an aggressive, attacking defensive identity, and his players are loving it. Odafe Oweh , Javon Kinlaw , Jeremy Reaves and Daron Payne are some who all shared great perspective on his teaching style and scheme. Jones has frequently moved the front seven into multiple alignments, creating unpredictability and forcing the offense to identify pressure and assignments differently on nearly every snap. A major question headed into training camp was the depth of the cornerback room. Rasul Douglas was a signing at the start of camp and has quickly made his presence felt early with turnovers and pass breakups. Trey Amos, as of today, is still recovering from last season’s leg injury, and he’s scheduled to be reassessed on Thursday. Ahkello Witherspoon was placed on Washington’s reserve/retired list, prompting Washington to sign Fabian Moreau . Whether the group can hold up over a 17-game season remains unanswered, but ,Washington, to me, has at least turned what looked like a glaring weakness into a position that appears capable of competing. On the latest Trap or Dive Podcast , Dre and I dive into the Training Camp Chronicles of the Washington Commanders, discussing our major takeaways from the first week of practices. Specifically, we discuss: Washington’s issue at Center Ben Sinnott vs. Colson Yankoff Cornerback room; Rasul Douglas impact Running back room is shining Ideal nickel defense Podcast: YouTube : Comment and let us know your thoughts a week into Washington’s training camp, and subscribe to the Trap or Dive Podcast.

title: Jeremy Reaves pushing hard for defensive role in Commanders camp
summary: Commanders defensive back/core special teammer Jeremy Reaves came up twice during Dan Quinn’s Tuesday morning press conference. The head coach used both questions to laud the veteran’s presence in this 2026 training camp, going well beyond the typical platitudes common this time of year.   It’s clear that Reaves has made a positive impression early […]
full_text: Commanders defensive back/core special teammer Jeremy Reaves came up twice during Dan Quinn’s Tuesday morning press conference. The head coach used both questions to laud the veteran’s presence in this 2026 training camp, going well beyond the typical platitudes common this time of year. It’s clear that Reaves has made a positive impression early on and is challenging for an increased role in Daronte Jones’ defens e. Reaves has built a career on excellent special teams play, with Pro-Bowl and All-Pro selection s honoring those efforts. His defensive contributions have been more minimal. They were virtually non-existent in 2023 – he played just five games that year – and again in 2024. His role increased in 2025, as the career safety got more involved. An injury to Will Harris created some opportunity – so did Quan Martin’s ineffectiveness — but Quinn also found ways to get him involved. Reaves posted a career-high 91 total tackles and had an interception and two passes defensed. Reaves has always been a valued presence in the Commanders locker room but he’s apparently pressing for even more in 2026. “His communication skills are elite as a ball player, as a teammate on the field and off,” Quinn said his Wednesday presser. “So much of what we’re doing goes through out communication hub at linebacker and safety, so seeing him and Frankie (Luvu) and others…he’s an initiator of so many good things that we talk through. He sets incredible standards for effort and speed. “We could use a hell of a lot more Jeremy Reaves. He’s a remarkable teammate, player – he’s definitely making his presence felt on defense more so than he has in the previous two years.” Jones is installing a new defensive system that requires different player strengths and an opportunity for everyone to compete for playing. While he may not be the most athletic player, his football IQ is sky high and he’s a physical player in the back. We’re also expecting some three-safety sets from Jones this season, so Reaves could find a role somewhere in one or more of the personnel packages. Reaves is getting a shot to prove himself in this camp. We’ll see what he makes of it. “He has earned the right to have these reps,” Quinn said. “He’s got high standards about how he wants to go. He’s very much in the mix from a defensive standpoint. As you’re starting a new, system, everyone’s on the same level to say, ‘where’s he gonna go?’ To see him take advantage of that, that’s a big deal. He has always had unique leadership communication qualities, so it’s nice to see that coming out on the defensive side as well.” What would it take for Jeremy Reaves secure significant snaps on the Commanders defense? Let us know in the comments below:

title: How Rachaad White, Jayden Daniels college connection can help Commanders
summary: Running back Rachaad White has known quarterback Jayden Daniels a long time, way before Commanders fans keyed on him prior to the 2024 NFL draft. The relationship began before his two LSU campaigns turned Daniels into a household name.   It started in 2020, after White transferred to Arizona State from a California junior college. […]
full_text: Running back Rachaad White has known quarterback Jayden Daniels a long time, way before Commanders fans keyed on him prior to the 2024 NFL draft . The relationship began before his two LSU campaigns turned Daniels into a household name. It started in 2020, after White transferred to Arizona State from a California junior college. Daniels had starred for the Sundevils a year prior, and White quickly saw something in the young signal caller. “I tell everyone this all the time. He’s just special,” White said in a press conference Wednesday after a Commanders training camp practice. “I knew that after I came into ASU, when I saw him move and throw the ball around, when I saw him in big games and how he came down in the clutch and won it for us. “To see how poised he is all the time – he just stays level-headed and even keeled. He has different things that (not everyone has). That’s what makes him unique. He has obviously matured since we were together in college but, other than that, how he handles and goes about his business, how he’s up early and how he attacks the day and always talks about football, football, football. That’s how he’s the same way (he has always been).” White has said a few time now that Daniels is the best quarterback he has ever played with. The Arizona State experience told him so, as did Daniels performance in the NFL. “He’s talented, but he can also apply himself,” White said. “I’ve seen him come through in the clutch so many times for us (at Arizona State). The same thing with his rookie year. He may have been banged up last year but, in the games he play, y’all were in those games. When you have a guy like that, and he’s so talented and the way he makes an impact, you’re going to be in every game.” Washington learned that in 2024, when Daniels was excellent in close games especially. He had four fourth-quarter comebacks and the Commanders were 8-4 in one-score games. White was starring in Tampa Bay at the time, but paid attention to Daniels’ meteoric rise. When free agency arrived and Washington showed interest, White jumped at the chance to reunite with his college teammate. The chemistry reformed quickly, picking up from a 2021 Arizona State season where both guys were awesome. Daniels has 2,380 passing yards and 10 touchdowns (and 10 picks), while White had 1,006 rushing yards and 15 rushing touchdowns, plus another 456 receiving yards. Daniels has targeted White a ton already, so the trust is already there. White is well versed on how to keep it going. “Everything with the quarterback starts with trust,” White said. “Him knowing that I know the play and I’ll be there in the right spot. He knows he can trust me to make something shake if he drops it down to me.” White’s joining a quality running back room where competition will sort out reps and roles. We discussed Bill Croskey Merritt on Tuesday, including his emphasis on improving receiving skill. White’s solid on third-down but can run inside, which makes them an enticing duo atop the depth chart. The carry/target breakdown will be influenced by this training camp and preseason, but also by matchups. Expect both guys to be heavily involved, even if neither guy sees many in-game touches. “The guys in the room (overall) do a lot of great things from the aspect of working on their game,” White said. “Bill has done a lot of things to work on his pass game and catch the ball well and working on his routes. …All of us in the room can do good things. It’s great to have everybody in there, competing against each other.” Will the chemistry between Rachaad White and Jayden Daniels lead to big receiving numbers for the running back? How will the carry split between White and Croskey-Merritt work out? Let us know in the comments below:

summary: The Daily Slop – 5 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles The Athletic (paywall) […]
full_text: ASHBURN, VA - JULY 29: Quarterback Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders looks on during training camp at BigBear.ai Performance Center at Commanders Park on July 29, 2026 in Ashburn, Virginia. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 5 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles The Athletic (paywall) How 50 executives and coaches rank 35 veteran quarterbacks 2026 Quarterback Tiers The panel this year consisted of eight general managers, five assistant GMs, five former GMs and three other executives, plus nine head coaches, 10 defensive coordinators, five offensive coordinators, two offensive assistants, one defensive assistant and two coaches specializing in analytics/game management. That’s 21 execs and 29 coaches overall. Each voter placed 35 veteran quarterbacks into five tiers, from best (Tier 1) to worst (Tier 5). Quarterbacks were then ranked by average vote and placed into tiers. The survey excludes rookies because voters have not seen them play in the NFL. Daniels proved as a rookie he can be one of the most dynamic quarterbacks in the game. His second season amplified durability questions that followed him into the league. “He’s got to reprove it,” a defensive coach said. Daniels suffered the third-largest year-over-year drop after Geno Smith and Tua Tagovailoa. “I think he was a little quick to take off and run last year,” an exec said. “They spent a lot of money on that offensive line and drafted some guys, so I think he has to just settle into that position. He has all the talent.” “Jayden was really, really good in terms of his authority to make plays both on and off schedule. It’s extremely difficult to defend guys who can do both, so I think they’ve got a chance for a real bounceback.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE 2026 QB Tiers is live!! @TheAthletic keeps raising the bar in terms of production quality This year you can produce your own tiers with your own votes Link in replies pic.twitter.com/MAy63JiKz5 — Mike Sando (@SandoNFL) August 4, 2026 In that @TheAthletic @SandoNFL piece on QB tiers – the #NFL execs/coaches put Caleb Williams slightly ahead of Jayden Daniels. Call me biased but as I said in the draft process & since – I would still take JD5 over Caleb, who I view as a wild card, inconsistent roller coaster — Chris Russell AKA the 🐓🐓! (@Russellmania621) August 4, 2026 Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders Training Camp Review: OL vs DL 1-on-1s The Washington Commanders had their first padded practice of training camp on Monday. There’s always a different level of hype and intensity when the pads come on for the first time and we finally get to see some physicality, especially in the trenches. Unfortunately, the team is still being very secretive with clips being posted online and fans in attendance being allowed to film, but some fans still posted a few clips One of the few clips I was able to find was a good one. It came from @AsiasAnalysis on twitter. She posted a clip of offensive line vs defensive line one-on-one drills. This is one of the best drills to watch when the pads come on so it was good to see a few reps. I’ll post the full clip from Asia first and then cut up each individual clip to break down in more detail. pic.twitter.com/gi5EtOJZV9 — Asia’s Analysis (@AsiasAnalysis) August 3, 2026 The first full rep we see is right tackle Josh Conerly Jr. against free agent signing Odafe Oweh . I wrote a few weeks ago about Conerly learning from Tunsil and you can see some improvements here, but still some things to work on. Oweh takes his first few steps up the field, challenging the edge. Conerly does a better job staying square compared to last year. His feet, hips and shoulders are much more square to the line of scrimmage than they were during the season last year. That’s a positive start. However, Oweh hits Conerly with a spin move. Conerly was guilty of giving up inside rushes a fair bit last year and part of the reason for that is that he often didn’t have his cleats in the ground at the point of contact. You can see here that as Oweh makes contact, Conerly is shuffling his inside foot backwards. Oweh works into his spin and if you pause the clip when you can see the full number 98 on Oweh’s back, you’ll see that both of Conerly’s feet are off the ground. That gives him no base to absorb any post. It’s a nice, tight spin from Oweh to get inside, but credit to Conerly for not giving up on the play. Conerly has the athletic ability to recover from bad situations and he does that here somewhat. He works to get his inside hand on Oweh’s chest to slow him down and try to delay the rush. Conerly leans on him and keeps a firm grip, enabling him to push Oweh down the line slightly. This would have bought the quarterback time to shuffle to his right and potentially scramble away from the pressure. Overall, it’s not an ideal rep from Conerly but one that shows some significant improvements with regards to staying square, while also showing there’s still some work to go, which we expect of all second year players. On the other side of the ball, it was a nice rush from Oweh that clearly generated plenty of pressure and would have forced the quarterback off the spot. With his athleticism, Oweh would have had a decent chance of breaking free and chasing down many quarterbacks too. I wrote about this clip from @AsiasAnalysis of Commanders OL vs DL 1-on-1s yesterday. Some fun reps, broke each one down: https://t.co/ib7afy3TBY https://t.co/Or5OUS41RF — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) August 4, 2026 Commanders Roundtable Commanders notes: McCaffrey stands out; defense brings the heat Luke McCaffrey — The Biggest Winner of the Day If you weren’t talking about Luke McCaffrey before today, you will be now. He was the standout of the practice. McCaffrey hauled in multiple deep catches, the most eye-catching of which was a 40-plus yard seam route out of the slot where Daniels put the ball right on him in traffic, splitting Mike Sainristil and Jeremy Reaves with a dime that had everyone on the sideline taking notice. McCaffrey caught it cleanly and didn’t get touched until the five-yard line on the run after the catch. The middle of the field was his territory all day. He added another deep grab later in practice — another 40-ish yard shot down the seam — and the combination of his speed, his hands, and Daniels’ willingness to trust him over the top is a matchup that defensive coordinators around the NFC are going to have a problem with. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders.com Training camp notebook | Jayden Daniels shines in strong practice for offense The depth at the tight end position continues to get more looks, and the players are stepping up with more positive plays in the passing game. Colson Yankoff has gotten most of the attention and had a nice catch from Marcus Mariota during team drills. But Lawrence Cager might have had the catch of the day near the end of practice making a leaping grab in the middle of the field with Daniels under center. It feels like most of the tight end room is with Okonkwo, John Bates and Ben Sinnott at the top of the position, but players like Yankoff and Cager are making strong cases for the Commanders to keep four tight ends on the roster. The Commanders are in the second day of a three-day practice stretch, and Quinn described it as “powering up.” That means the workload and intensity of practices are supposed to increase by the day, and he wants to see players push themselves. Wednesday will be the last practice before the players take a day off, so the players should expect to go through their most competitive and challenging practice of camp so far. title: 2026 NFL season: Future Hall of Famers from all 32 teams
summary: We went roster by roster to pick out the NFL players who are on track to make the Hall of Fame one day -- and those who still have some work to do.
full_text:
How many Hall of Famers are playing in the NFL right now?

 It depends on when you're evaluating, of course. There are veterans near the end of their careers who have already proved themselves as locks to receive the game's highest honor one day, such as  Aaron Rodgers and Derrick Henry . There are players in their prime who are well on their way, such as  Justin Jefferson and Pat Surtain II . And then there are young players who haven't yet proved themselves to be Hall of Famers but could break out in the years to come, such as  Caleb Downs or Arvell Reese from the 2026 draft.

 Go back to 2002, the first year of the 16-game era. There are 54 players who suited up for at least one game that season currently enshrined in the Hall of Fame. That list doesn't include Tom Brady (who becomes eligible in 2028) or borderline candidates such as Steve Smith and Reggie Wayne, who could earn enough votes to cross the threshold in the future. At the very least, we can use 55 Hall of Famers as our gauge, which is just under 3% of the 1,839 players who suited up for at least one game that season.

 
 Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' 

 
 Today, I'm going through each of the league's 32 teams and attempting to identify the players who either are on track or have a realistic hope of earning gold jackets one day. This will be my estimate of who is likely to make it using historical comparables as opposed to my opinion of who should or should not be enshrined at some point. Naturally, that includes positional preferences; voters have historically loved to honor quarterbacks, running backs and receivers, but the bar is higher for linemen. I won't attempt to pick among the rookies, whom we haven't yet seen line up for an NFL snap, but I'll work with everybody else and split the most notable candidates into one of five categories:

 
 Players listed as "in" have already done enough to earn enshrinement given their existing résumé. They could retire tomorrow and make it into the Hall of Fame after they become eligible. 
 Those "on the cusp" have already done the vast majority of the work required and need only another season or two of solid play to get over the hump. As it stands, their résumé might already be enough to get in, but another successful season could push them into lock territory. 
 The "keep it up" category is for players who are performing at a Hall of Fame level but haven't done so for a long enough time to guarantee their path to enshrinement. They need to play at or near their existing level for several more seasons to have a shot. 
 Guys who have "work to do" aren't on track to make it to the Hall of Fame with their existing résumé and/or their most recent level of play. In some cases, that could be because injuries slowed their progress in 2025, or because they haven't played at a Hall-caliber level for long enough. They still have a shot, but something has to change. 
 Finally, the "missing out" category is for veterans who are at the point where they don't have the existing résumé to make it to the Hall nor the time to reestablish themselves as viable candidates. Though anything's possible, it will be a serious surprise if any of these players end up in Canton one day. They're far more likely to end up in the Hall of Very Good. 
 
 I usually start these all-32 columns with teams on the East Coast, so let's mix things up and begin out west.

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LV | LAC | LAR | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 NFC West 
 

 Arizona Cardinals 
 On the cusp: S Budda Baker 

 Baker has been stuck on some bad teams -- the Cardinals have one winning season across his nine years in the league -- but Pro Bowl voters have consistently seen him as an impactful and rangy difference-making safety. He has made eight Pro Bowls across that span. Every eligible player with at least 10 Pro Bowl appearances has been enshrined in Canton, so if Baker can earn two more, he should be a lock. One more might even be enough for the 30-year-old.

 Keep it up: TE Trey McBride 

 The invisible force field that had kept McBride out of the end zone early in his career finally lifted in 2025, as he scored 11 touchdowns, nearly doubling his total over the prior three seasons combined (six). He's not quite as explosive or elusive after the catch as Travis Kelce was in his prime or Brock Bowers has been so far as a pro, but McBride makes up that for with great hands and massive target shares.

 

 
 

 Los Angeles Rams 
 In: WR Davante Adams , Edge Myles Garrett , QB Matthew Stafford 

 I don't think I need to do much convincing here. Garrett's one of the best defenders in league history, and Adams had a five-year peak as arguably the top wide receiver in football. The case against Stafford would have been that nobody had ever really seen him as the best QB in the NFL (or close to it) in any of his first 16 years ... but after winning MVP last season, that one's out the window. He's already in the top seven for career passing yards and touchdowns, and with an MVP and a Super Bowl victory, Stafford will waltz in.

 Keep it up: WR Puka Nacua 

 Nacua already has 1,486- and 1,715-receiving yard seasons to his name by the end of his third pro campaign, which is remarkable, even given that those years are part of the 17-game era. Just for fun, the 2023 fifth-round pick is also one of the league's best blocking wideouts. The only questions are whether Nacua can stay on the field for full seasons at a time and whether there's any drop-off once Stafford is ultimately replaced by Ty Simpson .

 

 Work to do: CB Trent McDuffie , DT Kobie Turner , Edge Byron Young 

 The talented young linemen the Rams already had up front should get a boost from playing alongside Garrett. I thought Turner was the best of the bunch last season, but Young was devastating at times and parlayed his 12-sack, 29-knockdown campaign into his first Pro Bowl. I'm intrigued to see whether the Rams can afford to keep their DL standouts -- both of whom are pending free agents -- alongside Garrett for years to come.

 

 
 

 San Francisco 49ers 
 In: WR Mike Evans , RB Christian McCaffrey , OT Trent Williams 

 Evans and Williams are easy first-ballot selections. McCaffrey has struggled with injuries, but he has had multiple seasons as the best RB in the league and plays a position that the Hall is always looking to appreciate.

 On the cusp: TE George Kittle , LB Fred Warner 

 Kittle's right on the borderline of being a lock, having made seven Pro Bowls over his past eight pro campaigns before he  tore his right Achilles last postseason. I'd vote for Kittle given his dominance as a blocker and four 1,000-yard seasons, but tight ends can go underappreciated by the Hall at times. One more substantial season would push Kittle, 32, to the "lock" side of things. I'd argue the same for Warner, who had four first-team All-Pro nods over a five-year span before his own serious injury a year ago.

 Work to do: Edge Nick Bosa , QB Brock Purdy 

 Bosa has a Defensive Player of the Year award to his name, but a pair of September ACL tears have essentially cost the 2019 first-round pick two of his seven pro seasons. He needs another great season and a couple more Pro Bowl-caliber campaigns to get back on the Hall track. Purdy's efficiency has slipped since that dramatic 2023 campaign, and he has suffered meaningful injuries in three of his four pro seasons.

 Missing out: FB Kyle Juszczyk 

 Remember when I said a minute ago that every eligible player with at least 10 Pro Bowl appearances was enshrined in Canton? Well, Juszczyk will be a fascinating case to see whether that keeps up, given that he just earned his 10th consecutive Pro Bowl nod in 2025.

 Of course, while Juszczyk is a good player, it's fair to wonder whether he's racking up Pro Bowl appearances by virtue of being the…

title: Proposing five big trades during 2026 NFL training camps
summary: NFL rosters are mostly locked in for 2026, but we crafted five potential win-win deals teams should consider making before Week 1.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL season might be a little more than a month away, but rosters aren't locked in quite yet. Training camp brings hope, optimism and trade talks, which is what we're focusing on here. And there are still a few roster holes to be patched -- and some trade candidates who could be dealt to fill them. So, let's play matchmaker.

 I'm proposing five deals that would make sense for both sides considering each team's depth chart, contention horizon and salary cap, along with each player's ability and contract. Is this finally the moment when the Giants move on from edge rusher Kayvon Thibodeaux ? Could Kayshon Boutte find a new home after the Patriots' wide receiver acquisitions? And is there a star defender who would fit well with the 49ers?

 Let's dive in. Here are five trades that should happen before Week 1.

 

 
 Jump to a proposed trade involving: 
 Bates | Thibodeaux 
 Coleman | Little | Boutte 

 
 

 

 49ers get a defensive boost with Bates 
 49ers receive: S Jessie Bates III , 2028 sixth-round pick 
 Falcons receive: 2027 third-round pick

 The Falcons' 2023 signing of Bates was an example of free agency gone right. The Falcons paid sticker price -- four years and $64 million -- to sign Bates, who was very effective in Cincinnati and continued that quality play in Atlanta. That was particularly true in 2023, when Bates delivered six interceptions and three forced fumbles while earning second-team All-Pro honors.

 He was good again in 2024, but he wasn't quite on the same level last season. Still, the 29-year-old Bates remains one of the best safeties in the league. (He ranked fifth in this year's survey of coaches and executives conducted by ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.)

 

 If the Falcons were expected to contend, it would make sense to keep Bates and see the original contract through. But they aren't, and with a ton of 2027 cap space even after the  Bijan Robinson   extension , the Falcons will likely be spenders next offseason. They would risk losing Bates without getting a compensatory pick in return if he walks in free agency. So it's better for Atlanta to deal him now. And while that would mean finding a replacement for Bates, the Falcons wouldn't be lacking in safety talent thanks to emerging second-year player Xavier Watts .

 It just so happens that former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, who coached Bates the past two seasons, is now the 49ers' defensive coordinator . And he could use an upgrade at safety alongside Ji'Ayir Brown and Malik Mustapha . The timing works, as the 49ers are contenders who could use defensive help after ranking 25th in EPA allowed per dropback last season.

 

 San Francisco would be giving up real draft capital for a short-term player, but that's an indicator of Bates' skill and the fact that his contract would cost the 49ers only $13 million in 2026 -- a below-market price to sign a player of his caliber.

 
 

 Patriots satisfy the edge-rush need with Thibodeaux 
 Patriots receive: Edge  Kayvon Thibodeaux , 2027 fifth-round pick 
 Giants receive: 2027 third-round pick

 I included a Thibodeaux trade in this same story last year . One year and another first-round edge rusher later, he's now an even more obvious candidate to be dealt.

 Thibodeaux is playing on his $14.75 million fifth-year option and is set to be a free agent at the end of this season. While there was an argument for having him as a third edge rusher behind Brian Burns and Abdul Carter  in the past, New York now also has first-round pick Arvell Reese , who plays linebacker and edge. To keep Thibodeaux around at this price point to potentially be the team's No. 4 edge rusher isn't ideal.

 So the Giants need to find a trade partner who:

 
 Has a need at edge 
 Has the cap room to take on Thibodeaux's 2026 contract 
 Is an immediate contender, given his pending free agent status 
 
 New England fits the bill and then some because Thibodeaux offers long-term upside if the Patriots decide to re-sign him. Their current edge rushers are Harold Landry III and Dre'Mont Jones . At this stage of their careers (Landry is 30, Jones 29), they're better fits as No. 2 and No. 3 edge rushers, respectively, on a contending team. Thibodeaux hasn't been good enough yet to be New England's unquestioned top edge rusher, but he possesses the promise to develop into that.

 Thibodeaux's 9.9% pass rush win rate at edge last season -- below average for the position -- was similar to what Landry (10.8%) and Jones (8.6%) posted. Thibodeaux had only 2.5 sacks last season in 10 games but has shown more in the past. In 2024, he recorded a 16.8% pass rush win rate at edge (16th best), and he recorded 11.5 sacks as a rookie in 2022. Thibodeaux is also solid in the run game, and his 27.9% run stop win rate at edge last season was above average for the position.

 Giants fans will likely feel like the team should get more in this deal. But it's all about the contract, as Thibodeaux has only one year left on his deal and is getting paid pretty close to what he would probably make on the open market.

 

 

 
 

 Colts give Coleman a fresh start 
 Colts receive: WR Keon Coleman , 2028 sixth-round pick 
 Bills receive: 2027 fourth-round pick

 Coleman was already a potential trade candidate before Bills owner Terry Pegula blamed the team's former coaching staff -- as opposed to the current front office -- for pushing to draft the wide receiver with the No. 33 pick in 2024. Coleman has struggled in two NFL seasons, but it was a fairly shocking insult toward a player still on the roster.

 Buffalo doesn't have to trade him, but between his on-field struggles and the negative vibes stemming from ownership's comments, it certainly could. And the Colts would be a logical candidate to bet on Coleman at a reduced cost.

 Coleman has recorded 1.65 yards per route run over 583 career routes, along with a 48-51-49 triple-slash of open, catch and YAC scores from ESPN's player-tracking based  receiver scores . Those numbers aren't great and aren't what the Bills hoped for when they drafted him, but they're not terrible either. He definitely could still be a contributing player to a winning team with some growth.

 Indianapolis needs receiver help. After being re-signed to a $28.5 million-per-year deal , Alec Pierce underwent  ankle surgery and is not yet back on the practice field. The Colts have the promising Josh Downs in the slot, but the depth chart on the outside behind Pierce is rough, with Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and Ashton Dulin the likely next options. The Colts could use another receiver regardless of Pierce's status, so taking a chance on Coleman's upside makes sense.

 

 The Jahan Dotson trade in 2024 , in which the Eagles sent a third-round pick and two seventh-rounders to the Commanders for Dotson and a fifth-rounder, is a useful comp. Like Coleman, Dotson was entering his third year after an uneven first two seasons. But Dotson was a higher draft pick (No. 16 vs. No. 33) and was better regarded than Coleman is now, which is why I think it would cost less to acquire the latter.

 
 

 Cardinals get offensive line help with Little 
 Cardinals receive: OT Walker Little , 2027 seventh-round pick 
 Jaguars receive: 2027 sixth-round pick

 Little was Wally Pipped last year by Cole Van Lanen , who ascended into the starting lineup at left tackle after Little missed two games with a  concussion . The Jaguars kept Van Lanen at left tackle even after Little returned, then extended him in the offseason. That makes Little an expensive third tackle, due an almost fully guaranteed $11.5 million this season.

 

 Little had his best season in terms of pass block win rate in 2025 but was still only in the 27th percentile among tackles. While tackle depth is important, my guess is that the cap-strapped Jaguars would cut Little if his money weren't guaranteed. But it is. Dealing Little would be a cost-saving maneuver, so the compensation on any deal ought to be barely above -- maybe…

title: Matthew McConaughey contacts Bijan Robinson following contract extension
summary: When word got out about Robinson's new extension with the Falcons, it didn't take long for McConaughey to get in touch. In fact, it was only a matter of minutes.
full_text:
When news of Bijan Robinson 's new contract broke Tuesday, the first person the star running back heard from wasn't a teammate or a family member.

 It was actor Matthew McConaughey.

 Robinson revealed Wednesday that when word got out about his three-year extension with the Atlanta Falcons worth up to $75 million, it didn't take long for McConaughey to offer his congratulations. In fact, it was a matter of minutes.

 

 "As soon as the news hit, Matthew McConaughey hit me," Robinson told reporters. "As soon as it hit. I think it hit at like 7:56 [a.m.]. Like 7:58, he texted me.

 

 "A lot of awesome, really cool people texted me, but it was cool to see him, as soon as it hit, like, he was the first one."

 Robinson played college ball at Texas , where McConaughey is an alumnus and longtime superfan. The Falcons showed in their post of Robinson's quote a photo he took with McConaughey as a recruit on a visit to Austin. The former Longhorns running back has expressed interest in getting into acting following his playing career and was connected with McConaughey, with the two developing a friendship during Robinson's final collegiate year in 2022.

 For now, though, Robinson's talents will remain on the gridiron -- talents he's now better compensated for than he was last week.

title: Tracking 2026 NFL hold-ins: Gibbs, Vea and Tuipulotu
summary: Here is the latest on Falcons' Bijan Robinson, Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs, Bucs' Vita Vea and Chargers' Tuli Tuipulotu.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL preseason kicks off with the Pro Football Hall of Game on Thursday , with three weeks of action to follow, but there are a handful of prominent players who are still not practicing because of their contract situations.

 The start of NFL training camps brought these negotiations to a head. Players can hold out and stay away from camp until their financial situations are addressed, or they can hold in, where they report to camp to avoid fines but skip practice while waiting for a new contract. We're tracking the important hold-ins across the league, with updates from our NFL Nation writers on each situation.

 The list of stars not practicing includes Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs ,  Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea  and  Los Angeles Chargers outside linebacker  Tuli Tuipulotu . 

 Which player will be next in resolving his contract dispute? Are any of these four willing to miss games once the season begins? Let's examine each situation.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Gibbs | Robinson | Vea | Tuipulotu 

 
 

 

 Jahmyr Gibbs , RB, Detroit Lions 
 

 Status: Holding in, seeking a new contract 

 Aug. 4 update:  Lions coach Dan Campbell said  Bijan Robinson 's record-setting deal with the Atlanta Falcons  is " certainly not gonna hurt " the team's contract negotiations with their own star running back, Gibbs. The Falcons and Robinson agreed to a three-year extension Tuesday that includes $51 million guaranteed, setting the stage for a new deal for Gibbs, who continues to hold in and miss practices at training camp. "[Robinson's deal is] not gonna hurt, but we'll see," Campbell said. "Look, I'm anxious to get Gibbs back out there."

 Aug. 3 update: Gibbs  missed his fifth consecutive practice Monday as his apparent hold-in continues while he looks to reach agreement on a new deal during training camp. However, the three-time Pro Bowler was spotted roaming the sidelines in a gray Lions cutoff hoodie for the second straight day at the Meijer Performance Center, often chatting with teammates Amon-Ra St. Brown , Jameson Williams and Jared Goff on the sideline in between drills. While leaving the field to enter the locker room alongside team security, Gibbs was briefly approached by reporters and stated that "only time will tell" when he returns in his first official comments on his absence from practice.

 

 Aug. 2 update: Gibbs was spotted on the sidelines Sunday, sporting a hoodie as he watched his teammates practice for the first time since training camp began. Gibbs has now missed his fourth consecutive practice as he seeks a contract extension. Lions WR Jameson Williams described Gibbs as "the best of the best" following practice as they were spotted communicating in between on-field drills. Williams feels Gibbs should be the NFL's highest-paid running back. "I wouldn't even say look at the stats, look at the film," Williams said. "Nobody close. He's the best."

 July 31 update: The Lions star missed his third day of practice as the hold-in continues. Coach Dan Campbell mentioned earlier this week that Gibbs was dealing with a "little bit of a back" issue during conditioning tests but clarified that it's nothing to worry about ahead of Friday's session. "No, I don't think it's severe," Campbell said. Gibbs, who is showing up at the team facility, has continued to communicate with teammates, such as wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown . "Obviously, we're missing one of our best players on offense, which sucks, but he's still in the building," St. Brown said. "He's still at all the meetings and everything. So, I think that the players understand what's going on. Everyone kind of gets it. It's part of this business, but we're still out there practicing, doing our thing."

 July 30 update:  The running back missed his second straight day of practice Thursday as the apparent hold-in continues until he reaches a new contract extension. Campbell addressed the situation ahead of Thursday's practice, saying that he is "not even sweating it" as both sides are working to secure a long-term deal. Gibbs did complete a conditioning test Wednesday in which Campbell said he "had a little bit of a back" issue, so it's unclear if Gibbs will start practicing right away once he inks a new deal.

 -- Eric Woodyard, Lions reporter 

 

 
 

 Bijan Robinson , RB, Atlanta Falcons 
 Status: Signed a new deal 

 Aug. 4 update:  The two-time Pro Bowler and the Falcons reached agreement on a three-year extension worth up to $75 million that now will make him the highest-paid running back in NFL history, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

 Aug. 1 update:  Robinson was again at practice, though not practicing, for the fourth straight day. Robinson left the field at one point during the media video shooting period and then came back when the cameras were off. Otherwise, he was with his teammates on the sidelines like he has been since camp started on Wednesday.

 July 31 update : Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski addressed Robinson's hold-in for the first time Friday morning. He said he was confident the contract situation will be resolved amiably.

 On how he is approaching the conflict, Stefanski said: "Just coach the football team."

 "Understand that there's a business side to everything we do and there's the football side and sometimes you're living in both worlds, if you will," Stefanski said. "But just going to continue to coach the football team."

 Robinson was once again in a jersey with no helmet or cleats for a third straight day. He was on the sideline encouraging teammates after plays. At the end of practice, he did pushups with his teammates who lost a drill.

 July 30 update: Robinson was a hold-in for a second straight practice Thursday. Like Wednesday, the team's first practice of training camp, Robinson was present on the field, chatting with teammates and seemingly in good spirits. He wore a Falcons jersey but had no helmet or cleats. Robinson and the Falcons have not commented on the situation, though coach Kevin Stefanski is likely to address it Friday morning.

 -- Marc Raimondi, Falcons reporter 

 

 
 

 Vita Vea , DT, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 
 

 Status: Holding in, requesting a trade 

 Aug. 2 update: The star defensive tackle remains sidelined with a back injury, as well as his contract hold-in. Coach Todd Bowles said there is "nothing new" to report on his injury, and he is unsure if Vea will make the trip to the  New York Jets  for a pair of joint practices starting Aug. 11.

 July 31 update: Vea, who stayed indoors to receive treatment Thursday, was back out on the practice field Friday with teammates but was still sidelined with a back injury sustained during the team's conditioning test. Bowles said he does not have a timetable yet for Vea's back.

 July 30 update: While Vea was on the sidelines during Wednesday's first training camp practice and was standing alongside teammates during positional drills, he was not on the practice field Thursday. Bowles said Vea tweaked his back in the team's conditioning test Tuesday and he was getting treatment. Vea did, however, participate in an interview on the "Up & Adams Show," but he did not discuss his contract. Vea is set to earn $17 million this season, but none of it is guaranteed, along with a per-game roster bonus that is capped at $1 million total. Bowles said they are preparing for the season as if Vea will play. 

 -- Jenna Laine, Bucs reporter 

 

 
 

 Tuli Tuipulotu , OLB, Los Angeles Chargers 
 

 Status: Holding in, seeking a new contract

 Aug. 5 update:  Tuipulotu, who has been a limited participant in practice this training camp amid ongoing contract negotiations, was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. The caveat is that the practice was a walkthrough, so Tuipulotu and the other Chargers players were going at half speed. He still has yet to participate in a non-walkthrough practice 11-on-11 period, but his participation could be a…

title: 2026 Atlanta Falcons training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Falcons training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Atlanta Falcons ' camp is taking place in Flowery Branch, Georgia, and Falcons reporter Marc Raimondi has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Falcons camp. We will update this file often. How will the QB battle play out between  Michael Penix Jr . and  Tua Tagovailoa for QB1? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Falcons stories 
 
 Sources: Falcons, RB Robinson reach 3-year deal worth up to $75M 
 Falcons sign Matthew Bergeron to four-year, $96M extension 
 Falcons' Jalon Walker tore ACL, out for season 
 Wife of DC Ulbrich dies of cancer 
 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Michael Penix Jr . explained his current situation in the clearest way possible Wednesday.

 "If I can't be on the field," Penix said, "how am I going to be the starter?"

 Penix has been on the field. He has done individual drills and 7-on-7 sessions. But what the Falcons third-year quarterback means is that he has yet to be cleared for 11-on-11 work. And until he does, there cannot be any kind of quarterback competition.

 That is not necessarily news. The Falcons coaching staff made that clear in the spring. But back then there was some expectation Penix would be fully ready for training camp. That has not been the case and Penix said it could be another several weeks before he's good to go.

 Tua Tagovailoa (tight back) took another step toward a full return Wednesday with more work in 11s. He went 5-of-7 passing. At this juncture, it's fair to say Tagovailoa will be the team's Week 1 starter unless something major changes.

 More observations: 

 
 Edge rusher Jalon Walker was officially confirmed as out for the season with a torn ACL after getting injured Tuesday at practice. It's a major blow for a pass rush that was depending him on to make a major impact. He had 5.5 sacks as a rookie last season. 
 Running back Bijan Robinson officially put pen to paper on his three-year extension, which is worth up to $75 million. He is still limited in practice and has not done any 11s as the team ramps him up. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Falcons running back Bijan Robinson returned to practice after a five-day hold-in Tuesday. Robinson got a three-year extension worth up to $75 million and is now the highest-paid running back in the NFL.

 Head coach Kevin Stefanski referred to Robinson's hold-in as "very amicable." Robinson had been at every practice on the hip of running backs coach Michael Pitre prior to actually coming back.

 "He wants to be out there practicing," Falcons running back Brian Robinson Jr . said. "You know he wants to be competing. So, I used to just tell him, 'Yo, take your time, handle your business. Whenever your time comes, it's going to come. I know you want to be out there with us, but we going to hold it down until you come back.'"

 Bijan Robinson didn't do much Tuesday. He worked a bit with the running backs in individual drills and did a play-action drill after practice with quarterback Michael Penix Jr . Pitre said they will work to ramp Bijan up over the next few days based on recommendations by the training and medical staff.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa (tight back) said he continues to make progress and expected to be practicing fully Wednesday. Tagovailoa has eased into 11-on-11 sessions the last two days, but has only thrown seven passes. He was 3-of-4 in 11s on Tuesday. 
 Quarterback Cooper Rush , who signed with the Falcons last Wednesday, got reps with the first-team offense in a two-minute drill near the end of practice. Penix has still not yet been cleared for 11s, but got reps again in 7-on-7 work Tuesday. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa participated in 11-on-11 team sessions Monday for the first time this training camp. Tagovailoa has been dealing with a tight back and was still limited. He did two series, going 3-for-3 passing in 11s with individual drills, as well.

 Michael Penix Jr . (right knee) had his best 7-on-7 session Monday, going 6-of-8 with two drops, working mostly with younger players and reserves. His best throw of camp came on the final play of practice. Penix found  Antwane Wells Jr . for a long touchdown pass down the left side.

 Penix has still not been cleared for 11s. The majority of those reps still went to Jack Strand , followed by veteran Cooper Rush . Strand was 7-of-11 passing in those sessions, while Rush was 3-of-7.

 More observations: 

 
 Defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich returned to practice Monday. Ulbrich's wife Cristina died last week after a battle with cancer. "He's a father figure, older brother for me," Falcons linebacker Divine Deablo said. "So, I was glad to have him back out here. I hugged him as soon as I seen him. Everybody just wants to play for 'Brich' at the end of the day." 
 This was the first camp practice with pads. 
 Offensive tackle Wanya Morris and defensive tackle  Da'Shawn Hand  both left practice with apparent injuries. 
 Michael Jerrell , Brandon Walton and rookie seventh-round pick Ethan Onianwa  rotated at right tackle. Free agent signee Jawaan Taylor is not yet cleared to practice after elbow surgery last season. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Cooper Rush has only been with the Falcons for a little more than 72 hours, but he is starting to get himself acclimated fairly well.

 The veteran quarterback got reps with the first-team offense for the first time Saturday morning in 11-on-11 team sessions. Overall, Rush was 6-of-10 with a red zone touchdown to tight end  Kyle Pitts Sr .

 The Falcons signed Rush on Wednesday , just before their first practice of training camp. Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa is dealing with a tight back and has yet to do anything but individual work and a walk-through. Michael Penix Jr . is not yet cleared for 11s after right ACL surgery last November.

 Undrafted rookie Jack Strand has gotten the majority of 11-on-11 reps with the first team and still did Saturday. But Rush is clearly starting to ramp up.

 More observations:  

 
 Tagovailoa only did individual work, while Penix did individuals and then a 7-on-7 goal-line session. Penix was 4-of-8 passing, including a touchdown pass to rookie running back Cash Jones . 
 Christian Harris has gotten the vast majority of reps with the first-team defense at inside linebacker, alongside Divine Deablo . But rookie sixth-rounder Harold Perkins Jr . broke in with first-team reps. Stefanski said a rotation at that spot -- and many others -- will continue during camp. 
 

 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 Undrafted rookie quarterback Jack Strand is drawing raves from his teammates and coaches for how well he has performed after getting thrown into the proverbial fire.

 Strand has taken the majority of reps in 11-on-11 team sessions with Tua Tagovailoa (tight back) and Michael Penix Jr . (right knee) not fully cleared. On Friday, Strand was 7-of-8 passing in 11s and completed his first six passes.

 "Being a rookie, being able to come into a system like this where it's not easy to be able to regurgitate what he's getting told in the headset to the offense," Tagovailoa said. "I think he's done a really good job this offseason studying, understanding the playbook a bit. And you don't see that a lot in rookies, especially rookie quarterbacks."

 The 6-foot-4, 240-pound Strand, who played at Division II Minnesota State-Moorhead, has an impressive arm, as well.

 "Dude can sling the ball," Tagovailoa said.
