title: 2026 Baltimore Ravens training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Ravens training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Baltimore Ravens ' camp is taking place at Under Armour Performance Center in Baltimore, and Ravens reporter Jamison Hensley has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Ravens camp. We will update this file often. Can new coach Jesse Minter get  Lamar Jackson  and the Ravens to the Super Bowl? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Ravens camp 
 
 Zay Flowers, Ravens agree to four-year, $140M extension 
 Derrick Henry, entering 11th year, not thinking about retirement 
 Ravens waive rookie Diego Pavia to make room for Ethan Pocic 
 Ravens' Madubuike (neck) practices for 1st time in 10 months 
 
 
 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane continues to be the talk of Baltimore Ravens training camp after another highlight reel catch.

 During red-zone drills, Lane leapt high in the back of the end zone to grab a Lamar Jackson throw for a touchdown. The way Lane is consistently pulling in passes has drawn lofty comparisons.

 "The guy that I was around that his hands remind me of is [former NFL great] Mike Thomas ," Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle said. "Mike Thomas had these strong hands where he could pull it down in a way. You threw it in the vicinity, and you felt like he was going to go get it. There is a lot of that feeling. He is a very friendly guy to throw to."

 Doyle was in New Orleans with Thomas from 2019 to 2022 as an offensive assistant. Thomas led the NFL in receptions in 2018 and 2019.

 Now, in his first season as the play-caller in Baltimore, Doyle has been impressed with the Thomas-like catch radius of Lane, who has been the headliner through the first seven practices of camp. He made a leaping, 30-yard reception over the middle last week and then wowed fans with a one-handed catch on Tuesday.

 When Doyle left the field Wednesday, Lane approached him to say he wasn't pleased with how he messed up at practice.

 Doyle told him, "Hey, you recognized what you made a mistake on. Now, the next step is let's fix it before that happens."

 Other observations:  

 
 After watching the Ravens not practice well in the rain during the spring, Doyle was pleased with how the players performed during the steady downpour on Wednesday. "We play in the AFC North," Doyle said. "In order to win games late in the year, you are going to play in some weather games." 
 Middle linebacker Roquan Smith is reacting to the ball better than he did a year ago. Smith ended the first team drill by picking off Lamar Jackson and then lateraling the ball on the return. 
 Wide receiver Zay Flowers added 8 pounds this offseason and is up to 186 pounds. What was the reason for the added weight? "Everybody gets mad at me when I'm running sideways," Flowers said. "So [now I can] run through some more tackles." 
 

 
 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane has become the star of Ravens training camp.

 Early in team drills, Lane made an unbelievable one-handed grab along the sideline, which will go down as one of the best receptions in Ravens' camp history. After running a route to the right sideline, Lane had to reach back to catch Lamar Jackson 's 20-yard pass with his extended right hand while falling backward to the ground.

 "That was a great play by Ja'Kobi," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "He's continued to flash and make those type of plays. As [for] anybody, you're always searching for consistency down after down. Again, the more he shows Lamar that he's making those types of plays, the more trust they build, and that's really what training camp and what practice is all about."

 

 Later, in one-on-one drills, Lane showed his playmaking ability again, using a double move to get behind cornerback T.J. Tampa and catching a long touchdown pass from Jackson.

 This has been an outstanding start to camp for Lane, a third-round pick from USC who has become the team's No. 3 wide receiver behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman . On Thursday, Lane first electrified the crowd by elevating over two defenders for a leaping, 30-yard catch over the middle.

 Other observations:  

 
 There was a brief scare when No. 1 cornerback Nate Wiggins leapt high to pick off Jackson and then landed hard on his back after safety Jaylinn Hawkins accidentally collided with him. Wiggins didn't move for a few minutes as trainers looked at him on the field. But Wiggins got back to his feet and continued to practice, saying he got the wind knocked out of him. 
 In one of the more unusual plays of camp, Jackson was intercepted by 310-pound defensive lineman David Olajiga , who had dropped back into coverage. But right tackle Roger Rosengarten made a heads-up play by knocking the ball away from Olajiga and forcing a fumble. 
 Reserve cornerback Amani Oruwariye picked off No. 3 quarterback Skylar Thompson with aggressive play. Oruwariye closed on tight end Ty Pezza and ripped the ball away. 
 
 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 On Monday, Ravens defensive end Calais Campbell practiced for the first time since his personal tragedy this offseason.

 Last month, Campbell's brother was charged with murder after police found their 71-year-old mother dead at home in Atlanta during a welfare check. Campbell's family told police that his brother struggled with mental illness.

 'We're excited to work him in, start to ramp him into getting ready," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "That'll be at a pace that's good for him."

 Campbell was not made available to reporters after practice. Last month, the Campbell family issued a statement asking for privacy while they deal with "overwhelming grief."

 Campbell's participation on Monday was limited to individual drills. The Ravens excused him from practicing for the first week of training camp.

 Campbell, 39, is entering his 19th NFL season after signing a one-year, $5.5 million contract with Baltimore in April.

 "He's a force multiplier of just how he operates and the wisdom that he brings," Minter said. "On top of, he's still a really high caliber player for his position."

 Other observations:  

 
 In the first padded practice of camp, first-round pick Olaivavega Ioane was looking to make a block downfield and he accidentally collided with running back Derrick Henry , which caused both of them to go to the ground. "Welcome to the league, huh," said Ioane, the Ravens' starting right guard. "Now I know to stay out of his way." 
 Offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford said it's going to take all of training camp for the Ravens to make a decision at starting center. Danny Pinter , Ethan Pocic and Jovaughn Gwyn are competing for that spot. "We want to make sure that we're diligent in giving everybody the opportunity that's here," Ledford said, "and just make sure we get the right guy that we want in there with that first group." 
 Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike is sporting a new neck roll at practice. Madubuike, who is looking to come back from neck surgery, has suited up but has not participated in individual or team drills. Asked about the neck roll, Minter said, "Whatever makes the players feel their best and play with the most confidence -- it definitely looks like a little bit of a throwback." 
 In one-on-one drills against cornerbacks, rookie third-round pick Ja'Kobi Lane flashed again, beating Chidobe Awuzie and catching a deep pass on a fly route. Lane is off to a fast start to the second week of training camp after a strong first week. He…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Chicago Bears ' camp is taking place in Lake Forest, Illinois, and Bears reporter Courtney Cronin has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bears camp. We will update this file often. Will the defense step up and lead the Bears back to the NFC North title? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Bears news 
 
 Darnell Wright agrees to record deal 
 New Bears safety Coby Bryant out 8-10 weeks with injury 
 Bears CB Johnson views 2026 as 'definitely a contract year' 
 Ben Johnson: Bears motivated to spurn 'regression' label 
 
 
 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 One day after becoming the highest-paid right tackle in NFL history, Darnell Wright got ribbed by coach Ben Johnson, who congratulated Wright on his four-year, $116 million extension ($93 million guaranteed) in front of the team before practice.

 Johnson joked that Wright "owed" offensive line coach Dan Roushar a loan. Wright agreed with Johnson's assessment and credited his position coach for helping him reach the point of his career where he's played his way into earning life-changing money.

 "[Roushar's] consistent every day in what he does and what he says," Wright said. "He's consistent in what he's telling you. ... Some coaches I've had in the past or some coaches in the league, they're not very good teachers. They see a guy with talent and blah, blah, blah, but they can't really convey what it is and teach you. You still need to be taught. So I think he is such a good teacher and he does it with such good -- he's not yelling at you, he's not screaming at you, he's not demeaning you, he's telling you what's good about the rep and he's telling you what's bad about the rep so you can see both sides.

 "If you have a coach that tells you just what you did was wrong with the rep so maybe the next rep, you just change everything. Now, you have a different result and you have no consistency to stack on top of each other, where as Dan he shows you what you did good with the rep so you can, you know, keep doing the good things and fix the bad things he tells you."

 During training camp in 2025, Roushar told reporters that he didn't see Wright playing with a consistently high motor. Wright said he appreciated the honesty and path Roushar laid for the right tackle to improve. That constructive criticism paid off as Wright earned second-team All Pro honors while playing through an elbow injury.

 Wright was the inaugural first-round draft pick by general manager Ryan Poles in 2023. The Bears traded back one spot, from No. 9 to No. 10, which allowed the Philadelphia Eagles to draft defensive tackle Jalen Carter , while Chicago snagged its franchise right tackle.

 Proving to Poles that he made the right decision is something Wright internalized over the first three seasons of his career. Seeing how the investment made by the GM went far beyond a financial commitment motivates Wright to continue to progress.

 "[Poles] really invested in me [by] helping me get more one-on-one time with the coaches, one-on-one time more with the strength staff, one-on-one time more with [assistant strength and conditioning coach] Mark [Phillipi] in there doing core strength," Wright said. "...Even when I was a young player, it's hard for you to go up to a coach and want to demand their time. I know you're a first-round pick and blah, blah, blah, so they would probably be obliged, but sometimes it's hard for a player to approach a coach and want to take all their time when they've got stuff to do ...but he was invested in me at a really early age, beyond what you'd think a GM would do."

 

 
 The Bears were in shells for a practice that lasted 90 minutes and had just a handful of team periods conducted at walk-through speed. 
 The highlight of the morning came during a 7-on-7 period when  Caleb Williams completed 9 of 10 attempts. Wide receiver Kaden Davis was on the receiving end of the best catch of the day, a one-handed sliding grab in the corner of the end zone from Williams. 
 Linebacker T.J. Edwards (calf) was activated off the non-football injury list before practice and got his mandatory 40 up-downs done as the defense looked on. 
 For a third straight day, Braxton Jones took his reps as the first-team left tackle. 
 Left guard Joe Thuney and defensive tackle Grady Jarrett were given veteran rest days. The Bears will be in pads Thursday for their fourth practice of the week. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 After the offense got off to a fast start during the Bears' first week of training camp, the defense has caught up and set the tone the last two days.

 Tuesday's two-hour practice featured a heavy dose of 11-on-11 periods and live tackling. The emphasis was on 13 personnel (3 TE, 1 WR, 1 RB), which leant itself to the offense establishing the run game early on.

 But the offense looked the sloppiest it has during any of the team's first six practices. There were dropped passes, pre-snap penalties and timing issues between quarterback Caleb Williams and his receivers.

 During the final period, the first-team offense began on its own 47-yard line trailing 28-23 with 54 seconds on the clock. After back-to-back false starts, Williams found himself being chased down by linebacker Devin Bush , who blitzed off the edge.

 Williams had three straight completions to Luther Burden III , Colston Loveland and Kalif Raymond but could not finish the drive in the end zone.

 With 3.2 seconds remaining, Williams launched a ball down the seam, where Burden went up in traffic to complete the play through multiple defenders and was subsequently blown up by Bush.

 "It was a last-minute play," Bush said. "Take a shot at the end zone. Our responsibility is to not let them in the end zone. Offense's responsibility is get the ball in the end zone. So just a competitive play and finished our practice in the two-minute drill."

 Burden was slow to get up but walked off the field on his own flanked by Williams and cornerback Tyrique Stevenson . A practice like this is an anomaly for the offense, but the lack of execution is something players know will be drilled down on in Tuesday afternoon meetings.

 "We're gonna go in there, clean up the film," Burden said. "You know, every day not gonna be a great day. I mean, you can strive for that, but it's camp. It's gonna be ups and downs. So that's the good part about it. We get to come back and watch it. We come back, be better, talk about it. Come back tomorrow, have a better day. That's what it's about."

 
 Braxton Jones was the first-team left tackle for a second straight practice. That's the first time since late last week when the Bears began rotating who would be with the starting O-line that a player got multiple days in a row with the first-teamers. 
 Cam Lewis will focus on playing safety while Coby Bryant (knee) is sidelined. Lewis, who was playing at nickel corner in place of Kyler Gordon , will be replaced by Jaylon Jones , Josh Blackwell and Malik Muhammad in the slot. Jones got the nickel reps with the 1s on Tuesday. 
 Dayo Odeyingbo worked from the interior of the D-line for most of the practice on pass rushing downs. He came away with an interception on a Tyson Bagent pass that was batted at the line of scrimmage.

 Latest news from Browns camp 
 
 Jerry Jeudy clarifies viral video, says he talked to Browns QBs 
 AJ Epenesa grateful to be Eagle after 'weird' Browns situation 
 Deshaun Watson: Preseason is 'great opportunity' after injuries 
 Deion Sanders gives Browns 'insight' on Shedeur Sanders 
 GM Andrew Berry 'hopeful' Browns can reunite with Jadeveon Clowney 
 Sources: Browns, Grant Delpit agree to 3-year, $48M extension 
 
 
 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Quarterback Deshaun Watson had a slow start to training camp but had his best day to date on Wednesday. After two consecutive practices in pads, the Browns practiced in shoulder pads and helmets and ran extensive red zone and goal line 7-on-7 drills. Watson excelled, throwing multiple touchdowns, but he also looked more in sync and confident pushing the ball downfield in other team drills.

 "I think to say who's ahead is a little extreme," Browns coach Todd Monken said before practice. "But we evaluate every day where our roster is, who's where. We try not to knee-jerk react on the one day; that's hard to do. We want every day to go as smooth as it can, and it doesn't, so you have to fight that part of it. We also have to fight; we're in install. We see what you see, and we see a little more in-depth because of the film. But the reality is we're always talking about personnel and the roster; the quarterbacks just happen to be part of that."

 Another observation: 

 
 Sixteen players did not practice Wednesday: tight end Joe Royer (personal), cornerback Myles Bryant and Damarri Mathis , fullback Michael Burton , linebacker Carson Schwesinger , defensive tackles Mike Hall Jr ., Kalia Davis , Mason Graham , Maliek Collins (PUP), Sam Kamara and Elijah Chatman ; centers Parker Brailsford and Elgton Jenkins ; offensive tackle Izavion Miller , guard Teven Jenkins and wide receiver Jamari Thrash . 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Quarterback Shedeur Sanders , leading the No. 1 offense in Cleveland's quarterback competition today, led a two-minute drill that ended in a field goal.

 It marked the second straight day Sanders led a successful two-minute drill to end practice.

 "I've been highly impressed over the last four months that I've been around him with how far he's come as a player, and he's only going to continue to get better," Browns coach Todd Monken said. "There's a lot to take in when you're installing. We got through the spring, then we were gone for six weeks, and then you start back up again in a new system. I think you'll continue to see his operation and mechanics improve, and I think that's the biggest part right now is in and out of the huddle, getting to the line of scrimmage, eliminating that anxiety, his anxiety and my anxiety."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Wide receiver KC Concepcion was at practice after avoiding a serious shoulder injury on Monday but was limited to individual drills. 
 Eleven players did not practice: tight end Joe Royer (personal), cornerbacks Myles Bryant and Damarri Mathis , fullback Michael Burton , linebacker Carson Schwesinger , defensive tackles Mike Hall Jr ., Kalia Davis , Mason Graham and Maliek Collins (PUP); and offensive linemen Kendrick Green and Teven Jenkins . 
 Safety Christopher Edmonds intercepted quarterback Dillon Gabriel in 7-on-7s; it was Edmonds' third pick in training camp, the most of any defender. 
 Browns offensive tackle Izavion Miller left practice with a member of the team's medical staff. Defensive tackle Sam Kamara also left practice on a cart. 
 The Browns claimed defensive tackle Coziah Izzard via waivers from Arizona and waived wide receiver Aaron Anderson , who left practice early with a member of the medical staff, with an injury designation. 
 Before practice, Cleveland signed cornerback Tyler Hall and waived offensive tackle Jack Conley . 
 

 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 On the first practice with pads for the Browns, quarterback Shedeur Sanders ended the day on a high note for Cleveland's offense. Running the No. 2 offense in the ongoing quarterback competition with Deshaun Watson , Sanders connected with wide receiver Gage Larvadain for a deep touchdown on a slot fade to end a two-minute drill in the end zone.

 One play before the touchdown, Sanders found wideout Tylan Wallace on a back-shoulder fade to put the offense in scoring position. Sanders also threw an earlier touchdown in team drills after rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion got behind the secondary for a deep score.

 Concepcion had an injury scare in a previous two-minute drill for the No. 1 offense when he had a hard fall while trying to make a catch and grabbed his right shoulder. Concepcion walked off the field under his own power and remained on the sideline as practice ended shortly thereafter. He is believed to have avoided a serious injury. 
 Linebacker Carson Schwesinger did not participate in practice for a second consecutive day because of what coach Todd Monken called a "minor injury." 
 In addition to Schwesinger, tight end Joe Royer (personal), defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr ., offensive linemen Kendrick Green and Teven Jenkins , wide receiver Jamari Thrash and defensive tackles Kalia Davis and Maliek Collins (PUP) did not practice. 
 Thrash, who also did not practice Saturday, was on the field before practice catching passes from a Jugs machine with a brace around his left leg. 
 Cornerback Myles Bryant left practice early with a member of the team's medical staff. 
 The Browns signed defensive tackle Travis Bell , who most recently played in the UFL, and waived running back T.J. Harden . 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 

 It was an opportunistic afternoon for the Browns' defense, which intercepted five passes on the fourth day of practice.

 Three of those picks were thrown by Deshaun Watson , who now has six interceptions in four practices, with  Christopher Edmonds  getting two and safety Donovan McMillon getting another. Rookie safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren made a strong play on the first interception, dislodging a ball from tight end Jack Stoll that Edmonds caught off the ricochet.

 Shedeur Sanders  was also intercepted for the first time in training camp, as he underthrew a deep pass to wide receiver Jerry Jeudy and was picked off by cornerback D'Angelo Ross .

 Dillon Gabriel was also intercepted by linebacker Reid Carrico in a red zone drill.

 The three quarterbacks, though, had success in the red zone drills, with each throwing multiple short touchdown passes.

 "It's multiple -- they're doing all types of different stuff, showing us different things," Watson said of Cleveland's defense before practice. "It's really good, especially for the quarterbacks, running backs and O-line, just protectionwise. They're showing us different things every time, and each group is getting different looks."

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Dallas Cowboys ' camp is taking place in Oxnard, California, and Cowboys reporter Todd Archer has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at the Cowboys' camp. We will update this file often. Will Dallas turn around the NFL's worst defense from 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Cowboys camp 
 
 Cowboys' Dak Prescott not shying away from setting lofty goals 
 Jones optimistic about Cowboys, likes 'what we put together' 
 Source: Ex-Cowboys QB Will Grier returns as offensive assistant 
 Quieter offseason has Cowboys focused on the right things 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 A year ago at this time, the Cowboys were learning about how  Javonte Williams  fit into their run game. They found out what he did well, as he rushed for 1,201 yards in 2025. Then they rewarded him with a three-year, $24 million contract in the offseason.

 As Williams enters his second season with the Cowboys, offensive coordinator Klayton Adams is looking to expand the list of what Williams does best.

 "Obviously the guy's pretty good on direct runs and he's hard to get down behind the line of scrimmage, but I think that he is a more diverse runner than he probably gets credit for," Adams said. "I think the guy does a really nice job with some of the outside zone stuff, particularly the weak side.

 "He's got really quick feet. He's able to get in and out of cuts really well. And he's one of those dudes that's not scared to run through the smoke, and that's what you're going to have to do on some of the time. I think he's good at a lot of things."

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 
 Sometimes coaches can be inventive when it comes to putting players through drills. On Tuesday, wide receivers coach Junior Adams had CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens catching passes off the Jugs machine during a special teams portion of practice while wearing what looked like a mosquito net or beekeeper's hat.

 The goal is to limit the receiver's vision and force him to concentrate longer on the catch. Lamb dropped one pass but figured it out. The first pass went through Pickens' hands, and he was finished.

 Longtime tight ends coach Mike Pope, who had a stint with the Cowboys, said he had 478 different drills for his tight ends. He would throw ice water at shirtless players while wearing a helmet. He had them wear swim goggles to limit their peripheral vision.

 Let's see if Adams has more tricks in his bag.

 More observations: 

 
 Defensive end  Donovan Ezeiruaku was tossed from practice for fighting. Brian Schottenheimer abhors fighting in practice because if a player throws a punch in a game, he gets ejected. A lesson to be learned for Ezeiruaku. 
 With linebacker  DeMarvion Overshown battling a sore leg (a source said it was nothing to do with his surgically repaired knee), rookie Jaishawn Barham worked with the first-team defense next to Dee Winters . 
 Quarterback  Dak Prescott went 13-of-17 in team drills and would have been better if not for drops by Lamb and tight end  Jake Ferguson . He tried to stretch the field once with a throwback down the field to Pickens, who drew a flag on cornerback  Shavon Revel  at the goal line for pass interference. 
 Ferguson had two excellent catches, however, adjusting on a slightly underthrown seam ball from Prescott and later securing a lower pass with one hand before getting it under control. 
 Cornerback  Cobie Durant came up with the defensive play of the day, knocking away a deep ball from Prescott to wideout  Marquez Valdes-Scantling . Safety Alijah Clark was tangled up on the play and limped off to the medical tent and did not return. 
 

 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 No, there is not going to be a playcaller controversy when it comes to the Cowboys this season, but coach Brian Schottenheimer gave the controls to coordinator Klayton Adams for two periods in Monday's practice, including red zone work.

 The result? Four touchdowns in a six-play span, including one to Ryan Flournoy where the receiver wrestled the ball away from cornerback  DaRon Bland for the score from Dak Prescott .

 "[Bland] actually guarded it great," Flournoy said. "I just had to win on that. I dropped slant before that so I had to make it up. Yeah, definitely great defense by DB. I just had to show strong hands."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Second-year CB Shavon Revel Jr.  had a solid day, breaking up Prescott throws to CeeDee Lamb  and Flournoy, and blanketing George Pickens on a fade in the end zone. He had a pass interference penalty, reaching too early on a throw to Pickens, but it might have been the best practice Revel has had. 
 CB Cobie Durant picked off Prescott, undercutting a throw to Lamb near the goal line in which he dropped off another receiver and came up with the interception. 
 TE Jake Ferguson was back at practice after missing Saturday for personal reasons. He displayed strong hands on a TD catch in the back of the end zone while being covered by S Markquese Bell . 
 NFL officials were on hand for practice, but backup QB Joe Milton III took it into his own hands when an official did not throw a flag on rookie CB Devin Moore on a contested throw to Lamb in the end zone. The pass came on the defensive sideline, so perhaps there was some influence there, but Moore was aggressive on the play in a good way. 
 Prescott was 12-of-21 in team drills Monday after starting 3-of-7 with the Durant pick. 
 TE Princeton Fant left practice early after colliding with RB Israel Abanikanda . 
 

 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 The red zone is an area the Cowboys want to see a lot of offensive improvement in in 2026, and Saturday's practice had plenty of work from inside the 20.

 Dak Prescott had touchdown passes to CeeDee Lamb on the post, two to Ryan Flournoy (dig, slot fade) and a bullet of a throw low to the outside that receiver  George Pickens  corralled for the score.

 There was one interception when a Prescott checkdown was tipped by running back  Jaydon Blue into the arms of safety  Malik Hooker .

 Prescott finished the day unofficially 11-of-18 in team drills.

 Last year, the Cowboys converted a touchdown on 37-of-65 red zone drives. So, what makes a good red zone offense?

 "Finishing in the end zone, executing when you need to, third downs, sometimes on first (down)," Lamb said. "Just being able to not really bat ourselves in the foot, those self-inflicted wounds or penalties that'll really bring us back or kill our momentum. And again, finishing in the end zone."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 It's hard not to notice rookie linebacker  Jaishawn Barham . He is seeing some work with the first-team defense so far. He is active in the run game, filling holes, but he also showed good feel for zone work, knocking down a Prescott pass near the goal line. 
 With Jalen Thompson (hip flexor) and P.J. Locke (knee) not practicing, safeties Alijah Clark and Markquese Bell shared the work with the first-team defense. 
 The catch of the day belonged to undrafted rookie Camden Brown on a fade from Sam Howell . The pass to the back pylon was in a perfect spot and Brown controlled the ball as he was going to the ground. 
 Brandon Aubrey went 5-for-6 on field goal attempts, missing wide right from 44 yards.

title: Can Cowboys achieve GOTI (greatest offense there is) status?
summary: Dak Prescott's teammates are buying into his new saying, but will they push the offense to new heights?
full_text:
OXNARD, Calif. -- After the first practice of Dallas Cowboys training camp, left tackle Tyler Guyton let everybody in on a little secret.

 "Dak has a new saying," Guyton said of quarterback  Dak Prescott , "GOTI: Greatest offense there is. So that's the standard for us."

 In the subsequent days, GOTI became a much-asked question to everybody from Prescott to wide receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens  to tight end Jake Ferguson to running back Javonte Williams .

 Prescott finalized the saying during pre-training camp workouts in Park City, Utah, with all of the skill players, and everybody has bought in.

 

 "We know what kind of offense we can be," Ferguson said. "We know what kind of weapons we have. We know who's at the helm, that's 4 [Prescott]. And when the lights are on -- when we're fully focused, when we're playing our game, we're dialed in -- we are the greatest offense there is, and we believe that. That's just something we're striving to be every single day [in] the meeting room, practice, whatever it may be."

 The Cowboys were one of the league's best offenses last year. They finished the season second in yards per game (391.9) and seventh in points (27.7). In the Super Bowl era, it was the fourth-best Cowboys season in terms of yards and 10th-highest in points.

 They scored 40 or more points three times. They had only one game in which they failed to score more than 14 points, matching the fewest in a season in which Prescott started the majority of the games (2021).

 The Cowboys were one of two teams with a 4,000-yard passer (Prescott, 4,552), two 1,000-yard receivers (Pickens, 1,429; Lamb, 1,077) and a 1,000-yard running back (Williams, 1,201). The Detroit Lions were the other.

 And they return every significant contributor to the offense in 2026.

 

 But making a historical leap to "GOTI" will require a lot more. In the Super Bowl era, the 2023 Denver Broncos , with Peyton Manning , averaged the most points (38.8). The 2011 New Orleans Saints , with Drew Brees , averaged 467.1 yards per game, most in the Super Bowl era.

 "One, we've got to evolve," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "We have to change the things that we didn't like last year that we didn't do very well. We've got to find ways to complement the things that we did well. We need a couple more guys to continue to step up -- not named Pickens and Lamb -- and that's the [ Ryan Flournoys ] of the world, it's some young tight ends, [running back]  Jaydon Blue , things like that. And I've been very open and honest -- I really do believe that this offense is going to be driven by our offensive line. Our ability to move people, our ability to knock people back in a run game, our ability to pass protect. I think that's incredibly critical and we've got a few position battles going there.

 "So I love it. I love the confidence, but we have to go out and do it."

 The Cowboys have to improve in two areas: red zone and penalties.

 Last season, the Cowboys scored touchdowns on 37 of 65 red zone trips. Their 56.9% conversion rate ranked 16th in the NFL. The Philadelphia Eagles were No. 1 at 70.21%.

 The Cowboys did an offseason study on red zone offenses, looking not only at their own but others in the NFL. So far in training camp, there has been more red zone work.

 "We're too good to be kicking the field goals that we were kicking," Schottenheimer said. "And I think that's part of GOTI. I mean, if we're going to truly be that, then we have to score touchdowns in the red zone."

 

 In 2025, the Cowboys committed 57 penalties on offense, 14th most in the league. The penalties accounted for 452 yards, which was eighth most. The San Francisco 49ers had the fewest offensive penalties (37) and yards (260).

 "Going into Year 2 [with Schottenheimer as the playcaller], we know that last year's success doesn't just carry over to this year's success," Prescott said.

 Prescott believes the Cowboys are ahead of where they were a year ago. With Lamb and Pickens, the Cowboys have arguably the NFL's best receiver duo. Flournoy is an up-and-coming No. 3 receiver. One of the best returners, KaVontae Turpin , has big-play ability at receiver. Ferguson had eight touchdowns in 2025. Williams set career highs in rushing yards, carries and touchdowns, leading to him signing a three-year, $24 million deal in the offseason.

 Prescott trusts his offensive line, as Guyton has locked down the left tackle spot for now.

 "It's going to be tough to cover all 53 and a half yards of the field and we're going to make teams do that," Prescott said. "And so whether it's the seams, whether it's the boundaries, whether it's getting in condensed formations and just keeping you off balance, that's the goal of this offense."

 Pickens does not believe there is a ceiling to what the offense can achieve.

 "The limitations and nuances of the limitations, you shouldn't put that on yourself," Pickens said. "You can really do anything you want. I feel like as an offense that's one thing and one mindset that we have, so just trying to be through the roof."

title: 2026 Denver Broncos training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Broncos training camp, including intel on the QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Denver Broncos camp is taking place in Englewood, Colorado, and Broncos reporter Jeff Legwold has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Broncos camp. We will update this file often as we track the Broncos' push toward getting to the Super Bowl after falling one game short last season. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Broncos camp 
 
 Payton to talk to Taysom Hill about interest in Broncos 
 Broncos QB Bo Nix won't be afraid to run on repaired ankle 
 How will Broncos' Sean Payton adjust to not calling plays? 
 Cooper practices Wednesday despite legal troubles 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle left Wednesday's practice and did not return. The Broncos' main offseason addition slowed down during a play in a team period and walked off to the locker room. He did not return to practice. Coach Sean Payton said after the workout that Waddle would be "fine" after the initial exam by the team's medical staff. "But we'll evaluate him ... he had some muscle tightness," he added.

 Payton has said repeatedly "we'll be smart" about returning players to practice after injuries. With the Broncos still nine days away from their preseason opener, Waddle could be held out of some practice time in the remainder of the week. Courtland Sutton was also given his second consecutive off day, so Marvin Mims Jr ., Troy Franklin and Pat Bryant got the bulk of the work with the starters after Waddle left the field. Payton said Sutton would practice Thursday.

 More observations: 

 
 Franklin and Bryant each had explosive plays in team drills Wednesday and Franklin might have had his best day of camp overall. The receiver combination of Sutton, Waddle, Mims, Franklin and Bryant -- if healthy -- looks like it will be the top five, so the Broncos would have to keep six receivers for another wideout to make the 53-player roster at the end of the preseason. 
 The Broncos again showed their cornerback depth, as Kris Abrams-Draine intercepted Bo Nix in an 11-on-11 period. 
 Sam Ehlinger took snaps with the second-team offense during multiple practice periods Wednesday and continues to push Jarrett Stidham for the backup quarterback job. Ehlinger re-signed with the Broncos this offseason after spending 2025 on the practice squad. He turned down multiple chances to sign with a team with an active roster spot a year ago. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Edge rusher Nik Bonitto limped off the practice field Tuesday after he suffered what appeared to be a lower left leg injury in a 9-on-7 run-game drill. Bonitto left the field with a trainer as well as one of the team doctors and did not return. After practice, Broncos coach Sean Payton would say only "he'll be fine, no updates."

 

 Bonitto has led the team in sacks in each of the past two seasons -- 13.5 in 2024 and 14.0 in 2025 - helping the Broncos lead the league and establish single-season franchise records in each campaign. Jonah Elliss and Jonathon Cooper took most of the snaps with the starters at the edge spots after Bonitto left practice, with second-year man Que Robinson getting more work throughout the day as well.

 It was the second consecutive day the Broncos had a starter leave practice. Center Luke Wattenberg , who dealt with a shoulder injury last season, left Monday's practice and did not practice Tuesday.

 More observations: 

 
 Add Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle to the list of those who have noticed Marvin Mims Jr .'s work this training camp. Mims made another leaping grab Tuesday -- this time in one-on-ones -- and Waddle was quick to praise it all after practice. "Man, Marv -- I'm a big fan of Marvin Mims, I'm not going to lie. He's very explosive, I love watching him work, love being in meetings (with him), picking his brain. Marvin's a big play always ready to happen, you've got to respect that kind of speed." 
 Wide receiver Courtland Sutton was held out of practice Tuesday for rest, as Payton had said this week he would begin to give some of the veteran players scheduled days off. Sutton was the first, but Payton said he has a group of players who have been scheduled for days off in the weeks to come. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton lamented with a laugh about how fans "certainly only cheer for one side of the ball" when watching the team's practices. But on Monday, cornerback Riley Moss made the kind of defensive play that gets folks on their feet.

 During team drills, Moss jumped alongside wide receiver Courtland Sutton on a deep throw from Bo Nix up the left sideline and snatched the ball away from Sutton as the two hit the ground. Few players in the league get tested more in practice and in games than Moss given that he plays across from four-time Pro Bowl selection Pat Surtain II -- the league's Defensive Player of the Year in 2023. But Sean Payton said Moss' play Monday is indicative to the kind of camp Moss is having as the corner enters the last year of his rookie deal.

 "Man he competes his tail off, I love that about him," Payton said. " ... He's moving around well right now."

 Moss continues to play at a high-enough level to continue to hold off Jahdae Barron  -- Denver's first-round pick in 2025. Safety Talanoa Hufanga said Monday that Moss is "one of the most athletic corners I've ever been around."

 More observations: 

 
 Considering that he was the 20th pick of the 2025 draft, Barron's progress is often a topic of queries pointed at Payton. The Broncos continue to carve out snaps for the second-year defensive back, even as Moss continues to improve. Barron is currently lining up at outside corner in some sets, as the nickel in others and plays at linebacker in the dime. If the Broncos do not re-sign Moss to the market-value deal he might command next offseason, Barron is poised to be next in line. 
 On a team with few roster spots available and almost no traditional camp battles for starting jobs, Sam Ehlinger continues to push Jarrett Stidham to be the team's No. 2 quarterback. Ehlinger has consistently moved the offense via limited snaps in team drills in and while Stidham continues to get most of the work with the second-team offense behind Nix, Ehlinger's work in the preseason and the practices to come will bear watching. 
 Center Luke Wattenberg walked off the field after being knocked down in one-on-one drills and did not return. After practice Payton said Wattenberg "should be fine," but Wattenberg did miss time last season with a shoulder injury. 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 After the Broncos tinkered with the idea this offseason to move Jonah Elliss from outside linebacker to inside linebacker, the first three days of training camp have reaffirmed the decision to leave Elliss right where he is as part of the team's pass rush.

 No matter the future of Jonathon Cooper , who was arrested twice on domestic violence charges this offseason, Elliss is expected to push for more playing time. He has been consistently impactful in practices. And coach Sean Payton has said he is glad they didn't move Elliss inside.

 "For me, it felt like man, we're taking a position that's harder to find and moving him to a position that we think might be a little bit easier to replace," Payton said. " ... I just think we felt like man, he's really ascending as an edge player."

 Elliss continues to push for more than 318 snaps he played on defense last season.

title: 2026 Green Bay Packers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Packers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Green Bay Packers ' camp is taking place in Green Bay, Wisconsin, and Packers reporter Rob Demovsky has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Packers camp. We will update this file often. Will the revamped WR corps help QB Jordan Love and the offense take another step? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news out of Packers' camp 
 
 Micah Parsons: Playing vs. Cowboys in Week 6 'realistic' 
 Packers RT changes last name to Bako-Bewele to honor heritage 
 Packers star TE Tucker Kraft activated off PUP after ACL recovery 
 Better, worse or the same: Packers defense 
 Packers CEO: Team needs financial bump to stay competitive 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 While much has been made about rookie kicker Trey Smack 's early struggles in training camp (see Monday's camp report), special teams coordinator Cam Achord explained why those practice kicks are only a small part of the evaluation.

 
Some of that has to do with the wind. Smack kicked in one especially windy day on Ray Nitschke Field, and Achord -- who is new to town -- was surprised at the difference in the wind on the practice field compared to inside Lambeau Field.

 
"We go in there and it's like, wow, you don't feel anything," Achord said. "So I don't put as much stock on the practice stuff as I will in the stadium stuff."

 
Lambeau Field has tricky winds of its own, but Achord said he believes gusts of 25 miles per hour outside "really feels like a light breeze almost inside. Whereas at practice you're out there and you're looking at the flags and it's moving. You're like, whoa, it's a tough day to kick."

 
Add into the mix that regular long snapper Matt Orzech has been unavailable because of a calf injury and holder Daniel Whelan is getting used to putting the ball down the way Smack likes it, which coach Matt LaFleur said is different than how previous kicker Brandon McManus wanted it held.

 
Achord was asked to explain the nuances of holding and didn't just explain it, he demonstrated it in the Packers' media auditorium. That demonstration can be seen here:

 

 Achord, defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon and offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich spoke to reporters on Wednesday, when the players were off.

 More observations: 

 
 Achord might be the only Packers coach ever to wear cleats to practice. He said he started wearing them in 2018, when he joined the Patriots' staff because he likes to get hands on with his players: "I got tired of getting thrown on the ground doing gunner releases with Matt Slater," he said. " Justin Bethel broke my nose. ... I'm 165 pounds and they're athletes, and I tell them like, quit pulling me like you're gonna pull a coach. I was like, pull me like you're gonna pull the freaking vise, yank. So they started yanking and broke my nose, fell down. So after that, I started wearing cleats just for better grip." 
 LaFleur has rarely played veteran starters during the preseason but with a new defensive coordinator in Gannon, might LaFleur want his players to get some exhibition game reps? Said Gannon: "I'll probably punt that one to Matt what we're going to do. How do I say this the right way to you guys? I think that our players have earned the right to play our stuff and get really good at it and go play." 
 Gannon on his plans for Micah Parsons when he returns from his ACL rehab: "We were talking the other day, he could see himself in a bunch of different spots in different calls, so that's kinda cool. Then it will be our job to make sure he gets his touches, which he will." 
 Six practices in, and MarShawn Lloyd is still healthy. That's an accomplishment for the third-year pro, who has played in exactly one NFL game and missed all of last season after getting injured on the first day of padded practices last summer. Asked whether his confidence in Lloyd has grown, offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said: "Every day he's out there and doing it, I have a little bit more. ... But I think this preseason's going to be a huge telling point of what we can do with him this year." 
 The Packers have a closed (to the public) practice Thursday and then hold their annual Family Night on Friday at Lambeau Field, where they will practice in front of a full stadium of fans. 
 

 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 If there were any questions about how new defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon plans to come up with a pass rush until Micah Parsons returns from his torn left  ACL, the first six training camp practices have offered a glimpse.

 
It's been blitz, blitz, blitz.

 
"Linebackers, safeties, corners, nickels," cornerback Benjamin St-Juste said. "Pretty much everybody."

 
St-Juste, who has been working mostly with the No. 2 defense, had what would have been a sack if tackling was allowed. He also had one on Monday. So did rookie cornerback Brandon Cisse , who has been working with the No. 1 defense. Another cornerback, Jaylin Simpson , had a QB pressure during Tuesday's practice.

 
"Feel like Micah Parsons a little bit," Simpson said.

 
It's not just the corners. Safety  Evan Williams got into the act with a sack of Jordan Love and a pressure to force an incompletion, while safety  Kitan Oladapo got home and forced a scramble. Linebacker Edgerrin Cooper has also been a regular blitzer.

 
Gannon was not blitz heavy as coach of the Cardinals the past three seasons. They ranked 19th, 17th and 32nd in the NFL in blitz rate. Before that, as the Eagles' defensive coordinator, Gannon's units ranked 22nd and 30th in blitz percentage. But he might have to be now -- at least until Parsons is available.

 
"He's got the personnel here to do it," St-Juste said."

 More observations: 

 
 It was the first day for one-on-one pass block/pass rush drills, and in the featured matchup, new left tackle Jordan Morgan blocked Lukas Van Ness on three straight reps. Van Ness tried a power rush, a speed rush and an inside move, and Morgan turned away all three. Morgan, however, did lose a rep against Barryn Sorrell . 
 Speaking of Sorrell, the second-year edge had perhaps his best day. He not only went 2-0 in the one-on-one drill, but he had a pick-six of Love on a backside screen for Josh Jacobs . Sorrell perfectly timed the play, and plucked Love's pass out of the air. "They ran a play like two plays later, and I was out there and I told Josh, 'Not again. Not again,'" Sorrell said. "Then next thing you know, it happened." 
 No wonder defensive tackle Anthony Campbell is so good at batting down passes (see Sunday's and Monday's camp reports). He won all four of his reps in the one-on-one pass rushing drill Tuesday. 
 Short on tight ends because of injuries, the Packers signed two of them: McCallan Castles and Drew Biber . They have been without Luke Musgrave (neck), Luke Lachey (foot) and RJ Maryland (hamstring) plus Tucker Kraft (ACL recovery) has been limited to individual drills only. The Packers then waived/injured Lachey and Maryland. Without Musgrave and Kraft, Josh Whyle , who had five catches in eight games last season, has worked as the No. 1 tight end. 
 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 Patience may be the operative word when it comes to kicker Trey Smack . The rookie had another uneven day on Monday, the first practice in full pads and the second in which the Packers kicked field goals during live periods.

 After going 3-for-5 in windy conditions on Sunday, Smack had a 5-for-8 day in slightly calmer…

title: Texans' Ryans uses Artemis II space launch to set expectations
summary: Houston's coach used NASA's trip around the moon as inspiration to rally his team.
full_text:
HOUSTON -- Before training camp began, DeMeco Ryans set the tone for his team with a different approach.

 The Houston Texans  coach delivered a speech with a picture of Artemis II towering over him in bold letters. The names from NASA's crew of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover (pilot), Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen sat beneath Ryans as he talked about the launch on April 1 and flight around the moon, marking the first time since Apollo 17 in 1972.

 Ryans, who mentioned how it was a 10-day mission to fly around the moon before returning safely to Earth, used the historical feat as an example of how the crew "went further" than anyone else. But he also highlighted how they laid the groundwork for years to make that moment possible.

 He compared the takeoff to what Houston could do this upcoming season. How this team could reach heights that it never has. Not only reaching the AFC Championship Game for the first time in franchise history, but winning the Super Bowl. 

 

 "The preparation that it took for Artemis II to launch, it took three years for that mission to take place, and that's the beauty of it," Ryans said. 

 Owner Cal McNair has been on record saying Houston wants to play "in the very last game," and All-Pro defensive end  Will Anderson Jr . called the Texans a "Super Bowl team" this offseason.

 "When you guys asked me about expectations, the only thing I know is high expectations," Ryans said. "That's why we do what we do to achieve the ultimate goal."

 But with the Texans' lofty goals comes the mentality of daily submission to the process.

 "The expectation is to take it one day at a time, one play at a time," quarterback C.J. Stroud said. "And then see where we are at the end of camp."

 The roster has the necessary pieces on both sides of the ball to reach the heights the franchise has failed to capture in years prior.

 Houston has a capable quarterback who has played at a Pro Bowl level before. The running game has a lead back in David Montgomery , a more physical offensive line with the addition of first-round pick Keylan Rutledge  (center), offensive tackle Braden Smith and former All-Pro guard Wyatt Teller . And wideout Nico Collins is a multiple time Pro Bowler.

 

 The defense is highly decorated with three All-Pros in cornerback Derek Stingley Jr ., Danielle Hunter  and Anderson. There's also three other Pro Bowlers in linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair , cornerback Kamari Lassiter and safety Calen Bullock . Each level has difference-makers, which helped them allow the fewest yards (277.2 per game) and second-fewest points (17.4) in the NFL last season.

 But the coaches and players have left those achievements in the past, shifting their focus toward a Super Bowl while putting a massive emphasis on the daily process.

 "You just have to realize that it's a marathon," Lassiter said. "It's a long season. Training camp is the beginning, but every day you want to get better. If we have a common goal, and we're all trying to reach that goal, you take each and every day with a sense of gratitude and you attack it like you don't have the next one."

 The push for goals never met is what's fueling this season, but they won't rush through the importance of the process.

 "You want to do things, you want to go places you've never been before, there's a lot of preparation in the background to prepare to launch," Ryans said. "We don't launch tomorrow. You don't just get there just by talking about it. You got to put the work in, and that's the main message."

title: 2026 Houston Texans training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Houston Texans training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Houston Texans ' camp is taking place in Houston at at NRG Park., and Texans reporter D.J. Bien-Aime has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Texans camp 
 
 Tank Dell returns to practice for first time since 2024 
 Houston bringing back former No. 1 pick Clowney 
 Texans have 'productive' contract talks with Stroud 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Wideout Tank Dell made his return to the practice field, participating in limited capacity. It marked the first time he engaged in any sort of team padded practice since Week 16 of 2024 after the 2023 third-round pick suffered multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap against the Chiefs.

 He caught a few passes from quarterback C.J. Stroud during individual drills and ran full speed routes.

 Dell didn't do much more after that, but this is the step in the right direction. Coach DeMeco Ryans won't rush Dell back and said "Tank is on the right plan." The goal is have him ready for team 11-on-11 contact reps. He still has a ways to go, but this is positive progress.

 Other observation:  

 Wideout Jayden Higgins continue to flash throughout practice. He made another impressive catch with Derek Stingley Jr . in coverage. It was a tightly contested catch but that's always a positive because it's against an All-Pro corner.

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 Texans wideout Jayden Higgins is starting to blossom as he's entering Year 2. When Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins  was asked about Higgins' progression he said "He's hooping right now, and I can't wait to see him rock out when it really matters."

 During Tuesday's practice, Higgins made multiple catches with All-Pro cornerback  Derek Stingley Jr . in coverage. One of those receptions occurred during a team third-down period for a 20-yard gain. The other one was during 1-on-1s -- where Stingley tried to aggressively jam Higgins, but he avoided the powerful jab and broke free for an easy toss from quarterback C.J. Stroud .

 Early in camp, Stroud said he expected Higgins to have a "dominant" Year 2, and so far we are starting to see it.

 Other observation:  

 Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was slow to get up after a collision with tight end Dalton Schultz . Al-Shaair was fine shortly after.

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 This was Day 1 of padded practices, and the defense shined. Quarterback C.J. Stroud  was forced to hold the ball longer than he would like as the secondary coverage was stout.

 Stroud occasionally scrambled more than usual to buy time to make throws and the defensive line forced a few sacks. Safety Calen Bullock intercepted Stroud.

 Also coach DeMeco Ryans used exotic blitzes throughout the day, and the offense sometimes had answers and other times didn't. Ryans deemed the first day in full pads as "successful." 

 Other observation: 

 First-round pick Keylan Rutledge is adding an extra juice of aggression to the unit. He got into a mini tussle with defensive end Danielle Hunter after a successful run play by running back Woody Marks .

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Saturday's padless practice featured more back and forth from the offense and defense. Some periods the defense dominated and others, the offense was able to counter their blitzing.

 The Texans start padded practices on Monday and that will be a "big part" of the evaluation process for the team according to coach DeMeco Ryans.

 The fourth-year head coach said: "There's a lot of all-stars in shorts," and later added the staff wouldn't be fooled by what players have done without pads.

 Another observation: 

 
 Cornerback Derek Stingley Jr collided with linebacker Henry To'oTo'o and was slow to get up, but he shook it off and was back on the field. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 It was mainly walk-throughs for the Texans. It's a theme that's been consistent for coach DeMeco Ryans throughout the offseason -- where he has focused on helping his team mentally work toward executing deep in the playoffs.

 "I've grown as a head coach," Ryans said in June. "For me, it's more so now about how much smarter can we play as a team. How can we be more elite on our execution? Our communication, can it be louder? Can we echo it more? Can we truly be tied together every time we line up? That's what I've seen when I talk about the process of us this year being better."

 Saturday's practice will be the first day with fans in attendance since training camp has opened. That will be a longer practice with more intensity compared to today's practice that was roughly a little over an hour.

 

 

 Thursday, July 30 
 The passing attack was centered around the quick game time to throw on Day 2 of practice. Quarterback C.J. Stroud was quick and decisive with his throws with all but one of his throws being made under 2.8 seconds, and his only rep over three seconds was when he extended the play and tried to find wideout Jayden Higgins in the back of the end zone.

 It fell incomplete, but the majority of his throws came with precision and decisiveness. Stroud was able to connect a few times with Higgins, who's development in Year 2 will be huge for the offense.

 Other observation:  

 
 Backup cornerback Alijah Huzzie was able to make a nice interception off of backup QB  Davis Mills  -- where took the ball away from the intended receiver. 
 
 
 Wednesday, July 29 
 The Texans were more forthcoming regarding contract discussions than normal. General manager Nick Caserio said there's a "possibility" the team and quarterback C.J. Stroud can reach a contract extension. Stroud isn't focused much on contract discussions; he's letting his agent handle it as he is "keeping the main thing the main thing."

 Stroud is going into Year 4 and is eligible for an extension for the first time in his career. Coach DeMeco Ryans said he doesn't get into a lot of deep discussions with guys when it comes to contract situations.

 But he added, "I truly believe you get the contract by what you do on the field. It doesn't matter what you say, what I say. It's about how you perform on the field, and if you're worthy of getting a contract and you deserve it, it'll happen for you."

 Other observation: 

 
 CB Kamari Lassiter intercepted Stroud with a diving catch and then punted the ball in celebration. That was the most exciting play on a relatively quiet morning.

 Chiefs' Mahomes fully cleared for camp, feeling 'amazing' 
 As training camp opens, Chiefs point to brighter future in 2026 
 
 
 Wednesday, Aug. 5 
 Rashee Rice , the Chiefs' No. 1 receiver, participated in 11-on-11 repetitions, a positive sign that his acclimation process is going well. In May, Rice underwent surgery on his right knee to remove loose debris that was causing inflammation. Since camp began, the Chiefs have been cautious with Rice's participation.

 Most of Rice's work was during the red zone period, where he had several short receptions, including a bubble screen on the perimeter and a touchdown in the back of the end zone. When Mahomes targeted Rice in the back corner of the end zone, Rice couldn't make a leaping, contested catch against cornerback Nohl Williams .

 It's clear Rice will need time to get into true football shape, as he showed fatigue before the long-drive drill, the final 11-on-11 repetitions. During that period, Rice was held out of the first-team offense's 12 repetitions.

 "He got a lot of good reps today, which is important," Reid said of Rice. "We've just got to ease him back in and just keep working. We know he's a good player. He actually got better as the practice went on, so that was a good thing."

 Other observations:  

 
 Linebacker Drue Tranquill missed his first practice of camp with lower back spasms. During the second half of Wednesday's work, Tranquill did some light strength work off the side with the training staff. 
 The other players who missed Wednesday's on-field session were cornerback Kristian Fulton (hip), linebacker Jeffrey Bassa (strained groin), defensive end Ashton Gillotte (strained right hamstring), defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee) and receivers Cyrus Allen (left shin) and Xavier Worthy (sprained right shoulder). 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 For the second consecutive day in pads, Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie right tackle from Indiana, performed well, even better than Monday, after once again receiving all of the repetitions with the first-team offense.

 In the first 11-on-11 period, Benson showed strong run-blocking skills by executing a double-team to move defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga back. The repetition finished with Benson also blocking linebacker Nick Bolton , which created more space on the right side of the field for running back Kenneth Walker III . A few minutes later, Benson blocked defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah in pass protection for quarterback Patrick Mahomes to connect with receiver Tyquan Thornton for a completion for more than 30 yards.

 "He's done great," Walker said of Benson. "We've got pads on now and you get to see how well he's doing out there. He's going to have a great impact on this team."

 Benson's work, on the field and in meetings, has pushed him to have true competition with Jaylon Moore , the five-year veteran, for the starting right tackle role.

 In the final 11-on-11 period, Benson didn't lose any of the five repetitions with the first-team offense. His matchups included Anudike-Uzomah, pass rusher Chris Jones and rookie defensive end R Mason Thomas .

 "We'll give you a chance here to learn, but if you start making [mistakes] consistently, then we've got a problem," Reid said Monday of Benson. "But he's been doing a good job. There's a hiccup here or there, but he fixes them normally."

 More observations:

 Receiver Rashee Rice (right knee) participated in 7-on-7 repetitions for the second straight day, this time catching a short pass from Mahomes against zone coverage. For the first time in camp, cornerback  L'Jarius Sneed , a six-year veteran, participated in 1-on-1 drills and 7-on-7 repetitions. 
 Joe Bleymaier said he has talked with offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy the past few days. For more than a week, Bleymaier, the pass game coordinator, has taken over Bieniemy's duties as offensive coordinator during his absence. He left the Chiefs after his wife, Mia Bieniemy, 57, was hospitalized in stable condition last week after being allegedly shot by the couple's son, Elijah Zion Bieniemy, 27, at the family's home in Virginia. "We miss EB, obviously," Bleymaier said. "It was great to hear from him, just on a personal standpoint. You're so devastated for him. He's been reaching out more and more lately with some of the football stuff, so that's kind of brought a little sense of normalcy back. As far as the [acting] offensive coordinator, calling in the plays and just making sure some of the administration stuff is handled has been the biggest thing." 
 One of Mahomes' best repetitions was during the first 11-on-11 period, when he, under center Creed Humphrey , rolled to the right on a play-action pass, completing an intermediate throw to Thornton while on the move. "We're not going to put any limitations on what Patrick can do rather than maybe emphasizing what we're going to try to do more," Bleymaier said of Mahomes, who had surgery in December to repair the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee. "We're really trying to eliminate holding him back -- or 'Let's not put him in this situation.' Everything is open. -- under center, rolling left or right, the whole playbook." 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 Among young players, the biggest winner from the Chiefs' first padded practice was rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods , the second of the Chiefs' first-round picks.

 In the 1-on-1 period, Woods had highlight repetitions, winning quickly in both of his matchups against backup guard Hunter Nourzad , a three-year player. When Woods went against right guard Trey Smith , a two-time Pro Bowler and a five-year veteran, the teammates split their two repetitions. The rookie used his quickness to push Smith back by gaining leverage using his right hand.

 "Peter is really talented, man, in terms of his hand utilization, speed, power," Smith said after practice. "He's really sort of the full package type of guy. He's young and he's figuring out the game, but he has a willingness to learn.

 "I've really enjoyed the way he's stepped into this program. He definitely has an outstanding future. I'm just really excited to help him in his development where I can."

 Selected with the 29th pick, which the Chiefs gained from the Los Angeles Chargers through the trade involving cornerback Trent McDuffie , Woods has been impressive in creating havoc at times for running backs by bursting through the offensive line just a second after the snap. The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Los Angeles Chargers camp is taking place at The Bolt in El Segundo, California, and Chargers reporter Kris Rhim has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Chargers camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 Latest from Chargers camp 
 
 Players with the most at stake during Chargers' training camp 
 Tracking 2026 NFL hold-ins: Tuipulotu 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 5 

 Outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu , who has been a limited participant in practice this training camp amid ongoing contract negotiations, was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. The caveat is that the practice was a walkthrough, so Tuipulotu and the other Chargers players were going at half speed. He still has yet to participate in a non-walkthrough practice 11-on-11 period, but his participation on Wednesday could be a sign that things could be headed toward a resolution.

 Other observations:  

 
 After an injury scare Tuesday scare to the same left leg in which he sustained a season-ending patellar tendon rupture last year, left tackle Rashawn Slater was a full participant in practice Wednesday without any limitations. 
 Branson Taylor and Trevor Penning rotated at left guard, continuing the five man race for this starting job. Rookie Jake Slaughter continues to play center with the second group. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 4 

 The Chargers had their first major injury scare Tuesday as left tackle Rashawn Slater appeared to sustain an injury to his left leg at practice. Slater went to the medical tent with a trainer and then did some on-field testing but didn't return to practice. Branson Taylor and Trey Pipkins III rotated at tackle in his absence.

 Slater ruptured the patella tendon in his left knee during last year's training camp, which forced him to miss the entire season. He appeared in good spirits after practice, walking around and taking pictures with his family.

 Quarterback Justin Herbert said that Slater told him he was healthy enough to return to the field.

 "He said he wanted to be out there, so I think that's okay," Herbert said.

 

 Other observations: 

 
 OLB Tuli Tuipulotu participated in one 7-on-7 rep but did not take part in the remainder of team drills, marking his sixth straight practice with limited participation as his contract situation remains unresolved. 
 Coach Jim Harbaugh said that Kayode Awosika is leading the competition to start at left guard, but added that Pipkins, Jake Slaughter and Taylor are all in the mix. Harbaugh said that he'd like to name a starter after the next ten practices. 
 The offense came out sharp, with Herbert completing his first eight passes before safety RJ Mickens broke up a pass. From there, the offense and defense traded wins throughout the rest of practice. 
 S Kendall Williamson intercepted Herbert on a pass that was intended for wide receiver Ladd McConkey . "That was nice. He snagged it," Derwin James Jr . said. 
 OLB  Nadame Tucker  had one of his best practices of camp, consistently generating pressure and recording three would-be sacks. 
 DT Teair Tart was disruptive throughout, including what likely would have been at least one sack. The Chargers' interior defensive line generated pressure throughout the day. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Monday's practice was one of the better days for the defense, as they were constantly disruptive throughout. Undrafted cornerbacks Rodney Shelley and Avery Smith were among the stars. Smith continued his strong start to camp with another good day, as he intercepted quarterback DJ Uiagalele i and had an impressive pass breakup on a Justin Herbert pass. Shelley was sticky in coverage throughout and had a few pass breakups, celebrating after each.

 The rookies will have their first NFL training camp practice in pads on Tuesday at the University of San Diego, a chance to affirm the way they've been playing.

 

 Other observations:

 
 Edge rusher  Tuli Tuipulotu continued to not participate in team drills, continuing his limited participation as his contract situation remains unresolved. 
 Rookie Jake Slaughter and Kayode Awosika split reps at left guard as the competition for that spot continues. 
 Second-year wide receiver  KeAndre Lambert-Smith , who has been quiet so far, made one of the top highlights of the day with impressive downfield catch while cornerback Deane Leonard was draped in coverage. 
 Quentin Johnston also produced another offensive highlight, tracking a perfectly placed deep ball from Herbert over the outstretched arms of safety Derwin James Jr. along one sideline. 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Coach Jim Harbaugh declined to say whether outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu 's absence from team drills at practice is contract-related, saying only the situation is being "handled internally" and repeatedly describing Tuipulotu as "ramping up."

 Tuipulotu hasn't taken part in team drills amid contract negotiations since camp began this week, as he is heading into the final year of his rookie contract. He finished sixth in the NFL in sacks last season.

 Without Tuipulotu again Saturday, rookie Akheem Mesidor flashed, looking explosive coming off of the edge throughout practice.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Saturday marked perhaps the highest-energy practice as the Chargers offense had its best day this week. Wide receivers Ladd McConkey and Derius Davis caught deep passes that energized the crowd at the Chargers facility. 
 Cornerback Donte Jackson was active in coverage with a couple of pass breakups, causing fans to cheer in reaction. 
 
 

 Friday, July 31 

 Friday's practice was at half-speed, walkthrough pace, but the most significant development came at left guard.  Trey Pipkins III  began with the first group blocking for quarterback Justin Herbert , the first time he's done so this week. Throughout camp and the offseason program,  Kayode Awosika , Trevor Penning  and rookie Jake Slaughter have rotated at left guard, with Awosika getting most of the reps with Herbert.

 Coach Jim Harbaugh said earlier this offseason that the race for a starter at left guard would be between these four players. This is the first time that Pipkins has gotten reps with the top group.

 Still, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel cautioned against looking too much into the rep distribution, noting that the real evaluation will come with padded practices next week.

 "It's much different when you have 300 pounds of mass on your edge," McDaniel said, "and a subtle 6-inch step determines whether or not you can actually execute that block."

 Other observations:  

 
 Tuli Tuipulotu continued not to practice amid ongoing contract negotiations. He went through individual drills, worked off to the side with a trainer and watched practice. 
 Wide receivers Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey said that McDaniel has changed the way they run routes, particularly by emphasizing how quickly they finish the top of a route and locate the football. "We weren't all the way used to running routes like that," Johnston said. 
 

 
 

 Thursday, July 30 
 Tuli Tuipulotu didn't practice for the second straight day amid ongoing contract negotiations, but he did more on the field work with teammates than on the opening day of camp. On Thursday, Tuipulotu wore a helmet and jersey and went through individual drills with the team before working off to the side with a trainer. On Wednesday, he was in a…
